final_records.name: Claude Code
final_records.deployment: local CLI/IDE/Desktop client with cloud inference; Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions; customer-run cloud-session runners (public beta, Team/Enterprise) keep execution on own hosts but not inference or transcripts
final_records.model_backend: Claude models only (Anthropic). Routes: Anthropic API or Claude subscription, Claude Platform on AWS (Anthropic-operated), Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) or Microsoft Foundry (the deployment's hosting option decides Azure or Anthropic infrastructure); LLM gateways may front these, but Anthropic does not support routing to non-Claude models. Covered Models (Claude Fable 5, Fable 5.1) keep prompts and outputs at least 30 days by default; ZDR applies to them only where Anthropic expressly authorizes it.
final_records.data_handling_note: Consumer plans (Pro and Max; Free excludes Claude Code): model training is opt-out. Retention is 5 years with model improvement on and 30 days when it is off. Commercial use (Team, Enterprise, API and cloud providers) is not used for training by default unless the customer opts in, for example through the Development Partner Program. Team, Enterprise and API data has 30-day standard retention; cloud-provider routes follow that platform's policy. ZDR covers Claude Code inference only for Anthropic-approved organizations (Claude Enterprise or a commercial API-key organization), enabled per organization. Legal and misuse exceptions apply: flagged sessions may be kept up to 2 years, and safety-classifier results are retained. Covered Models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) keep prompts and outputs at least 30 days by default and are unavailable under ZDR unless Anthropic authorizes them. Under ZDR, cloud sessions, Claude Tag, Artifacts, feedback and Remote Control are disabled; Cowork, analytics, admin data and third-party integrations/MCP fall outside ZDR. Telemetry: usage metrics (no code, prompts or file paths) are on by default with the Anthropic API (DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 turns them off); /feedback transcripts are kept 5 years; error reports are on by default for Pro/Max sign-ins from v2.1.198 (redacted); session-quality surveys run on every provider, and answering 'Yes' to the follow-up uploads transcripts and source code, kept up to 6 months; the WebFetch hostname check reaches Anthropic on every provider. Local plaintext transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/ expire after 30 days by default. ~/.claude/history.jsonl keeps every typed prompt until deleted (swept only under the HIPAA configuration). Sessions started or last continued in Desktop or Cowork are kept at any age unless desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays, a managed cleanupPeriodDays or the HIPAA configuration applies. With the Enterprise Compliance API on, Anthropic captures Claude Code session content, readable for 30 days.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a commercial route (Team, Enterprise, API or a contracted cloud provider) under a DPA; Anthropic documents a processor role only for commercial plans, so consumer Pro/Max accounts are not a route for other people's personal data (if used for own data, turn the training setting off; 30-day retention still applies). Confirm the exact surface and model are covered: ZDR disables cloud sessions and excludes Covered Models unless authorized. The HIPAA configuration covers only local CLI and Desktop Code-tab sessions, not the VS Code/JetBrains extensions, gateways, cloud providers, connectors/MCP, plugins or skills. Enforce organization login, allowed providers and transcript retention through managed settings, and protect local plaintext transcripts and history.jsonl. Data sent to MCP servers or other integrations is not covered by ZDR or the BAA; check each service's handling.
suitability_notes.special: Every documented inference route is cloud: the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Agent Platform and Foundry. Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude (for example local) models. ZDR, the HIPAA configuration/BAA and self-hosted runners do not keep inference or the session conversation on institution-controlled infrastructure. Under this index's strict rule, do not use it for identifiable or controlled-access health, genetic or clinical data.

compliance: Anthropic lists ISO 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and SOC 2 Type I and Type II (reports via the Trust Portal); the scope of each report for Claude Code requires confirmation.

A BAA is available to HIPAA-ready Enterprise organizations. It extends to Claude Code in the terminal and the Desktop Code tab either with the HIPAA configuration (Anthropic must turn it on through the account team and the Primary Owner applies it; Enterprise sign-in connecting directly to the Claude API; Claude Code v2.1.285 or later; server-side data then follows Anthropic's standard retention) or with ZDR for Claude Code. Console API-key use is covered only when that Console organization has ZDR. Under the HIPAA configuration, the VS Code/JetBrains extensions, cloud-provider, gateway or custom-base-URL sessions, connectors, MCP servers, plugins, skills, Claude in Chrome, beta or research-preview features, cloud sessions, Remote Control and mobile are not covered.
final_records.pricing: Claude Code is included in all paid Claude plans (not Free) and shares the plan's usage limits; API/Console and cloud-provider use is metered separately. Listed 2026-10-10 (USD, excluding tax): Pro $20/month, or $17/month billed annually; Max from $100/month; Team standard seat $25/month, or $20 billed annually; Team premium seat $125/month, or $100 billed annually; Enterprise $20/seat/month billed annually, plus usage at API rates.
final_records.academic: Claude Team plan for scientists (promotional terms effective 2026-08-27, Supplemental Terms under the Commercial Terms): PIs or equivalent at accredited universities and nonprofit research institutes in the natural sciences, mathematics, computer science, engineering and related fields can apply; for-profits, CROs and industry R&D are excluded. For 12 months, Standard seats are $0 and Premium seats $15/month ($0/$180 per seat per year annually); 1-25 seats; initial group of 10,000 verified scientists; limited availability, final pricing confirmed after verification. A payment method is required, seats renew at the then-current price after 12 months, and 90 days without use can end the promotional pricing. Includes Claude Code. Institution-wide Claude for Education plans are available through Anthropic's Education team; confirm Claude Code inclusion.

final_records.name: OpenAI Codex
final_records.deployment: Local clients (Codex CLI, IDE extension, Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app) with OpenAI-hosted inference by default; Codex cloud tasks run remotely in OpenAI-managed cloud environments and require ChatGPT sign-in. Documented alternative model routes: custom providers or gateways (Responses API), a built-in Amazon Bedrock provider, and CLI --oss mode with local Ollama or LM Studio.
final_records.model_backend: OpenAI-hosted models by default: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, with the GPT-5.6 family still available during the rollout; GPT-5.5 retires from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 14 October 2026 (API unaffected). API-key use follows the key's API model access. Custom providers and gateways need a Responses-compatible endpoint; Amazon Bedrock and local open-weight models via Ollama or LM Studio are documented alternatives.
final_records.data_handling_note: Business, Enterprise, Edu and API data are not used for training by default (API sharing is opt-in). Free, Plus and Pro personal workspaces share data for training by default, with an opt-out under Data Controls. With ChatGPT sign-in, Codex follows the workspace's retention and residency settings; with an API key, the API organization's retention settings apply. API abuse-monitoring logs are kept for up to 30 days; ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring needs OpenAI approval, and OpenAI can make specific models ineligible after written notice. API ZDR does not define ChatGPT Work retention, and no Codex-cloud-specific deletion schedule was found; for Work cloud tasks, execution state follows a lifecycle separate from chats. Local clients send anonymous usage and health metrics to OpenAI by default (opt-out via [analytics]); OTel export is off by default. With the Amazon Bedrock provider, requests go to Amazon Bedrock with AWS authentication and OpenAI's hosted Responses API is not in the request path; AWS-side retention was not assessed.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace or a contracted API organization with a DPA, not a Free, Go, Plus or Pro personal plan. Confirm chat, file and cloud-task retention for the exact surface and any approved API ZDR scope, and disable analytics on managed machines.
suitability_notes.special: Only the open-source Codex CLI in --oss mode (or a custom no-auth provider) against Ollama in local-only mode (no :cloud models) or LM Studio on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware, with no ChatGPT or API sign-in, analytics, feedback and web search disabled, and egress verified. OpenAI-hosted, Codex cloud, ChatGPT Work and Amazon Bedrock routes are not appropriate.

compliance: OpenAI states its business data practices align with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 and CSA STAR, and offers a DPA; confirm that the Codex surface and plan are in scope.
A BAA is offered to ChatGPT for Healthcare and API healthcare customers; OpenAI's Work admin FAQ says HIPAA/BAA coverage depends on the features and agreement in use.
Data residency is available for eligible Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare and API customers; Codex with ChatGPT sign-in follows workspace residency settings.
final_records.pricing: Codex is included in ChatGPT plans (US list prices): Free and Go ($8/month) get GPT-6 Luna in the desktop app, subject to rollout; Plus $20/month; Pro $100, $200 or $500/month. ChatGPT Business: Standard seat $20/user/month billed annually or $25 monthly; Premium seat (5x Standard usage, no 5-hour limit) $100 annually or $125 monthly; for teams of 2-200. Enterprise and Edu through sales. New Codex-only pay-as-you-go Business seats have not been offered since 24 June 2026 (existing seats unaffected). Purchased credits extend plan limits; API-key use is billed at API rates.
final_records.academic: ChatGPT Edu is sold through OpenAI sales. Verified university students in the US and Canada can claim $100 (2,500 ChatGPT credits) for Codex, valid 12 months; the offer is limited to those two countries. Maintainers of widely used open-source projects can apply to Codex for Open Source (API credits, ChatGPT Pro with Codex).

final_records.notes: Multi-surface coding agent: Codex CLI, IDE extension, Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex cloud, plus code review, Codex Security and a GitHub Action. Current models include GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol (recommended for complex coding, launched 29 September 2026), GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna; GPT-5.5 leaves Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 14 October 2026. Codex and ChatGPT Work share usage limits. Licence scope: Apache-2.0 covers openai/codex (Codex CLI, SDK and app server); OpenAI lists the IDE extension and Codex cloud as not open source, and the ChatGPT desktop app is not among the listed open-source components. The special-category route covers only the local --oss CLI configuration; OpenAI-hosted routes remain unsuitable for such data. Basis for that route: OpenAI's --oss and no-authentication local-provider documentation, plus a source review of codex-rs on 10 October 2026 showing that login is skipped for non-OpenAI providers and that the model-catalog refresh runs only with the Codex backend, command auth or API-key discovery. Network egress of an --oss session was not tested.
final_records.tier_gate: Personal data: Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace or contracted API org (not consumer plans); special-category data: local --oss CLI only, no OpenAI sign-in

required_controls: Run only the Apache-2.0 Codex CLI (including codex exec) with --oss, or a custom provider pointing to Ollama or LM Studio on hardware the researcher or institution controls; do not sign in with ChatGPT or an OpenAI API key, and remove stored OpenAI credentials (codex logout).
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Set [analytics] enabled = false and [feedback] enabled = false; keep OTel export off or send it only to an institution-controlled collector with log_user_prompt = false.
Set web_search = "disabled" and do not use Codex cloud, ChatGPT Work, the desktop app, remote connections, plugins, connectors or remote MCP servers.

Verify network egress on the deployed version (firewall allowlist), turn off startup update checks where updates are centrally managed, and apply institutional retention to local history under CODEX_HOME (or set history.persistence = "none").
residual_risks: OpenAI-hosted inference (ChatGPT sign-in or API key), Codex cloud and the Amazon Bedrock provider send data outside institution-controlled infrastructure; ZDR, data residency or a BAA do not change this.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so an --oss session pointed at local Ollama can still send prompts to Ollama's cloud unless local-only mode is enabled.
Analytics and feedback are on by default, and OpenAI's docs do not state that an --oss session makes no other network calls; egress has to be tested.
Codex needs a Responses-compatible endpoint (Chat Completions-only servers are unsupported), and local open-weight models are less capable than the hosted models.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Gemini CLI
final_records.deployment: local CLI / cloud inference
final_records.model_backend: Google Gemini models via the paid Gemini API, Vertex AI (Google Cloud docs now titled Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform), or Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences; free-of-charge and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended 2026-06-18 and moved to the separate Antigravity CLI product
final_records.data_handling_note: The CLI is an Apache-2.0 client; data handling follows the backend route. The supported routes (paid Gemini API, Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise) do not use prompts or code for training by default. Retention differs by route. On the paid Gemini API, prompts and responses are logged for a limited period for abuse monitoring, and Google points users who need guaranteed ZDR to Vertex. Agent Platform allows ZDR if you request an abuse-monitoring exception; it also keeps a 24-hour in-memory cache, which can be disabled per project. Google describes Code Assist Standard/Enterprise as stateless services that do not store prompts and responses in Google Cloud. The CLI's built-in google_web_search tool uses Grounding with Google Search, whose logs cannot be disabled: 30 days on the Gemini API, up to 3 days on Agent Platform. Unpaid use is no longer a supported Gemini CLI route. If an API key without an active billing account still works, the unpaid terms let Google use content to improve products, except in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, where the paid-service data-use terms also cover unpaid quota. Anonymous usage statistics are on by default and do not include prompt content, per the docs; turn them off with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false. Free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended on 2026-06-18.

suitability_notes.personal: Use only a paid route covered by a Google data processing addendum: a Gemini API key in a billed Cloud project (Gemini API Paid Services terms), Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, or a Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licence (Google Cloud terms). For regional processing, use Agent Platform with GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION set to a regional location (not global) where the chosen model is offered; global endpoints give no data-residency guarantee. For ZDR on Agent Platform, request the abuse-monitoring exception. Code Assist processing is not guaranteed to stay in-region, and the paid Gemini API may cache data in any country. Restrict the built-in tools (tools.core) so that google_web_search stays off, because grounding logs cannot be disabled. Turn off usage statistics, and enforce the authentication type in system settings (security.auth.enforcedType). If you enable OpenTelemetry, set telemetry.logPrompts to false, because it defaults to true. On the Gemini API route, share no AI Studio log datasets with Google, because shared datasets are processed under the unpaid terms. Confirm with your DPO.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.

compliance: Google Cloud or Code Assist contract and service scope must be verified; infrastructure certifications are not a blanket Gemini CLI certification
Google's Code Assist security page lists ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 and SOC 1, 2 and 3 for Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise; these cover the service, not the open-source CLI client
final_records.pricing: The open-source CLI is free. Model use is billed per token through a Gemini API key or Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, or through per-seat Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise subscriptions. The geminicli.com quota and plans pages still list free, Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra quotas, but per Google's banner and blog those routes were retired on 2026-06-18 and moved to the separate Antigravity CLI product.
final_records.academic: No dedicated academic or student discount for Gemini CLI was found on the current plans or quota pages. Since 2026-06-18 Gemini CLI itself has no free consumer route. Free consumer access is available only through the separate Antigravity CLI product.

final_records.name: Aider
final_records.vendor: Aider AI LLC (GitHub: Aider-AI); open source, Apache-2.0
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: BYO key - local models (Ollama, LM Studio or other OpenAI-compatible servers) or most cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenRouter, etc.)
final_records.data_handling_note: With a local model (e.g. Ollama in local-only mode, or LM Studio on localhost) inference stays on controlled infrastructure; with a cloud API, prompts and code go to that provider under its terms. Aider states that analytics are opt-in and never collect code, chat messages or keys; a random subset of users is asked to opt in, the prompt defaults to Yes and, per source code, is auto-accepted under --yes-always; events go to PostHog (US host by default), and --analytics-disable turns analytics off permanently. By default Aider also checks PyPI for a new version on launch (at most once a day) and downloads LiteLLM's model-metadata file from GitHub (no code or chat content). Chat and input histories are written to .aider.chat.history.md and .aider.input.history in the project root by default; these files, repository contents and executed commands need access, retention and network controls.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model, or a cloud provider covered by an appropriate DPA and no-training terms; Aider itself is not the processor for cloud inference. Keep analytics permanently disabled (--analytics-disable).
suitability_notes.special: Requires a fully local model on controlled infrastructure (Ollama in local-only mode if used), analytics permanently disabled, the launch-time update check off and outbound traffic blocked except to the model endpoint. Any cloud-model configuration moves data outside that boundary and is not acceptable under this index's strict rule.

final_records.notes: Local-capable pair-programming CLI. The latest PyPI release is 0.86.2 (12 Feb 2026); the GitHub Releases page still lists v0.86.0 (Aug 2025) as latest. The last main-branch commit is dated 22 May 2026 and the last maintainer comment 23 May 2026; through 10 Oct 2026 nothing further was merged while new issues kept arriving. The project is not declared discontinued; treat maintenance as stalled and check compatibility with the chosen model before adopting.

required_controls: Point Aider only at a model endpoint on the workstation or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network (e.g. Ollama via OLLAMA_API_BASE), and name every model role explicitly: --model, plus --weak-model and --editor-model, whose defaults depend on --model. Keep cloud API keys out of the environment, .env and Aider config files (without --model, Aider auto-selects a cloud model when a cloud key is present, or offers OpenRouter sign-in when none is).
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Disable analytics permanently with aider --analytics-disable (or AIDER_ANALYTICS_DISABLE=true) before any run with --yes-always.

Turn off the launch-time update check (--no-check-update) and block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint, then verify the block; Aider downloads model metadata from GitHub by default.
Turn off URL detection (--no-detect-urls), do not use /web or /voice, and do not add web pages to the chat in sensitive sessions.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions: Aider also loads .aider.conf.yml (git root, current directory or home directory) and .env (git root), so confirm that no such file sets a cloud model or API keys or undoes the controls above.

Restrict access to and set retention for local history files (.aider.chat.history.md, .aider.input.history, any --llm-history-file) and for the git commits Aider creates automatically; in sensitive repositories turn auto-commits off (--no-auto-commits) or review every Aider commit before it is pushed.
residual_risks: Any cloud-model configuration moves prompts and code outside the controlled boundary.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost OLLAMA_API_BASE alone does not guarantee local inference.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

Maintenance has stalled: no main-branch commits after 22 May 2026 and no maintainer comments after 23 May 2026 (checked 10 Oct 2026); two published GitHub advisories against aider-chat <= 0.86.2 (prompt injection in architect mode; scraper SSRF) list no patched version.
Aider's documentation warns that it may not work well with less capable models, which limits the choice of small local models.

final_records.name: Goose
final_records.vendor: AAIF / Linux Foundation (originally Block; donated to Agentic AI Foundation in Dec 2025)
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: User-configured (Desktop model switcher, goose configure, GOOSE_PROVIDER or recipe). Local: built-in llama.cpp inference, or local servers such as Ollama, LM Studio and Docker Model Runner; OpenAI-compatible self-hosted endpoints (e.g. vLLM) are supported. Hosted: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini/Vertex AI, Azure, Bedrock, Databricks, OpenRouter and many others. ACP providers (Claude Code, Codex, Amp, Pi) route work to that agent under its own subscription and terms, and receive Goose extensions as MCP servers.
final_records.data_handling_note: With a local model, prompts and code stay on the machine; with a hosted or ACP provider, content goes to that provider under its own retention and training terms. Goose stores full conversations and tool calls/results locally (sessions.db; no documented retention limit); CLI and server logs are deleted after two weeks, and llm_request logs keep the 10 most recent raw model requests and responses. Anonymous usage data (PostHog) is opt-in, off until the user agrees, and excludes conversations and code. OpenTelemetry export is off unless an endpoint is set; message-content capture defaults to false. Since v1.53.0 (2 Oct 2026) the default build (used for the macOS and Windows Desktop bundles) fetches public model metadata from models.dev at startup (no session content; bundled offline fallback); Desktop also runs an auto-update check by default. Opt-in Live voice in Desktop (v1.52.0) sends audio, recent conversation context and delegated tool results to OpenAI, whatever model provider the session uses; opt-in cloud dictation (OpenAI, Groq, ElevenLabs) sends audio to that service. No project-level DPA or certification.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer a local model; use a hosted or ACP provider only under an institutional DPA/no-training agreement for that provider. Keep anonymous usage data off; keep Live voice (OpenAI, whatever the session provider) and cloud dictation off unless an institutional agreement covers that service.
suitability_notes.special: Only with inference on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware, all cloud and ACP provider routes unused, usage data off, OTel export off or sent only to an institution-controlled collector, Live voice and cloud dictation off, Desktop updates centrally managed, and outbound egress blocked or allow-listed at host or network level (the default build contacts models.dev at startup; Desktop checks for updates).

compliance: Customer-operated local route; Apache-2.0 client license does not certify a deployment.
final_records.pricing: Free open-source software (Apache-2.0); no paid Goose plan found on first-party pages. Hosted model, API or subscription costs depend on the chosen provider.

final_records.notes: Open-source desktop app, CLI and API under Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) governance. Privacy posture is set mainly by the configured model provider and enabled extensions. Actively maintained: five releases between 14 Sep and 8 Oct 2026 (v1.50.1 to v1.54.0); Nostr session sharing was removed in v1.54.0, and roaming (p2p remote access) is experimental and absent from released binaries.

required_controls: Run inference only on the same machine (built-in llama.cpp, or Ollama/LM Studio serving on localhost) or on an institution-owned model server inside the network (e.g. a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as vLLM); leave all hosted and ACP provider routes unconfigured, and point every model role Goose uses, not only the main session model, at that endpoint.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Keep no cloud provider API keys in the environment, .env files or Goose's stored configuration, and check the effective provider, model and extension settings before use (environment variables such as GOOSE_PROVIDER and recipes can also set the provider).

Keep anonymous usage data off (GOOSE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false or GOOSE_TELEMETRY_OFF=1); leave OpenTelemetry and Langfuse export unset, or send OTel only to an institution-controlled collector with content capture off.

Block or allow-list outbound network egress at the host or network level and test that the block holds. The default build fetches model metadata from models.dev at startup (since v1.53.0); a build without online-model-meta removes only that request.
Manage Desktop updates centrally: the auto-updater is on by default, so disable or block it and roll out reviewed releases through institutional software management.

Keep opt-in cloud features and network tools off: Live voice (OpenAI), cloud dictation (OpenAI, Groq, ElevenLabs), the Telegram gateway, web search or fetch tools, and remote or cloud-hosted MCP extensions.
Protect the local session database, command history and logs (including llm_request logs) under institutional access, encryption and retention rules.
residual_risks: No documented runtime setting locks Goose to local providers; the project's custom-distribution guide only suggests a modified UI or an enforcing recipe. One mis-set provider, ACP agent, extension or voice/dictation setting can send data off-device.

sessions.db keeps full prompts, tool arguments and results with no documented retention limit; llm_request logs keep the raw payloads of the last 10 model requests; only CLI and server logs have a documented two-week cleanup.
Local models have smaller context windows and weaker tool calling (per Goose's own local-inference post), which can push users toward cloud routes mid-project.
Model weights downloaded from Hugging Face and third-party MCP extensions need provenance and security review.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
Updates can add new default network calls (v1.53.0 added the startup models.dev fetch), so a configuration checked once must be re-checked for each release.

final_records.name: Cursor
final_records.deployment: cloud (local IDE/CLI client; inference, planning and the agent loop run in Cursor's cloud; Cloud Agent tool execution can move to customer-run machines, but tool outputs, which may contain code, and transcripts still flow to Cursor)
final_records.model_backend: Cursor models (Composer 2.5; Grok 4.5/4.6/4.7, Grok 4.5 documented as a joint Cursor/SpaceXAI model) + hosted third-party models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Moonshot, Z.ai) + BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock); all requests routed through Cursor's backend
final_records.data_handling_note: Terms (3 Sep 2026) bar training on Content without explicit agreement; turning Privacy Mode off lets Cursor store and use code data to train its models, and some inference providers may temporarily store inputs and outputs. Privacy Mode is on by default for Teams and Enterprise and admin-enforceable; the individual-plan default is not stated (Cursor's MDM guidance warns personal accounts might not have it on). With Privacy Mode on, providers run under ZDR agreements, but abuse-flagged data may be stored for investigation, and the Privacy Policy (29 Sep 2026) allows analysis of security-flagged inputs. Standard Privacy Mode still lets Cursor store code for Cloud Agents and Grok Bot; Privacy Mode (Legacy) does not support Cloud Agents and blocks Grok Bot. Exceptions: BYOK is outside Cursor's ZDR and still transits Cursor's backend. Anthropic retains Claude Fable 5/5.1 inputs and outputs for harm review (deleted after 30 days unless under safety investigation or legal hold); these models stay off until an admin approves the retention policy on Enterprise (approved per organization, then controlled per team or group) or with Privacy Mode on, but are on by default for individual and Teams accounts with Privacy Mode off. Cursor temporarily caches encrypted file contents. Cloud Agents keep transcripts (prompts, responses, tool calls, diff context) indefinitely by default (deletable via API; Enterprise can cap retention) and encrypted VM snapshots including cloned code for up to 90 days of inactivity, not deletable on demand; other Cursor pages state shorter retention, so the longest documented figure is used. Grok Bot, included with paid individual plans and on by default for Teams, keeps files on persistent US cloud computers not covered by the US-only residency program by default, and ignores model allowlists; its security page says team Privacy Mode applies, while Cursor's privacy FAQ calls it a separate product surface with its own data flows. The DPA bars sensitive/special-category data and does not cover individual plans.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Teams or Enterprise under the DPA (individual plans are not covered) with Privacy Mode enforced org-wide. BYOK blocking, group-level model access control, the Grok Bot off switch and Cloud Agent retention caps are Enterprise-only. On Teams, Grok Bot is on with no off switch unless the team uses Privacy Mode (Legacy), Fable-class retention models stay off only while no admin approves them, and personal data should be kept out of Cloud Agents and Grok Bot. US-only data residency is Enterprise-only; EU coverage is inference-only and on request.
suitability_notes.special: Inference and the agent loop always run in Cursor's cloud (Cursor states it is not an on-prem product), and the DPA bars special-category data. The Enterprise HIPAA BAA and Self-Hosted Machines do not create a customer-controlled inference boundary, so this catalog's rule excludes health/genetic/clinical data.

compliance: Cursor states AIUC-1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certifications and a SOC 2 Type II attestation; reports are on request via trust.cursor.com and were not reviewed.
HIPAA BAA on Enterprise only; PHI is limited to the Eligible Services and Models in Cursor's HIPAA Guide, with Privacy Mode locked org-wide.
DPA (last updated 5 Nov 2025) prohibits sensitive/special-category data and does not apply to individual plans.
final_records.pricing: Monthly list prices (USD, excl. tax): Hobby free; Pro $20; Pro+ $60; Ultra $200; Teams Standard $40/user and Premium $120/user; Enterprise custom. Cursor Start (India only) INR 649/month incl. tax, Cursor models only. Third-party models draw on a pool billed at API rates; Teams/Enterprise also pay a Cursor Token Rate of $0.25/M tokens, including on BYOK requests. US-only data residency adds 10% to eligible model pricing.
final_records.academic: Legacy student discount closed to new sign-ups on 25 Jun 2026 (existing rates kept until the plan expires). Cursor's help centre invites Master's/PhD students, academic researchers and educators to request credits through an Anysphere-hosted Typeform (amounts and criteria not stated); undergraduates get credits or discounts through on-campus and online events.

final_records.notes: AI editor and CLI with cloud inference. SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor on 14 Aug 2026; Cursor now ships Grok models built with SpaceXAI and the bundled Grok Bot agent. Self-Hosted Machines run only tool execution on customer hardware; inference, planning and the agent loop stay in Cursor's cloud. Enterprise adds CMEK for Cloud Agent data, US-only data residency and a HIPAA BAA. BYOK and custom endpoints still pass through Cursor's backend. No customer-controlled inference route is documented.
final_records.tier_gate: Teams or Enterprise with Privacy Mode enforced org-wide + DPA for personal data (individual plans not covered); BYOK blocking, model access control, Grok Bot off-switch and network controls, Cloud Agent retention caps, BAA, CMEK and data residency are Enterprise-only; special-category data not appropriate (cloud-only inference)

residual_risks: Inference, planning and the agent loop run only in Cursor's cloud; Cursor states it is not an on-prem product, and Self-Hosted Machines move tool execution only, with tool outputs (which may contain code) and transcripts still sent to Cursor.
The DPA prohibits sensitive/special-category data; the Enterprise HIPAA BAA is a contractual control on a cloud service, not a customer-controlled boundary.
BYOK and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints still route through Cursor's backend, and BYOK falls outside Cursor's ZDR.
Cloud Agent transcripts are kept indefinitely by default and VM snapshots with cloned code for up to 90 days of inactivity; Grok Bot keeps files on persistent US cloud computers.

final_records.name: GitHub Copilot
final_records.deployment: cloud (GitHub-hosted models via IDE extensions, Copilot CLI, the Copilot desktop app, GitHub.com and cloud agent; not available for GitHub Enterprise Server) / local-capable (Copilot CLI offline mode with a local BYOK model)
final_records.model_backend: GitHub-managed routing to models hosted by OpenAI and GitHub's Azure (OpenAI models); AWS Bedrock, Anthropic and Google Cloud (Anthropic models); Google Cloud (Gemini); xAI (Grok); Azure AI Foundry in GitHub's tenant (Microsoft MAI); and Fireworks AI (open-weight models, and inline-suggestion models for Free and Student; Business/Enterprise inline suggestions run on Azure). Free and Student use auto model selection only. Background utility models run on every plan and surface, and admins can disable them only by disabling Copilot. Local (client-side) BYOK is available in Copilot CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, the Copilot app (public preview; requires GitHub sign-in) and the Copilot SDK; the CLI accepts OpenAI-compatible endpoints (incl. Ollama, vLLM, Foundry Local), Azure OpenAI and Anthropic. Enterprise BYOK (public preview) runs server-side.
final_records.data_handling_note: Business/Enterprise: GitHub states it does not use this data for training (GitHub DPA). GitHub's stated default retention for Business/Enterprise: IDE chat and completion prompts/suggestions are not retained; all other access (e.g. GitHub.com, Mobile, CLI) keeps prompts 28 days; engagement data is kept 2 years. Cloud-agent session logs stay on GitHub.com and can be archived but not deleted. CLI and Copilot app sessions sync to the user's GitHub account by default; for Business/Enterprise users this happens only if the 'Store local sessions in the Cloud' policy allows it. GitHub announced on 28 Aug 2026 that GitHub.com and Mobile chat will be retained for the life of the account once they merge with cloud agent (no earlier than 28 Sep 2026); the chat docs still state 28 days. Individual Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max: GitHub may use interaction data for training from 24 Apr 2026 unless the user opts out; Student is also an individual plan and should be treated the same. GitHub states that model providers operate under ZDR or no-training agreements. Exceptions: Claude Fable 5/5.1 (offered on Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise), where Anthropic retains prompts and outputs by default and ZDR is available only to approved enterprises under a time-bound exemption to end-2026; and some Anthropic beta/preview features. Provider ZDR does not remove GitHub's own retention.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Business/Enterprise under the GitHub DPA; direct volume-licence subscriptions and renewals from 5 Mar 2026 fall under the Generative AI Services Terms. Prefer IDE surfaces, where GitHub states prompts are not retained under Business/Enterprise default settings. Review retention on CLI, GitHub.com and cloud agent, and set the session-sync policy. Keep Claude Fable 5/5.1 disabled unless a ZDR exemption is in place. Review the 'Default policy for new features', effective 22 Oct 2026. US/EU residency requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency and does not by itself establish compliance. Individual and education plans (Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max) are not a personal-data route; where they are used for non-sensitive work, turn off AI model training in Copilot settings.
suitability_notes.special: Only Copilot CLI with COPILOT_OFFLINE=true and a model served on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware qualifies, and only with every special_route control in place (auto-update off, egress blocked, remote MCP servers and web tools off, Ollama in local-only mode). GitHub documents that this mode contacts no GitHub servers and disables telemetry. IDE and Copilot-app BYOK routes were not appraised as fully offline (the app requires GitHub sign-in). GitHub.com, cloud agent and all GitHub-hosted models remain unsuitable.

compliance: The GitHub Data Protection Agreement applies to GitHub Copilot. The GitHub Generative AI Services Terms (Version March 2026) apply to Generative AI Services purchased directly from GitHub under a volume licensing agreement, for new subscriptions and renewals from 5 March 2026 (no training on Inputs or Outputs without documented instructions). Earlier Business/Enterprise subscriptions stay under the archived Copilot Product Specific Terms until renewal.

Customers without a volume licensing agreement are governed by the GitHub Terms of Service (Gen AI Terms §1.B); GitHub's controller processing for individual plans is described in the GitHub General Privacy Statement. Purchases through Microsoft fall under the Microsoft Product Terms for GitHub Offerings (§1.C). Preview features fall under the GitHub Pre-Release License Terms (§7).

US/EU data residency for Copilot is available only with GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency and is off by default; it restricts inference routing but is not by itself an institutional approval.
final_records.pricing: Free ($0; limited chat/agent use, 2,000 completions/month) · Student (free, verified students) · Pro $10/mo (1,500 AI credits/mo incl. 500 flex) · Pro+ $39/mo (7,000) · Max $100/mo (20,000) · Business $19/granted seat/mo (1,900 credits, pooled) · Enterprise $39/granted seat/mo (3,900 credits, pooled). Usage-based billing since 1 June 2026, at 1 AI credit = $0.01. Chat, agents, CLI, the app and code review consume credits; code completions and next edit suggestions are unlimited on paid plans; code review also uses Actions minutes. Data-residency enforcement adds 10% to AI-credit consumption. From 1 Oct 2026, Business/Enterprise seats paid by card or PayPal are charged upfront.
final_records.academic: Copilot Student is free for verified GitHub Education students. Verified teachers and maintainers of popular open-source projects can get Copilot Pro free. Eligibility is re-evaluated monthly. These are individual plans: GitHub's plans FAQ applies AI-model training to individual subscribers unless they opt out, and the plans docs list Student among the individual plans (the training-policy page names only Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max). Treat Student and free Pro as in the training program and set 'Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training' to Disabled.

final_records.notes: Individual Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max interaction data may be used for training unless the user opts out (treat Student the same); Business/Enterprise are excluded. Under Business/Enterprise default settings, GitHub states that retention differs by surface: IDE chat and completion prompts are not retained, other surfaces (GitHub.com, Mobile, CLI) keep prompts 28 days, and cloud-agent logs persist. US/EU residency requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency and adds 10% AI-credit consumption; it does not by itself establish research-data approval. Copilot CLI offline mode (COPILOT_OFFLINE=true) with a local model is the only route this review appraised as documented to run without contacting GitHub; GitHub documents it, but this review did not test it, so confidence is medium. Copilot is not available for GitHub Enterprise Server.
final_records.tier_gate: Business / Enterprise for organizational cloud use; Copilot CLI offline mode with a model on researcher/institution-controlled hardware for special-category data

required_controls: Use Copilot CLI with COPILOT_OFFLINE=true and COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL pointing to a model served on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network (for example Ollama, vLLM or Foundry Local). The endpoint must serve only institution-hosted models and must not forward requests to external providers. Point every model the CLI uses at that endpoint and use no GitHub-hosted models.

If the model is served by Ollama, run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the server.json of the account that runs the Ollama server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no ':cloud' models.

Enforce offline mode and the provider endpoint in a managed environment, verify the effective configuration (environment variables and configuration files) before each session, and keep no GitHub tokens or cloud-provider API keys in that environment. Block egress to GitHub and all other external hosts at the network level and confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.

Disable CLI auto-update (COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false or --no-auto-update; the autoUpdate setting defaults to true and downloads CLI and first-party plugin updates at session start). Install and update a pinned CLI version through an institution-controlled channel.

Enable local sandboxing (off by default) with network access denied or limited to the local model endpoint. Use no remote MCP servers (they are never sandboxed), restrict local MCP servers, and deny or disable built-in web search and web fetch tools.
Do not use /delegate, cloud agent, remote control, session sync or remote export, GitHub.com, the Copilot app or IDE extensions for special-category data.
residual_risks: The CLI is proprietary and closed-source (GitHub Copilot CLI License). Its offline-mode network behaviour is documented by GitHub but cannot be audited independently, and this review did not test it.

COPILOT_OFFLINE is documented only in two how-to pages and the 7 Oct 2026 changelog. It is not listed in the environment-variable table of the CLI command reference, and the offline-mode pages do not mention auto-update or plugin-marketplace updates specifically.

Without COPILOT_OFFLINE=true, GitHub documents that telemetry is still sent even with a local BYOK model and no GitHub sign-in. Discovering or choosing a local Ollama model with /model does not turn on offline mode.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a CLI pointed at local Ollama can still send data to Ollama's cloud unless local-only mode is enabled.

Local sandboxing is off by default and is lightweight OS-level isolation, not a VM or container. The CLI's built-in file tools run in-process outside the OS sandbox and follow the sandbox policy only on a best-effort basis. Unsandboxed agent commands can reach any network the machine can reach.
Copilot CLI keeps full session records under ~/.copilot/session-state and a local SQLite session store. Institutional access, retention and deletion controls are needed.
Capability depends on the local model, which must support tool calling and streaming; GitHub recommends a context window of at least 128k tokens.

final_records.name: Devin Desktop
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Cognition in-house SWE models (SWE-2, SWE-1.x, swe-grep) plus third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weight families (e.g., Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek); Adaptive routing and Fusion pairings. Availability depends on plan; Teams and Enterprise admins can allowlist models. SWE-1.7 Lightning is served on Cerebras.
final_records.data_handling_note: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop. Cognition may train on Customer Data by default; opt-out is limited to paid plans (Pro, Max, Teams; on Teams only an admin), after which Cognition applies no-training and model-provider ZDR, except for abuse/safety flags and legal process. Teams and Enterprise admins can also unlock Anthropic and OpenAI models that require provider retention for up to 30 days (no training). Enterprise terms bar training without written consent. Provider ZDR does not end product retention: Cognition keeps processed data for the customer relationship (DPA: term plus 30 days), keeps Feedback and User Interaction Data as long as it determines, and collects anonymized Usage Data. Third-party ACP agents run outside Devin Desktop's privacy terms, and the data terms for GPT requests billed to a linked ChatGPT plan are not documented. Customer Dedicated Deployment is Cognition-hosted; the Devin brain stays in Cognition Cloud.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-held Teams or Enterprise plan: Pro and Max are individual plans, and the Cognition DPA binds the contracting customer as data controller. On Teams an admin must opt out of training; Enterprise terms bar training without written consent. The posted Cognition DPA applies by reference. Keep ChatGPT-plan linking, third-party ACP agents and the provider-retention model toggles off, and use the Teams/Enterprise model allowlist to restrict to models whose providers are listed DPA subprocessors. Platform and Enterprise terms bar medical/health information and sensitive personal data (e.g., birth dates, ID numbers); remove these fields, because pseudonymization does not make medical data permissible. Customer Dedicated Deployment is still Cognition-hosted.
suitability_notes.special: Inference for Devin Desktop's own agents stays in Cognition Cloud on every route currently offered, including Customer Dedicated Deployment and Devin Cloud Outposts. The legacy Windsurf self-hosted deployment has been in maintenance mode since May 2025 and takes no new customers. The terms also bar medical and sensitive personal data. Not suitable for special-category data under the controlled-infrastructure rule.

compliance: Cognition states SOC 2 Type II (docs and DPA); the trust centre was not publicly readable. The posted DPA applies by reference; exact service/model scope requires confirmation.
US federal deployments only: Cognition lists FedRAMP High, IL4 and ITAR for Devin Desktop, with ZDR for all Desktop features; scoped to federal deployments, not commercial plans.
final_records.pricing: Free $0; Pro $20/month (includes Devin Cloud access); Max $200/month. Teams (up to 200 users): the pricing page lists $80/month plus $40/month per full seat, while the billing docs describe $80/month as a minimum met by $40 full seats and/or prepaid on-demand credits; Devin Desktop needs a full seat (flex seats exclude it). Usage beyond quota is billed at API pricing via on-demand credits. Enterprise: contractual ACU pricing.
final_records.academic: No current official student discount was confirmed.

final_records.name: Google Antigravity
final_records.deployment: cloud inference for Antigravity 2.0, CLI, IDE and IDE extensions (consumer Google account or Gemini Enterprise/Google Cloud); local-capable Antigravity SDK with on-device or local OpenAI-compatible models
final_records.model_backend: Google-hosted Gemini models (Flash and Pro families) plus third-party models offered through Google (Anthropic Claude; GPT-OSS-120b on consumer plans until its announced 2 November 2026 removal). Availability varies by surface, plan and enterprise administrator opt-in, and lightweight Gemini models still run in the background when a third-party model is selected. Only the SDK can use local models (Gemma 4 via LiteRT, or Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM endpoints).
final_records.data_handling_note: Consumer accounts: Google records and stores Interactions (user data, usage data, metadata, feedback) and uses them to improve Google and Alphabet products and machine-learning technologies, and employees and contractors may review them. Turning off Enable Telemetry in Antigravity 2.0 Account settings stops interaction collection. The CLI's enableTelemetry setting is documented only as anonymous usage statistics and crash reports, so whether it also stops interaction use is not stated. Deletion is by email request, and no retention period is stated. Gemini Enterprise/Google Cloud: Google Cloud terms apply, Google Cloud's training restriction bars training on Customer Data without permission, and client telemetry and model interactions are logged to the customer's selected Google Cloud project. Enterprise inference stays in Google Cloud (global, us or eu; third-party models have no in-country regions). SDK with a Gemini API key: model calls fall under the Gemini API terms (unpaid quota is used for product improvement with human review; paid quota is not, but prompts are logged for a limited period for abuse detection). No SDK-specific terms are published. The SDK local-model route is documented to run without an API key or internet connection.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Gemini Enterprise or a Google Cloud project under the institution's Google Cloud agreement, through Antigravity 2.0, the CLI or the IDE extensions (the standalone Antigravity IDE is not supported for enterprise). Keep telemetry in an institution project, choose the eu location where residency matters, and leave third-party models disabled unless assessed. Google Cloud lists no ISO 27001 or SOC 2 scope for Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise. Consumer accounts are not suitable for personal data; the SDK local-model route is an alternative.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Antigravity SDK local-model route qualifies: LiteRTAgentConfig with an on-device Gemma checkpoint, or LocalOpenAIAgentConfig against a localhost server, on researcher-controlled hardware with outbound network blocked and verified. Do not use LocalAgentConfig: despite its name it calls Google's cloud. Antigravity 2.0, the CLI, the IDE and IDE extensions use cloud inference and are not acceptable, Gemini Enterprise and VPC Service Controls notwithstanding.

compliance: Enterprise route runs under the Google Cloud Terms of Service. 'Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise' is listed by name under Agentic AI Services in the Google Cloud Platform Services Summary (last modified 30 Sep 2026), and the Service Specific Terms state that Google will not train on Customer Data without permission.

Google Cloud's AI developer tools overview (last updated 2026-10-08) states that Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise does not support Access Transparency, FedRAMP, IL4/IL5, ISO 27001/42001, ITAR or SOC 1/2/3.
Consumer use is governed by the Google Terms of Service, the Antigravity Additional Terms and the Google Privacy Policy; no data processing addendum is listed for consumer use.
final_records.pricing: Individual: USD 0 plan with weekly-refreshed quota; Google AI Pro and Ultra add higher rate limits and AI-credit overages (consumer plan prices are not listed on the Antigravity pricing page). Business plan via Google Cloud: API access with consumption-based pricing; for eligible customers, Gemini Enterprise Standard/Plus from USD 30 per seat per month or Pay-as-you-go with no seat fee. Enterprise third-party models require administrator opt-in and are billed by token consumption. Google Cloud's AI developer tools overview states that the enterprise project must have Cloud Billing enabled on an invoiced billing account.
final_records.academic: No academic tier or education entitlement is listed on the Antigravity pricing or plans pages. Consumer Google AI plans are not an institutional data-protection route.
