final_records.name: Sourcegraph Cody
final_records.deployment: cloud / self-hostable / on-prem
final_records.model_backend: Sourcegraph Model Provider (Cody Gateway) gives Enterprise instances hosted Anthropic, OpenAI and Google models. It is configured by default on Sourcegraph Cloud; self-hosted customers confirm access with their account manager. Autocomplete and Smart Apply models include Fireworks-hosted models (US Iowa). Self-hosted instances can instead configure BYOK providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini/Vertex, Fireworks), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Hugging Face TGI; the docs say BYOK with managed services is supported only on self-hosted instances. The model list changes often; check the current supported-models page and the instance's modelConfiguration.
final_records.data_handling_note: Enterprise only. The Cody FAQ states Sourcegraph will not train on Enterprise customers' data; the ToS (last modified 2026-07-22) allows fine-tuning only if enabled for the instance and says Partner LLMs reached through Sourcegraph keep zero retention (temporary abuse/harm retention excepted) and do not train. Product-level retention is separate: the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) lists maintaining AI conversation history during the subscription term as a processing purpose; after expiry Sourcegraph returns or deletes data on the customer's instruction, and without an instruction within 60 days deletes all Customer Personal Data, including AI conversation data, within 90 days. The partner zero-retention commitment applies only to access through Sourcegraph's Partner LLMs, so with BYOK the customer's own provider agreement sets retention. The AI Terms (2026-06-12) apply only to agreements signed before 2024-02-15 or Order Forms that incorporate them; the Cody notice (2024-02-15) applies only to older Cody licences. Self-hosted instances send aggregated pings (no code, but including the installer/admin email, instance URL and IP) and license verification checks, and export telemetry events (numeric metadata, anonymized user IDs) to Sourcegraph by default.

suitability_notes.personal: Requires an Enterprise Order Form and the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05; EEA/UK transfer terms). The subprocessor list names Anthropic, Fireworks AI and Google (all USA) for AI queries and code snippets. OpenAI is listed only for embeddings when the customer enables them. Amp (USA) is listed for error data that can include customer code. Confirm which AI terms the Order Form incorporates, the model routing (Cody Gateway vs BYOK), conversation-history retention and deletion on request. Context Filters can restrict which repositories Cody sends as context. BYOK to a cloud model is still an external processor. Agentic context fetching is on by default and its review step defaults to Gemini 2.5 Flash (fallback Claude Haiku or GPT 4.1 mini), so a Claude-only chat setup can still send context to Google or OpenAI; include it in the routing check. The subprocessor page says self-hosted personal data is processed only when shared for support, but self-hosted instances using Cody Gateway still send prompts and code snippets to the LLM providers.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate. The ToS, which also covers self-hosted Software, says the product is not designed to store GDPR Art. 9 special-category data or HIPAA PHI and must not be used to store it; the DPA marks special-category data as not processed. Default routing also sends code snippets to cloud LLMs, and no first-party source documents an end-to-end deployment with inference on customer-controlled infrastructure.

compliance: SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 listed on the Sourcegraph Security Portal; reports are access-gated and Cody/AI-feature scope is not confirmed
Standard DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) with EEA/UK restricted-transfer terms
ToS: Sourcegraph is not a HIPAA Business Associate; GDPR Art. 9 special-category data excluded
Applicable Order Form and AI terms require confirmation
final_records.pricing: Sourcegraph Enterprise only: the pricing page lists a $16K minimum annual contract that includes credits for AI features and scales with team size; contact sales. The pricing page does not name Cody. Cody access on Free, Pro and Enterprise Starter ended 2025-07-23.
final_records.academic: No published academic or student discount. Cody is available only with Sourcegraph Enterprise ($16K minimum annual contract on the pricing page). The pricing FAQ offers sales-led trials with credits; contact sales about institutional pricing.
use_cases: Multi-repo codebase understanding and architecture queries
AI chat, inline edit, and autocomplete in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio (experimental)
Context-aware code generation using Sourcegraph Search context from local and remote repositories
Automated prompt workflows (custom Prompts feature)
Debug, explain, and refactor code with enterprise codebase context
Run suggested terminal commands from chat; agentic terminal context is experimental and off by default on Enterprise
Large-scale research or bioinformatics pipelines with complex cross-repo dependencies
final_records.notes: Active, Enterprise-only. Sourcegraph 8.0 (2026-09-17) added a supported Cody model. The Cody FAQ still carries its 2025 line that Sourcegraph is fully committed to Cody Enterprise, but its 2026-10-05 edit removed the longer sunset section, including the statement that Cody Enterprise will be actively supported, developed and maintained. The VS Code and JetBrains extensions were last released on 2026-06-17. Since Sourcegraph 7.0 (2026-02-25), Deep Search replaces Cody in the browser for Deep Search customers; the editor extensions are unaffected. Current AI use is governed by the Sourcegraph ToS and DPA. The AI Terms apply only to pre-2024-02-15 agreements or Order Forms that incorporate them, and the Cody notice (last modified 2024-02-15) only to older Cody licences. The model-provider docs nonetheless say the AI Terms apply to all Model Provider use. The Ollama local-model page is scoped to the discontinued Free/Pro plans. The extension package ships an Apache-2.0 licence file, but the client source repository is no longer public (an archived 2025 snapshot remains) and the required Sourcegraph Enterprise server is proprietary.
final_records.tier_gate: current Enterprise contract + DPA + verified model routing

residual_risks: The ToS (last modified 2026-07-22) excludes GDPR Art. 9 special-category data and HIPAA PHI for hosted Services and self-hosted Software; the DPA (2026-10-05) marks special-category data as not processed.

Default Cody Gateway routing sends prompts and code snippets to cloud LLM providers. Defaults: Anthropic for chat, Fireworks AI (US Iowa) for autocomplete, Google Gemini for the agentic-context review step (on by default). OpenAI models are selectable.

An OpenAI-compatible or Hugging Face TGI endpoint can be configured, but no first-party source documents an end-to-end customer-controlled deployment; the FAQ says self-hosted instances need internet access for external LLM services, and license verification checks contact Sourcegraph unless the license is exempt.

final_records.name: OpenCode
final_records.deployment: local-capable / cloud
final_records.model_backend: BYOK cloud providers (75+ via Models.dev, plus GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT Plus/Pro and GitLab Duo sign-in) or local Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints; optional hosted OpenCode Zen (pay-as-you-go) and OpenCode Go (subscription) gateways, and in V2 the hosted OpenCode Console gateway for your own provider keys.
final_records.data_handling_note: The client keeps sessions, logs and credentials on the local machine (~/.local/share/opencode). The vendor states that it does not store code or context data and that prompts go directly to the selected provider. With no OpenCode key set, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models by default (vendor source code), so choose a provider explicitly and block the rest. The hosted routes are not uniformly zero-retention. On Zen, OpenAI and Anthropic requests are retained for 30 days; Mistral and Jev data follow those providers' own retention policies; several free models may use data to improve the model; NVIDIA free endpoints log use; and Muse Spark Contributor trains Meta models. On Go, the Grok, GPT Luna and Claude Haiku routes retain for 30 days, the Muse Spark Contributor models train, and the DeepSeek ZDR agreement is renewed monthly. The V2 Console gateway records each request and its cost; its content retention is not documented. The Terms allow Content from unpaid accounts on the hosted Services to be used to improve them. V1 session sharing uploads conversations to opencode.ai; V2 has no sharing yet. Both lines can send web searches to third parties (V1 when the OpenCode or Go provider is used, or with the Exa/Parallel flags; V2 through five search providers or Console-hosted search), and the webfetch tool, allowed by default, can reach any URL. Disable sharing, web search and webfetch for private work, and review every selected provider.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local provider, or a direct provider or Zen/Go model whose retention and DPA you have verified. Zen and Go are not uniformly ZDR, and the Muse Spark Contributor models permit training. The built-in OpenCode free models are enabled by default when no key is set: block them, and disable sharing, web search and webfetch.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a fully local model on controlled infrastructure (a self-run Ollama in local-only mode, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM), all other providers blocked (including the built-in OpenCode free models), and sharing, web search and webfetch disabled. V1 can enforce these settings through system managed config. V2 documents no system managed config (only user, project and .well-known files, plus vendor-hosted Console policy), so pin to 1.x for enforced settings or lock the V2 config with OS controls. Zen, Go, the Console gateway, Ollama Cloud or Ollama ':cloud' models and other cloud providers are not acceptable.

final_records.pricing: The client is free and open source (MIT). OpenCode Zen (optional) is pay-as-you-go, priced per 1M tokens, with card fees passed through. By default Zen adds $20 when the balance falls below $5; this can be changed or disabled. Zen team workspaces are free during the beta, with pricing to be announced. OpenCode Go (optional) is a subscription: Go at $10/month or Go Plus at $40/month, with per-model usage limits. Enterprise is per-seat and quote-based, with no token charge when your own LLM gateway is used.
final_records.academic: The open-source client is available without an academic subscription; no special academic entitlement is asserted.
use_cases: Terminal-first AI coding agent (TUI)
Multi-provider LLM coding assistant
Local/offline AI coding with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM
Multi-session parallel agents on same codebase
Enterprise coding agent with internal LLM gateway
LSP-integrated code editing with AI
MCP tool integration for coding agents
GitHub Copilot / ChatGPT Plus account integration
final_records.notes: Open-source coding agent for the terminal, desktop, web and IDE, with local, direct-provider and hosted Zen, Go and Console routes. OpenCode 2 (2.0.0 published on npm on 11 September 2026; the opencode.ai installer now installs v2 and replaces the V1 binary) is developed in parallel with the maintained 1.x line. V2 does not yet support session sharing or run language servers, always runs a local background service, offers web search through five third-party providers (Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Tavily, TinyFish) or Console-hosted search, and accepts provider and permission policies from the Console. The Zen docs say models are hosted in the US and EU; the Zen landing page says the US. Advisory GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 (September 2026, high severity) affected `opencode serve` on npm/pnpm/Bun installs and was fixed in 1.18.22. Keep the client patched and do not expose the local server.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model, all other providers (including the built-in OpenCode free models) blocked, sharing, web search and webfetch disabled for regulated data

required_controls: Run inference only through a local model runtime (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM) on controlled infrastructure; do not use the separate Ollama Cloud provider.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Block all other providers, including the built-in "opencode" provider whose hosted free models are enabled when no key is set: V1 enabled_providers/disabled_providers, or a V2 experimental.policies provider.use deny "*" followed by an allow for the local provider. Check the log, because invalid policy statements are dropped with a warning.

Set every model role explicitly to the local provider (V1 model and small_model), and confirm sessions do not switch models (V2 falls back to the newest available supported model when the configured one is unavailable). Keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env files, and remove stored hosted-provider credentials from ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.
Set share to "disabled" (V1 default is manual; V2 does not yet support sharing).

Disable web search (V2 "websearch": false; on V1 avoid the OpenCode/Go providers and leave OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA/PARALLEL off) and deny webfetch (V1 permission webfetch deny; V2 policy permission "webfetch:*" deny). Review MCP servers, plugins and LSP downloads for egress.

Enforce the settings: on V1 through managed config (/etc/opencode, /Library/Application Support/opencode, %ProgramData%\opencode, or a macOS MDM profile). V2 (2.0.26) has no documented system managed config, so pin to 1.x where enforcement is required, or protect the V2 config files with OS controls; Console-delivered policy needs a vendor-cloud connection.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions, because project config files, remote .well-known config and the OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT variable are also loaded and may set providers, tools or permissions.

Disable auto-update or manage updates centrally (V1 autoupdate false or OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE; V2 update "disable"). On offline hosts also disable the remote model-catalog fetch and LSP downloads (documented V1 flags: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD).
Restrict host network egress to the local model endpoint, because shell commands run with the user's network access, and confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.
Keep clients at or above the patched versions; do not expose opencode serve/web or the V2 background service beyond localhost, and set a server password.
residual_risks: Local sessions, logs, credentials (auth.json) and the session database under ~/.local/share/opencode need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

Out of the box, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models, and V2 falls back to the newest available model when the configured one is unavailable; a missing deny rule or a stopped local runtime can route prompts to hosted models, some of which permit data use for improvement or training.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
V2 provider policies are experimental, invalid statements are dropped with a warning, and policies do not sandbox plugin code.
V2 has no documented system managed config; users can change their own global config unless OS controls prevent it.
The local HTTP server and web UI have had high or critical advisories (most recently GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4, September 2026); V2 always runs a local background service.
OpenCode 2 is a new major line; V2 equivalents of some V1 egress flags were not verified.
Third-party MCP servers, plugins and LSP servers can send data outside the controlled boundary.

final_records.name: Crush
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: Bring your own provider: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Hugging Face, Vercel AI Gateway, Z.ai, MiniMax, Moonshot and other Catwalk-listed providers via API keys (Vertex AI and Bedrock also via Google Cloud or AWS credentials), or any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint; account sign-in for Charm Hyper (official, optional), GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT and xAI Grok; local models via Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, oMLX or LiteLLM
final_records.data_handling_note: The CLI keeps sessions, logs (./.crush) and state on the machine; model requests go to the providers configured for the large and small model slots. Built-in tools can still reach the web from a local-model setup: the sourcegraph tool (enabled by default, no permission prompt) sends model-written search queries to sourcegraph.com; agentic_fetch asks once, then a sub-agent searches DuckDuckGo and fetches pages without further prompts; fetch and download ask per call. Pseudonymous usage metrics (PostHog via data.charm.land) are on by default; the README states that prompts and responses are never collected, but source code shows crash and panic error messages are sent. Disable metrics with CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or `option metrics false`. A Hyper login links the metrics device ID to the Hyper account. At startup Crush queries the GitHub releases API for new versions (no documented opt-out) and, unless provider auto-update or default providers are disabled, refreshes the Catwalk catalog and the Hyper provider definition from hyper.charm.land. Optional Hyper, per its privacy policy: no training on prompts or outputs; content not stored by default but kept up to 30 days when retained for debugging, abuse prevention or legal compliance; operational usage data 90 days; operated from the US and routed to unnamed third-party model providers. The README and Hyper home page call Hyper zero data retention; the privacy policy's 30-day exception is the operative term. ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot and Grok sign-ins follow those accounts' own terms.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local model with metrics disabled and governed tool and network access, or approve the chosen cloud route separately: Hyper under its DPA, or an API provider or signed-in account (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Grok) under that vendor's terms.
suitability_notes.special: Only with fully local models in both the large and small model slots (Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, LM Studio, oMLX, or LiteLLM serving local models only), no cloud sign-ins or provider keys, metrics and provider auto-update disabled, built-in web tools denied (sourcegraph, agentic_fetch, fetch, download), egress blocked and controlled execution. Hyper and all cloud providers are not appropriate. FSL-1.1-MIT is source-available, not an OSI open-source licence, until each release converts to MIT on its second anniversary.

compliance: Hyper: DPA available on request (legal@charm.land); Charm acts as processor for prompts and outputs and as controller for account, usage and analytics data.
Hyper: EEA, UK and Swiss data is transferred to the US under safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses; third-party model providers may process data in other jurisdictions.
No SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA/BAA statement found on the Hyper pages checked; GDPR compliance is a vendor statement.
Hyper terms do not govern a fully local model route.
final_records.pricing: Crush CLI: no licence fee (FSL-1.1-MIT); local models carry no vendor inference fee. Optional Hyper (checked 2026-10-10): Free $0/month with 100 Hypercredits per month; Subscription $20/month, listed as 250 Hypercredits 'refreshing daily' (the Plans & Billing docs describe monthly allocations, so the paid-plan cadence is unclear); non-expiring prepaid bundles from $5 for 100 Hypercredits; 1 Hypercredit is currently 5 cents. API providers and ChatGPT, Copilot or Grok subscriptions bill separately.
final_records.academic: FSL-1.1-MIT expressly permits internal use, non-commercial education and non-commercial research at no cost; only a Competing Use is excluded. No academic pricing for Hyper found on its first-party pages; inference costs depend on the provider.
use_cases: Agentic code generation and editing in the terminal
Multi-file codebase exploration and refactoring
LSP-enhanced code context for AI prompting
MCP-extensible tool workflows (stdio, http, sse)
Local/offline coding on privacy-sensitive code via Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or oMLX
Multi-model mid-session switching for cost/quality tradeoffs
Plan Mode for agreeing a plan before the agent edits files
Non-interactive scripted runs with crush run
Shared local workspaces across several clients via the opt-in client/server mode
Air-gapped or restricted-network deployments
final_records.notes: Local-capable terminal coding agent from Charm under FSL-1.1-MIT (source-available; each release converts to MIT after two years). Actively maintained, with several releases a month (latest v0.98.1 on 2026-10-09). Since September it added sign-in with a ChatGPT subscription (v0.94.1) and an xAI Grok account (v0.98.0). Sensitive-data use requires fully local models, no cloud sign-ins, metrics and provider updates disabled, built-in web tools denied, and blocked egress.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local models with cloud sign-ins, metrics, auto-update and built-in web tools off for special-category data; Hyper DPA or an approved provider contract for cloud use with personal data

required_controls: Configure only local inference for both the large and small model slots (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, oMLX, or a LiteLLM gateway that serves local models only); `option default-providers false` hides built-in cloud providers.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Do not sign in to Hyper, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT or Grok, and keep cloud provider API keys out of the environment.
Disable usage metrics with CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or `option metrics false`.

Disable provider catalog auto-update (CRUSH_DISABLE_PROVIDER_AUTO_UPDATE=1 or `option provider-auto-update false`) and block egress at the network level, including the startup version check to api.github.com, then verify the block.
Deny the built-in web tools with `permissions deny sourcegraph agentic_fetch fetch download`; sourcegraph sends queries to sourcegraph.com without a permission prompt.
Keep tool permission prompts on (no --yolo), restrict MCP servers, hooks and shell access, and review any project crushrc or crush.json before launch.
Apply institutional access, retention and encryption controls to local sessions, logs (./.crush) and the data directory.
residual_risks: A cloud provider key in the environment or a misconfigured provider or model slot sends prompts off the machine; verify egress.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, and Crush auto-discovers models from local providers, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
Project-local crushrc and crush.json run as trusted code at load, so an untrusted repository can execute commands.
Built-in web tools (sourcegraph without a prompt; agentic_fetch, whose inner web search and fetch calls skip prompts and hooks), MCP servers, hooks and shell tools can move data off the machine.
In the opt-in client/server mode, --yolo is first-wins per workspace, so a later client cannot restore permission prompts on a workspace another client started with --yolo.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
FSL-1.1-MIT is source-available, not an OSI open-source licence, until each release converts to MIT on its second anniversary.

final_records.name: Mistral Vibe
final_records.deployment: cloud / local-capable / self-hostable
final_records.model_backend: Mistral-hosted models (product page lists Mistral Medium, Devstral 2 and Codestral) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted Devstral Small 2 or Mistral Small 4. Teleport/Vibe Code Web sessions always run on Mistral Medium 3.5 in Mistral's cloud. Model licences are separate from the client licence.
final_records.data_handling_note: Best route is local: the Vibe CLI with a self-configured OpenAI-compatible model server, enable_telemetry=false and enable_auto_update=false, and no Mistral API key configured; Mistral's offline docs say the CLI then does not contact mistral.ai, but a configured Mistral API key triggers a startup fetch of admin-managed config from Mistral, and MCP servers, connectors and skills that reach external systems must be disabled separately. Defaults are cloud-facing: telemetry (anonymous usage and error data) and auto-update are on by default. Cloud training (help article dated 2026-08-31): Vibe inputs/outputs train Mistral models by default unless opted out; Enterprise is opted out by default under admin control; no separate Team exception is stated; Mistral Studio pay-as-you-go keys have their own opt-out control. Thumbs-up/down feedback authorizes use of the rated input/output on any plan. Retention (Privacy Policy effective 2026-09-03): API inputs/outputs kept 30 rolling days for abuse monitoring unless ZDR is active; Vibe conversations until deleted. ZDR is discretionary and available only to pay-as-you-go organizations for stateless API calls; Vibe CLI calls follow it only when such an organization has approved ZDR; it never covers Vibe Work, Chat or other stateful products. Teleport ('/teleport', '&' prompts) moves a session into a Mistral cloud sandbox whose activity is retained per plan.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer the local route. Cloud route: Enterprise (training opted out by default) or a verified training opt-out on other plans, under the DPA where it applies to the plan; Mistral may train as controller unless the customer opted out. Accept 30-day API abuse-monitoring retention (ZDR only for approved pay-as-you-go organizations); give no thumbs-up/down feedback; do not teleport to Vibe Code Web unless its plan retention is accepted.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Vibe CLI on a self-configured local model server, with telemetry and auto-update off, no Mistral API key configured, external tools/connectors and Teleport disabled, outbound traffic blocked except to the model server, Ollama (if used) in local-only mode, and the active provider checked each session. Cloud plans, Enterprise no-training or ZDR are not sufficient.

compliance: Mistral commercial processing terms are service/plan scoped; no general certification or EU-only storage guarantee is asserted.
DPA (effective 2026-07-27) allows transfers outside the EEA under adequacy decisions, other adequate safeguards or SCCs, and lets Mistral train as controller unless the customer has opted out.
final_records.pricing: Free (limited coding sessions); Pro $14.99/month (plan card lists $25.5/month in API credits); Team $24.99/user/month (price calculator starts at 2 users); Enterprise custom (private, self-hosted or on-premises deployments). Prices exclude tax; usage beyond plan limits can continue on pay-as-you-go at API rates. As displayed 2026-10-10.
final_records.academic: Pro Education: $5.99/month (excl. tax) for verified students at accredited higher-education institutions, for at most 12 months and only if they have not used Vibe or Le Chat before; the student card lists $15/month in API credits. No staff or institutional academic discount is stated on the pricing page.
use_cases: Multi-file code refactoring
Automated test generation
Pull request review and creation
Legacy code migration
Agentic terminal coding (long-running autonomous tasks)
IDE-integrated coding assistance (VS Code, JetBrains, Zed)
Codebase-wide context and search
GitHub/GitLab/Jira/Linear integration
Local/air-gapped coding with self-hosted Devstral Small 2
Research software engineering and scripting
API documentation generation
final_records.notes: Apache-2.0 repository and default Python TUI; the bundled Rust TUI (vibe-rs, started with VIBE_CLI=rust) declares a Proprietary licence in its Cargo.toml. Commercial Vibe plans, a VS Code extension, ACP integration for JetBrains and Vibe Code Web cloud sandboxes; the former Mistral Code product page redirects to Mistral Vibe. Actively maintained (v2.26.1, 2026-10-09). Since 2026-09-11: advisory MAI-2026-003 (2026-09-14) reported shell-permission bypasses fixed in v2.25.4; v2.26.0 extended client usage telemetry and Teleport in the Rust CLI and VS Code extension; v2.26.1 removed the built-in local Devstral model, and a stale pin to it falls back to the hosted default with a warning.
final_records.tier_gate: Cloud personal data: Enterprise (training opted out by default) or a verified training opt-out (DPA coverage per plan to confirm); special-category data: self-configured local model, telemetry and auto-update off, no Mistral API key configured

required_controls: Define the local OpenAI-compatible provider and model explicitly in config.toml (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio or Ollama on hardware you control), make sure no model entry in the effective configuration points to a hosted provider, and check the active model, provider and API base (for example with /status) before each session.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Keep no Mistral API key on the machine or in the environment (MISTRAL_API_KEY, OS keyring, ~/.vibe/.env): with a key present the CLI fetches admin-managed config from Mistral at startup, and Teleport and the hosted-default fallback can reach Mistral's cloud.

Set enable_telemetry = false and enable_auto_update = false in a local config the institution controls; do not rely on Mistral admin-managed config, which Mistral describes as a distribution mechanism, not a security control, and which is fetched over HTTP from Mistral.

Disable or vet MCP servers, connectors, skills and web tools that reach external systems; do not use /teleport, '&' prompts or Vibe Code Web; do not trust repository folders that ship their own .vibe/config.toml.
Keep enable_otel off (OpenTelemetry export requires enable_telemetry = true, so it cannot be combined with the telemetry-off route).
Run v2.25.4 or later (MAI-2026-003 shell-permission fixes) inside an isolated workspace with least-privilege credentials; with auto-update off, track Mistral security advisories and update manually.
Block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the local model server, and verify the block before sensitive sessions.
residual_risks: Since v2.26.1 a stale pin to the removed built-in local model ('local' alias) falls back to the hosted Mistral default with only a warning; if a Mistral API key is present, code and data can go to Mistral's cloud.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost API base alone does not guarantee local inference.
Telemetry and auto-update are on by default; a missed setting sends usage/error data or update checks off-host.

Configuration precedence (admin config > CLI flags > env vars > project config.toml > user config.toml) means an organization admin config or a trusted repository's .vibe/config.toml can silently change the active model or provider; admin-managed values show only inside /config, with no startup indicator.
Shell-permission bypasses disclosed in September 2026 show prompt-injected content can trigger commands; treat the agent as able to read anything the user account can.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Cloud no-training or ZDR is not a substitute: ZDR covers only pay-as-you-go stateless API endpoints, not Vibe Work, Chat or other stateful products; Vibe Code Web retains session activity per plan.

final_records.name: Kiro CLI
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Managed cloud catalog; Kiro states it is powered by Amazon Bedrock. Includes Anthropic Claude models, OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, open-weight models (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen) and an Auto router; several models (including Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, all GPT-5.6 tiers and some open-weight models) are labelled Experimental, and Claude Fable 5.1 is an Enterprise-only Preview that admins must add through model governance. Per the models page (updated 8 Oct 2026), GPT-5.6 has Global inference scope and uses the US endpoint even for Frankfurt profiles; other models have Geography scope (the enterprise profile's US or EU geography; Free and individual users use the US endpoint); Fable 5.1 runs only in us-east-1. AWS GovCloud (US) has a separate catalog with inference kept in GovCloud. The docs index lists no local or bring-your-own model option. Models and credit multipliers change often.
final_records.data_handling_note: Free Tier and individual subscribers (paid plans accessed via GitHub, Google or AWS Builder ID) may have content used for service improvement, which Kiro says can include model training, unless they opt out (CLI: turn off Telemetry and 'Share Kiro content with AWS'); their content is stored in us-east-1, and Free Tier inputs may also be kept up to 60 days for abuse detection. Students-tier accounts use the same sign-in methods and the Students FAQ points them to the same training opt-out; Kiro does not state whether they count as individual subscribers. Enterprise users (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) are excluded from service improvement and automatically opted out of telemetry/content collection, but content may be stored in the profile Region (US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt) or AWS GovCloud (US)) to run the service; prompt logs and daily activity reports, when enabled, go to a customer-chosen S3 bucket in the customer's AWS account. Kiro may also collect operational signals (error logs and metrics based on instructions, feedback and responses). Model-specific abuse retention applies to all users: OpenAI GPT classifier-flagged traffic up to 30 days; all Claude Fable 5.1 Preview traffic up to 30 days, with possible human review of flagged traffic by AWS. GPT-5.6 uses Global cross-region inference (possibly outside the profile geography). Optional --cloud sessions keep conversation history, cloned repositories and sandbox files in a Kiro-managed cloud sandbox (us-east-1 only for Identity Center organisations; off for Enterprise until an admin enables it). Running the CLI locally does not make inference local.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Kiro Enterprise profile under institutional AWS terms (Frankfurt profile for EU storage). All models are allowed by default, so restrict GPT-5.6 (Global inference) and Fable 5.1 through model governance, and block Auto if the approved list must bind (Auto can route to any Active model on the profile). Keep Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off unless separately assessed, and decide deliberately on prompt logging. Individual paid, student or social-login plans are insufficient by themselves.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud inference only (commercial or GovCloud AWS Regions); no local or customer-controlled model endpoint is documented, so not suitable under the controlled-infrastructure rule.

compliance: Kiro documents HIPAA eligibility for Kiro IDE and CLI; AWS's HIPAA Eligible Services Reference lists Kiro excluding Kiro Web. A BAA, account, Region and configuration scope still apply; coverage of CLI cloud sessions is not stated.
Kiro states it is in the scope of AWS's ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification; AWS's ISO services-in-scope list shows Kiro (excludes Fable).
final_records.pricing: Individual: Free $0 (50 credits/month; open-weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5, rate-limited); Pro $20/user/month (1,000 credits); Pro+ $40 (2,000); Pro Max $100 (5,000); Power $200 (10,000). Paid add-on credits $0.04 each. Enterprise uses the same paid tiers billed through AWS, with opt-in overage at $0.04/credit and no Free tier; AWS GovCloud (US) is about 20% higher. Prices exclude taxes.
final_records.academic: Kiro for Students gives verified students (18+) at listed universities 1,000 credits/month free for one year (SheerID check; GitHub, Google or Builder ID sign-in with a university email; no add-on credits), then reverts to Free. No Czech institution appeared in the eligible-school list in the page HTML on 2026-10-10. Student accounts are not Enterprise accounts; the Students FAQ points to the training opt-out, so content may be used for service improvement unless the student opts out. Kiro does not state whether Students-tier users count as individual subscribers.
use_cases: Terminal-based AI-assisted coding and chat, including spec-driven development (CLI V3)
Custom agentic workflows via hooks, custom agents, sub-agents and Workflows
MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration with external tools and data sources
CI/CD automation in headless mode with API-key auth (paid plans)
Context-aware shell autocomplete
Kiro agent inside ACP-compatible editors (JetBrains IDEs, Zed)
AWS-native development with IAM Identity Center/SSO auth
US government workloads via AWS GovCloud (US) Enterprise profiles
Long-running tasks in Kiro-managed cloud sandbox sessions (--cloud)
Migration path from Amazon Q Developer CLI (backward-compatible q and q chat entry points)
final_records.notes: Closed-source terminal client and ACP agent for Kiro's cloud inference; successor to the Apache-2.0 Amazon Q Developer CLI, whose repository now receives only critical security fixes. The migration guide states that Kiro CLI is licensed under the AWS Intellectual Property License. CLI V3 (early release, opt-in with --v3) runs the same agent harness as the Kiro IDE and Web. Apply the IDE's enterprise data-protection boundary; payment alone does not establish no-training: the /enterprise page says Pro to Power content is not used to train foundation models, while the data-protection page treats paid social-login/Builder ID users as individual subscribers whose content may be used for service improvement unless they opt out. This record follows the stricter data-protection page (revised 17 Sep and 8 Oct 2026).
final_records.tier_gate: Kiro Enterprise profile (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) under institutional AWS terms, with model governance restricting Global-scope and Preview models (block Auto if the approved list must bind) and Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off or assessed separately; operational storage and model-specific abuse retention still apply

residual_risks: Cloud inference only (commercial or GovCloud AWS Regions); no local or customer-controlled model endpoint is documented.
Running the CLI locally does not keep prompts, code context or tool output on researcher-controlled infrastructure; --cloud sessions also move execution and files to a Kiro-managed cloud sandbox.

final_records.name: Warp
final_records.deployment: Desktop client (macOS, Linux, Windows) and Warp Agent CLI, with Warp-cloud agent harness, control plane and run-data storage. Enterprise can self-host cloud-agent execution workers and map cloud-agent run transcripts, artifacts and attachments to its own AWS S3 bucket; orchestration, run records and Warp Agent inference still route through Warp.
final_records.model_backend: Warp-managed models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weights models hosted by Fireworks AI (e.g. GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek); BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys), ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscription, and OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints (public URL only, e.g. OpenRouter, LiteLLM), all relayed through Warp's server-side agent harness; Enterprise BYOLLM via AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI.
final_records.data_handling_note: Tier-specific. Business and Enterprise: Warp's privacy docs say these plans are covered by its ZDR agreement and no AI interaction or console data is collected; data collection is off by default and admin-enforceable. Free: telemetry must stay on to use AI features, and Warp's agent FAQ reserves the right to use collected data to train models (the privacy notice, last modified 18 Aug 2026, also lists model training as a purpose). Other paid plans (docs: 'paid teams'): data collection is on by default; users can opt out and keep AI. Provider ZDR (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Fireworks AI) covers Warp-managed inference only and excludes Claude Fable 5/5.1, which Anthropic retains (off by default for Enterprise teams; Business default not stated). With customer-supplied inference (BYOK, custom endpoints, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscriptions, team-managed keys, BYOLLM) provider retention and training follow the user's or team's own provider terms; Warp says it cannot enforce ZDR for subscription requests. Product-level retention remains: cloud-synced conversations (per-user setting; Enterprise can disable org-wide) and cloud-agent transcripts, artifacts and attachments sit in Warp-managed storage; only the cloud-agent run data can be mapped to an Enterprise-owned S3 bucket, which Warp's control plane still reads and writes. Codebase Context keeps embeddings; telemetry, when collected, is kept indefinitely; shared sessions expire after about one week. First-party pages conflict: the privacy page requires telemetry for AI on Free while the security pages say opt-out keeps full functionality, and www.warp.dev/legal/security says ZDR is available on the Enterprise plan while the model page says ZDR applies across all plans.

suitability_notes.personal: Business or Enterprise only, with a signed DPA (EU SCCs; subprocessors in the US and Canada). Keep data collection disabled, restrict non-ZDR models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) in the Admin Panel, decide on cloud conversation storage and session/link sharing, and confirm every connected model provider or endpoint; member-provided inference (BYOK, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscriptions) falls outside Warp's ZDR and can be disabled by admins.
suitability_notes.special: Not suitable under this index's rule: for the Warp Agent, the harness and inference routing run on Warp's servers on every route (BYOK, custom endpoints, subscriptions, BYOLLM, self-hosted workers), and local models can be used only when exposed at a public URL. Claude Code or Codex runs on self-hosted workers call their provider directly, but orchestration, transcripts and tool output still pass through Warp's control plane.

compliance: SOC 2 Type II per Warp's security docs; report available to Enterprise customers on request (Trust Center).
DPA (last modified 22 Aug 2025) incorporating EU SCCs; subprocessor list last modified 2 Sep 2026.
Provider ZDR is separate from Warp's own collection and storage; Claude Fable models are excluded from ZDR.

The subprocessor list (last modified 2 Sep 2026) also names Morph LLM (AI-enabled functionality) and Cohere, Turbopuffer and Voyage AI (codebase search); Warp's docs do not state their retention terms.
final_records.pricing: As listed on 10 Oct 2026: Free $0 (no bundled Warp AI; pay-as-you-go add-on credits, or bring-your-own inference limited to individuals and organisations with 10 or fewer employees); Build $20/month; Max $200/month; Business $50/user/month (up to 25 seats; lower with annual billing); Enterprise custom. Warp Factories is priced separately and usage-based. AI, compute and platform credits apply; confirm the live amount before purchase.
final_records.academic: No student or non-profit discount: Warp's pricing FAQ states it does not currently offer discounts or program credits for students or non-profits.
use_cases: Terminal-native agentic coding with the Warp Agent in the desktop app or the Warp Agent CLI
Cloud agents on the Automation Platform (formerly Oz) triggered by schedules, Slack/Linear/GitHub integrations, API or CLI
Codebase indexing and search across large codebases
Running third-party CLI agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) inside Warp with rich input, notifications and code review
Issue triage, spec writing, implementation and PR review through Warp Factories (Early Access) or cloud agents
Team-wide AI-assisted terminal workflows with centralized Admin Panel governance
Enterprise BYOLLM with self-hosted execution workers
final_records.notes: Cloud-orchestrated terminal and agent platform. The Warp Agent harness runs on Warp's backend, so prompts and context pass through Warp even with BYOK, custom endpoints or BYOLLM; Enterprise self-hosting keeps execution, repository clones and runtime secrets (and optionally run data in S3) on customer infrastructure. Separate provider ZDR from Warp's own collection, conversation storage and telemetry, and check the exact plan. The client codebase is open source at github.com/warpdotdev/warp (AGPL-3.0; UI framework crates MIT); the backend that runs the harness and control plane is a Warp-operated cloud service.
final_records.tier_gate: Business or Enterprise with DPA; data collection kept off and non-ZDR models disabled

residual_risks: Warp's control plane orchestrates every run, records run data and routes Warp Agent inference, including runs on self-hosted execution workers; Claude Code or Codex harness runs call their provider directly but still send transcripts and tool output to Warp.
The Warp Agent harness runs server-side, so BYOK and custom-endpoint requests (including tunnelled local models) relay prompts and context through Warp's backend.
Session transcripts, which can contain code context and command output, route through Warp even when execution is self-hosted.

final_records.name: Augment Code
final_records.vendor: Augment Computing, Inc. (Cosmos, Auggie CLI and Context Engine assets acquired by Harness, Inc.; announced 2026-10-08)
final_records.deployment: cloud (vendor-hosted Context Engine and inference; Cosmos tool execution in Augment sandboxes or on customer-run daemons, which still send all LLM calls to Augment)
final_records.model_backend: Managed multi-provider selection plus Prism routing: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Google (Gemini), xAI (Grok), Zhipu AI GLM (hosted on Fireworks) and Moonshot AI Kimi (hosted on Fireworks and Baseten). Enterprise BYOK for customers with their own Enterprise Agreement with Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS or GCP. No local or customer-hosted model endpoint documented. See current model documentation for versions.
final_records.data_handling_note: Paid plans (Standard, Business, Enterprise) exclude training: pricing FAQ ('Commercial Terms of Service'); Professional and Enterprise Terms v1.9 §1.4 ('Company will not train its Models'); third-party model providers are bound by terms 'at least as protective'. Public pages do not say which terms document governs Standard/Business. The Community Terms v1.9 (2026-01-14) instead grant Augment and its model providers training rights on code, output and usage data; the pricing page lists no free plan, so confirm which terms govern a trial. Product retention: the Context Engine stores indexed code (every workspace file not excluded by .gitignore/.augmentignore); Cosmos session snapshots are kept 14 days; Cosmos Files (Expert outputs and memory) persist on Augment with version history (at least one weekly version kept beyond 30 days; deletions recorded as tombstones); the privacy policy gives no fixed periods ('as long as necessary'). No public product-level ZDR; Enterprise admins can allow-list models by provider data-retention policy. Default storage and processing in the US; EU tenants can enforce EU-inference-only; data residency and CMEK are Enterprise-only on the pricing page, and BYOK is documented in the Enterprise admin guide. DPA and subprocessor list on request only. Telemetry goes to an Augment analytics endpoint; the terms exclude customer code from usage data; no telemetry opt-out was found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a paid plan (no training under the commercial terms) and request a DPA. Use .augmentignore to keep personal-data files out of the stored index; it is documented as an indexing exclusion only, and the IntelliJ and VS Code changelogs (Sep 14) show the agent can still read such files after user approval, so keep personal data out of the workspace and do not store it in Cosmos Files. Prefer Enterprise for an EU tenant with EU-inference-only and model allow-listing by retention policy. Re-check terms and the DPA counterparty after the Harness transfer.
suitability_notes.special: Inference and the Context Engine run in Augment's cloud. final_records.model_backend: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Moonshot, NVIDIA, Azure OpenAI, Requesty, OpenRouter (100+ models); ChatGPT Plus/Pro and SuperGrok subscription sign-in; gptme.ai managed gateway; local/self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama-cpp-python); third-party provider plugins
final_records.data_handling_note: Local route: the MIT client runs tools with the user's permissions and saves every conversation, including tool calls, in local logs (~/.local/share/gptme/logs). With a local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama in local-only mode, LM Studio, vLLM), inference stays on the machine. Optional OpenTelemetry tracing is off by default (GPTME_TELEMETRY_ENABLED default false). Offline use needs a pre-cached tiktoken tokenizer, because gptme may otherwise fetch it. Cloud routes send prompts and any file content the agent reads to the chosen provider. OpenRouter requests default to data_collection='deny', which restricts routing to endpoints OpenRouter classifies as non-training but does not prove deletion: require OpenRouter ZDR when retention matters. ChatGPT Plus/Pro and SuperGrok subscription routes fall under those consumer plans' terms (not reviewed here). gptme.ai managed service (beta) has a provisional privacy policy (v0.1.4, updated 2026-10-02) naming Superuser Labs Lund AB as data controller. It states no training on instance content; instance data is kept while the instance exists and deleted 30 days after deletion; LLM request metadata (no prompt or completion content) is kept 1–90 days (default 90) and server logs 90 days. Conversation content is sent to third-party model providers: the policy lists OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter, and the ToS adds OpenRouter sub-providers and Google. Hosting uses Google Cloud GKE and Supabase in the EU, but the policy says some infrastructure and processors operate outside the EU (SCCs or comparable safeguards). Web analytics and error reporting via PostHog (EU). No DPA was located.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model and controlled execution. gptme.ai now has provisional privacy terms, which name Superuser Labs Lund AB as data controller, and no DPA/processor agreement was found; do not use it, or ChatGPT/SuperGrok consumer-subscription routes, for personal data.

final_records.deployment: local-capable / optional hosted inference
final_records.model_backend: Rust terminal agent forked from OpenAI's Codex. Built-in providers are OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock and local Ollama/LM Studio; a generated catalogue adds hosted providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, Z.ai, Qwen, Groq), and custom Responses, Chat Completions or Anthropic Messages endpoints can be added. final_records.data_handling_note: Route-dependent. Local Ollama/LM Studio providers keep model traffic on the machine (for Ollama only in local-only mode, because a signed-in Ollama server can also serve ':cloud' models through localhost); own API keys send content directly to that provider under its terms; Open Interpreter-hosted models pass through its servers, which log full prompts, responses, attachments and metadata for up to 30 days (privacy policy updated 14 July 2026; no training by Open Interpreter; US hosting possible). Sessions, logs and file-stored credentials are kept locally under ~/.openinterpreter; history.persistence="none" stops only the global prompt-history file (history.jsonl), and session records are still written (exec --ephemeral skips them for non-interactive runs). Source code (not the docs) shows analytics on by default: OTEL usage metrics to a Codex-inherited Statsig endpoint and, when signed in (all events with ChatGPT sign-in, plugin events only with API-key auth), events to an Open Interpreter endpoint; [analytics] enabled=false turns both off. Web search, MCP, memories and tools are separate data paths.

Do not use Kilo Desktop (beta) on this route: its local model server requires a Kilo account, its licence is unconfirmed, and first use binds existing users to the 30 Sep 2026 Terms

Set the webfetch and websearch tool permissions to deny in kilo.jsonc (the default is ask), review or disable MCP servers, and keep no cloud provider API keys in kilo.jsonc, the environment or .env files
Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions, including any project-level kilo.jsonc (project root or .kilo/), which takes precedence over global configuration
Manage client updates centrally (for example, disable VS Code extension auto-update) and re-check model roles, telemetry and tool permissions after each upgrade

Restrict MCP servers, web search and other tool egress with institutional network controls; block host egress except to the local model endpoint and verify it with egress monitoring before processing special-category data
Obtain written confirmation from Kilo/Anaconda that the Terms' prohibition on providing regulated sensitive data does not apply to fully local use of the MIT client, or written permission
residual_risks: The install flow prompts for a Kilo account. The docs say logging out of Kilo Gateway ensures no Gateway inference but do not say the clients never require an account. Kilo Desktop's local model server requires a Kilo account and Anaconda Desktop requires an Anaconda sign-in

If small_model is left unset while signed in, background tasks (session titles, commit messages, prompt enhancement) silently use Kilo Gateway's kilo-auto/small; autocomplete defaults to the Kilo provider
Telemetry is on by default. Per the public source code it sends usage events to PostHog's US endpoint, aliased to the account email when signed in, and the payload is only partly documented
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local
A misconfiguration (Ollama Cloud, a Gateway model, or no configured model, where Kilo's model precedence ends at Auto Free) moves prompts and code to hosted providers

Ownership moved to Anaconda and the Terms were updated on 30 Sep 2026 (binding existing users by 30 Oct 2026 at the latest); the Terms do not say whether they govern fully local use of the MIT client. Re-check terms and defaults on each upgrade
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls

final_records.name: Google Colab (Data Science Agent)
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Google-hosted Gemini models. The BigQuery Data Science Agent guide (last updated 2026-10-08) lets users choose a model and names the default as "Gemini 3.0 Flash"; the Colab Enterprise guide and the consumer Colab FAQ name no model. Treat the model as Google-managed and subject to change.
final_records.data_handling_note: Colab Enterprise: Google states that Gemini does not use prompts or responses to train its models, and handles prompts under the Google Cloud terms and Cloud Data Processing Addendum; the Cloud Service Specific Terms also bar training on Customer Data without the customer's permission. Data Science Agent session data, such as conversation history, is stored at rest; the Colab Enterprise CMEK page says it is encrypted with the default runtime template's CMEK key, but the BigQuery Data Science Agent guide says CMEK is not supported. No retention period and no agent-specific zero-data-retention option are documented. Google does not guarantee that Data Science Agent requests are processed in the notebook's region. Consumer Colab (free or paid): Google collects prompts, related code, outputs, feature usage and feedback to improve products and machine-learning technologies; human reviewers may read them; data is stored so it cannot be linked to the user, deletion requests can then no longer be fulfilled, and it is kept up to 18 months; Google asks users not to include sensitive or personal information.

suitability_notes.personal: Use only Colab Enterprise in a Google Cloud project under an accepted Cloud DPA, with institutional review of region, VPC Service Controls and CMEK. Gemini processing may happen outside the notebook region, so check transfer terms. Consumer Colab AI is not suitable, including paid Colab or Google AI plans and Workspace accounts, where Colab is administered as an additional Google service.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. Do not use for special-category data under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule.

compliance: Google Cloud controls only where the exact Colab Enterprise service, region, and contract are in scope
Colab Enterprise documents VPC Service Controls and CMEK support for the Data Science Agent; the BigQuery Data Science Agent guide lists CMEK as unsupported, so confirm for the access path used
final_records.pricing: Colab Enterprise: the Colab pricing page lists Data Science Agent usage at USD 3 per million input tokens and USD 20 per million output tokens, billed on top of runtime compute (list prices checked 2026-10-10). Other Gemini in Colab Enterprise assistance is "currently available to try at no additional cost". Consumer Colab: free tier plus Colab Pro, Pro+ and Pay As You Go at country-specific prices on the sign-up page; eligible paid Google AI plans also add Colab compute benefits.
final_records.academic: No academic privacy tier was confirmed. Colab Pro for Education (free one-year Pro for US university students and faculty) is closed to new sign-ups; educational use does not change data-handling terms.
use_cases: Automated EDA (exploratory data analysis) from natural language prompts
Agent-planned Python notebook code for data cleaning, visualisation and predictive modelling
Statistical analysis and feature engineering
BigQuery-scale data processing with BigQuery DataFrames and BigQuery ML (Colab Enterprise)
Distributed processing with PySpark via Managed Service for Apache Spark (Apache Spark 4.0 code only)
Chart generation (histograms, box plots, scatter plots, bar charts)
Natural-language analysis of data (consumer: uploaded CSV, TSV, JSON or Excel files; Enterprise: uploaded CSV files or BigQuery tables)
Generated code kept in notebook cells for review and re-running
Model training and evaluation within notebook environment
final_records.notes: Cloud notebook agent; generally available in Colab Enterprise since 26 May 2026 and enabled by default for eligible consumer Colab users (aged 18+ and in a supported locale). Google now documents Colab Enterprise as part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI). Consumer and Enterprise data terms differ substantially. Google's own docs disagree on CMEK for the agent (Colab Enterprise guide and CMEK page: supported; BigQuery guide: not supported). Avoid fixed model identities and broad GCP certifications without product, region and contract scope.
final_records.tier_gate: Colab Enterprise + Cloud DPA/governance for personal data

residual_risks: Cloud-only. Do not use for special-category data under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule.
Agent inference runs on Google-hosted Gemini; Google does not guarantee that Data Science Agent requests are processed in the notebook's region.
Agent session data such as conversation history is stored at rest by Google; no retention period is documented.
CMEK support for the agent is contested between Google's Colab Enterprise and BigQuery guides; VPC Service Controls and CMEK are Google Cloud controls, not a customer-controlled inference boundary.

final_records.name: Deepnote
final_records.deployment: Multi-tenant cloud (US, us-east-1) / Enterprise single-tenant (Deepnote-managed, or in the customer's own AWS, GCP or Azure account) or on-premise; no air-gapped option. Open-source VS Code extension, CLI and toolkit run notebooks locally.
final_records.model_backend: Native OpenAI and Anthropic models (user-selectable or Automatic). Enterprise adds OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints for Agent, block edits and prompt suggestions, plus EU-hosted OpenAI via Azure Sweden Central. Code completions use a separate Deepnote completions provider. The open-source CLI agent block calls a user-configured OpenAI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama and LiteLLM documented) and defaults to OpenAI when no provider or endpoint is set.
final_records.data_handling_note: Deepnote states AI-processed content is not used for model training and that its provider agreements prohibit training. The AI privacy page says AI context can be processed in the US and worldwide, allows provider safety retention (OpenAI up to 30 days) and cites zero-retention only for some real-time code suggestions; the security overview separately states ZDR for Anthropic. Product-level retention of prompts, agent history and AI-action logs is not published. The security overview also states that an encrypted temporary copy of workspace data can be stored on other compute providers' machines, with AWS used for long-term storage. Sharing block outputs (which can include row-level data) with the LLM is a separate switch, and admins can disable Deepnote AI. The terms let Deepnote use usage statistics (not Customer Data) to improve the product. Enterprise custom endpoints cover Agent, edits and suggestions but not code completions.

suitability_notes.personal: The default multi-tenant cloud runs in the US (us-east-1, per the June 2025 deployment whitepaper), and Deepnote states AI context can be processed in the US and worldwide, with provider safety retention. Use an Enterprise agreement/DPA with single-tenant EU residency (EU-hosted OpenAI covers only OpenAI-model inference), or a customer-operated deployment with a controlled endpoint. Configure code completions and block-output sharing separately.
suitability_notes.special: Only a customer-managed Enterprise deployment (own cloud account or on-premise) with a customer-controlled model endpoint that serves only institution-hosted models can qualify. Disable code completions and block-output sharing, block native AI providers at egress, restrict external MCP access and the Agent's MCP integrations, configure any CLI agent block explicitly, review every integration and obtain institutional approval. Deepnote Cloud and Deepnote-hosted single-tenant deployments do not qualify.

compliance: Deepnote states SOC 2 Type II; pricing lists HIPAA compliance on Enterprise, and the acceptable use policy permits PHI only under a signed BAA. Exact deployment and signed DPA/BAA scope must be confirmed.
final_records.pricing: Free (3 editors, 5 projects, limited AI), Team and Enterprise (custom) are listed. Team is displayed at $39/editor/month billed yearly and includes $39 of AI credits plus CPU and GPU compute credits per month; the billing docs say AI use beyond a plan's quota is billed pay-as-you-go, while the Enterprise card lists Unlimited AI. Additional machines are pay-as-you-go on Team and Enterprise; Enterprise pricing and deployment terms are by quote.
final_records.academic: Free Education plan for students, teachers and researchers verified by school email (an Education workspace can invite educators and students). The education overview and FAQ exclude Deepnote AI, scheduling and advanced machines and limit the plan to learning and teaching; the verification page's 'all Deepnote features' wording conflicts. No institution-wide academic entitlement found.
use_cases: Collaborative data science notebooks (Python, R, SQL)
AI-assisted data analysis and code generation (Deepnote Agent, which absorbed Auto AI in October 2026)
Data team workflows with real-time multiplayer editing
Database querying and exploration (100+ native integrations)
Scheduled notebook execution and background jobs
Deploying data apps and running notebooks programmatically via the Deepnote API
Version-controlled notebooks with YAML format (.deepnote) for git workflows
Local notebook development with the VS Code extension (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity)
Connecting external coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to a workspace via Deepnote MCP or the open-source CLI
final_records.notes: Cloud collaborative notebook with Enterprise customer-managed or on-premise deployment; Deepnote states no air-gapped option. The open-source CLI (v0.9, under active development) can run an agent block locally against a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but it defaults to OpenAI unless configured, is headless and is not a complete local AI product; a local 'Singleplayer' app is announced as coming soon. Licence scope: Apache-2.0 covers the open-source .deepnote format, CLI, MCP and toolkit packages; the VS Code extension is MIT-licensed; Deepnote Cloud and the Enterprise platform are proprietary.
final_records.tier_gate: Enterprise for custom AI endpoints, single-tenant/customer-cloud/on-premise deployment and HIPAA/BAA; special data only with a customer-managed deployment plus a customer-controlled model endpoint

required_controls: Enterprise deployment in the institution's own cloud account or on-premise (not Deepnote-hosted single-tenant)

Customer-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint set as workspace default for Agent, edits and suggestions; the endpoint serves only models hosted on institution-controlled hardware and forwards nothing to external providers (verify with egress monitoring)
Code completions disabled
Native OpenAI/Anthropic providers blocked at network egress and the block tested; per-user model selection confirmed with Deepnote
Block-output sharing disabled
External MCP client access disabled or limited to approved clients; the Agent's connected MCP integrations and any other external tools limited to approved services inside the institutional boundary

If the open-source CLI agent block is used, set its provider, model and institution-controlled endpoint explicitly (it defaults to OpenAI) and keep no OpenAI or Anthropic API keys in the environment or .env files
Deepnote's automated updates and any maintenance access managed under institutional change control, with the effective configuration re-verified after each update
All integrations, telemetry settings and subprocessors reviewed
DPO or data-steward approval before use
residual_risks: Deepnote Cloud and Deepnote-hosted single-tenant deployments do not qualify.

No documented admin switch removes native providers from the Agent model selector, and the custom-models doc says users can switch back to OpenAI or Anthropic from the dropdown; misconfiguration can send notebook content to OpenAI or Anthropic.
Deepnote states it does not support air-gapped deployments; updates, collaboration and remote support need network connectivity, and maintenance access may be requested.

Customer-cloud ownership, automated updates and maintenance access are described in a deployment whitepaper created in June 2025 that the current enterprise page still links; confirm current terms with Deepnote.

The open-source CLI agent block defaults to OpenAI, and unreleased changes on main move self-hosted endpoints to a separate openai-compatible provider and add an Anthropic provider, so its configuration must be re-checked at each CLI update.
Deepnote does not guarantee Agent quality on custom models; local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Databricks Genie Code
final_records.deployment: cloud (Databricks workspace); the Genie Code CLI (Beta) runs in a local terminal, but its model inference goes through Databricks Unity Gateway
final_records.model_backend: Databricks-selected models. With the partner-powered AI features setting on (default for non-CSP workspaces), Agent mode uses Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI on Databricks and Anthropic on Databricks (Databricks states the Anthropic endpoints are hosted by Databricks within its security perimeter), and other Genie Code chat uses Azure OpenAI Service and OpenAI on Databricks. With it off (default for CSP workspaces), Genie Code runs on a Databricks-hosted open model without agentic capabilities; in CSP workspaces this fallback exists only under the HIPAA, FedRAMP Moderate (US), PCI-DSS or HITRUST (US/ANZ) standards. Autocomplete always uses a Databricks-hosted model. Since 2026-09-08 the setting can no longer be switched off in the settings UI, but the Settings API can still change it until 2026-11-01. On that date the toggle is removed and existing values persist; after that, changes go through the Databricks account team. The CLI (Beta) uses a Databricks-selected model via Unity Gateway.
final_records.data_handling_note: Databricks states it does not use prompts, responses or submitted data to train generative foundation models it makes available to third parties; partner-powered features use partner zero-data-retention endpoints. Product-level retention remains: Genie Code chat history is stored with notebook content (small notebook results default to the Databricks control plane), Genie Code saves automatic cross-session memory, and Agent mode sends data samples and cell outputs to the model. Provider ZDR is therefore not end-to-end deletion. These commitments are stated for the workspace AI assistive features; the Genie Code CLI (Beta) sends prompts and local file content as Unity Gateway model usage, and the trust page does not separately document how that traffic is handled.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional Databricks agreement on a full (non-Free-Edition) account in a suitable Geo (EU workspaces use a Europe-based model for AI assistive features; keep cross-Geo processing off unless approved), narrow Unity Catalog permissions, the 'Ask first' approval mode, no scheduled tasks on personal data (they always auto-approve), and defined retention for notebooks, chats and memory. Not on Free Edition, which has no compliance enforcement, SSO or security customisation. Model-provider ZDR is not notebook/chat deletion.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.

compliance: Contract-, cloud-, region-, and compliance-profile dependent; verify exact Databricks service scope
HIPAA requires the compliance security profile and an active BAA with Databricks; Genie Code and Genie Code Agent Mode are listed in the HIPAA regional feature-support table (AWS)
Designated Service under Databricks Geos: content is processed in the workspace Geo unless cross-Geo processing is enabled
final_records.pricing: Pay-as-you-go since 2026-07-08. Each user (service principals excluded) gets 150 DBUs of free Genie LLM usage per month; Genie compute (e.g. SQL Serverless) is billed separately. Usage above the allowance is billed in DBUs under the Serverless Real-Time Inference SKU; the pricing page's example is 150 DBUs = $10.50 in US East, and the dollar equivalent varies by region. A 25% promotional discount applies to billed Genie usage until 2027-01-31. Genie Code CLI (Beta) is billed as Unity Gateway model usage, not under Genie pricing.
final_records.academic: No research discount or trial-credit amount is asserted. Databricks Free Edition (no cost, quota-limited, non-commercial) includes Genie Code but lacks compliance enforcement, SSO and security customisation, so it suits learning with non-sensitive data only. Institutional programmes require current vendor confirmation.
use_cases: Autonomous multi-step data pipeline engineering (Lakeflow)
Exploratory data analysis and model training in notebooks
AI/BI dashboard generation and analysis
SQL query building and optimization in SQL Editor
Agentic debugging of pipeline failures and errors
Scheduled autonomous data operations (overnight jobs, pipeline summarization)
GenAI application debugging and evaluation in MLflow
Document processing pipelines (parse, classify, extract) from unstructured files
final_records.notes: Cloud data-platform agent in the Databricks workspace (notebooks, SQL editor, Lakeflow, dashboards, MLflow). Chat history and notebook/control-plane content are kept separately from partner-model retention; automatic cross-session memory is also kept by Databricks (storage location and retention period not documented; users can ask Genie Code to forget or delete memories). Agent mode reads data samples and cell outputs and, on first use, defaults to classifier-based auto-approve, which Databricks says is not a security boundary; scheduled tasks always auto-approve. It can also reach MCP servers, native SaaS connectors and (Beta, admin-enabled) web search. For research data, set 'Ask first' and scope permissions narrowly. Genie Code CLI (Beta, Databricks License) adds a local terminal client with cloud inference.
final_records.tier_gate: Full (non-Free-Edition) Databricks account under an appropriate contract; Agent mode needs partner-powered AI features and a supported Geo; regulated data needs the compliance security profile (plus an active BAA for PHI) and workspace governance

residual_risks: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.
Genie Code CLI (Beta) runs locally, but prompts and any file content it reads are processed by Databricks-hosted inference via Unity Gateway; it is not a local-inference route.

final_records.name: Posit AI Pass / Posit Assistant
final_records.deployment: Hosted model service (Posit AI Pass) used from a local client in RStudio, Positron or the pa terminal; local-capable with Ollama/LM Studio; self-managed Posit Workbench with Preview admin provider controls
final_records.model_backend: Posit AI Pass: Anthropic Claude models (ZDR agreement) plus open-weights GLM and Kimi models served through Baseten; Next Edit Suggestions use Posit-hosted models. The lineup changes (Gemma 4 26B retired September 2026); the in-app model picker is authoritative. Own-provider routes include Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry and others (some Preview); local Ollama and LM Studio; custom OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic endpoints are Preview.
final_records.data_handling_note: Posit AI Pass: training on user Content is opt-in at sign-up (Help Improve Posit AI). Opt-in trace data may be used for up to 5 years to train models and improve the service. Opted-out accounts: Posit keeps basic operational data, excluding prompts and responses, for 30 days and does not use it for training or improvement (FAQ). The Service Terms (1 Oct 2026) state that Posit will use Content to provide, maintain, develop, train and improve Posit AI; their Opting Out clause limits training of Posit's models to accounts that opt in. First-party pages disagree on ZDR scope. The FAQ, models page and Responsible Use Policy say every AI Pass model is covered (Anthropic for Claude; Baseten for GLM/Kimi). The Service Terms say some, not all, models, and the product page says select models. NES runs on Posit-hosted models. Provider ZDR does not remove Posit's own retention. With own-provider or local Ollama/LM Studio routes, Positron documentation states that Posit receives no AI traffic, and the chosen provider's terms apply.

suitability_notes.personal: AI Pass route: leave trace collection off and review the click-through Service Terms (no AI Pass DPA found). The FAQ and the Service Terms disagree on ZDR scope. Alternatively, use an institution-approved provider agreement or a local model.
suitability_notes.special: Only Posit Assistant with an Ollama (in local-only mode) or LM Studio model server on institution-controlled hardware qualifies; on Workbench, enforce it with ai-providers-enforced. Cloud providers do not qualify, including Workbench managed-credential routes (Amazon Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex, Microsoft Foundry). Posit AI Pass, NES, web search and remote MCP servers must be off. The AI Pass Service Terms prohibit health data.

compliance: Posit AI Pass Service Terms and Responsible Use Policy (both 1 Oct 2026) prohibit inputting health information, financial information, government ID numbers or other highly sensitive data.

ZDR scope conflict: the FAQ, models page and Responsible Use Policy say every AI Pass model is covered; the Service Terms say some, not all, and the product page says select models. NES runs on Posit-hosted models under Posit's own retention terms.

AI Pass uses individual click-through terms (Massachusetts law; separate EU consumer terms); no DPA for AI Pass was found on fetched first-party pages. Posit's GDPR page offers a DPA on request for Posit Cloud Services (posit.cloud, shinyapps.io); whether it covers AI Pass is unconfirmed.
Workbench Posit Assistant and its admin provider/settings controls are Preview; Posit describes these controls as best-effort policy, not a security boundary.
final_records.pricing: Posit AI Pass Pro: $20/month including $15 of monthly Posit Assistant credits (no rollover) and unlimited NES; credit usage is charged at a 10% premium over model-provider rates. The free trial ended in September 2026; eligible new subscribers pay $5 for the first month, and a payment card is required. Extra credits: one-time purchases of $20-$250, or opt-in auto-recharge with an optional monthly cap of $15-$500; purchased credits expire after 12 months and need an active subscription. Own-provider or local use: the provider is paid directly; no separate Posit Assistant fee is stated on fetched pages. Workbench licensing is separate.
final_records.academic: The FAQ states there is no education discount at this time; Posit says it is exploring options for the academic community. Check institutional Workbench terms separately.
use_cases: R and Python code writing and debugging in RStudio and Positron
Exploratory data analysis with live session context (data frames, variables, plots)
Shiny and Streamlit app scaffolding and Quarto reports (/report)
Next Edit Suggestions inline completions (Posit AI Pass only)
Multi-step agentic tasks with Plan Mode, permissions and skills
Codebase understanding and refactoring
Terminal and headless use via the pa client
Local-model analysis via Ollama or LM Studio when data must stay on controlled infrastructure
final_records.notes: Posit Assistant is Posit's proprietary data-science agent for RStudio (2026.04+), Positron and the pa terminal client.
