residual_risks: Cloud-only: inference always runs on Snowflake GPUs or on cloud-provider model endpoints (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP), none of which the institution controls. Contractual no-training and no-persistence statements do not make it suitable for special-category data under this catalog's rule.

final_records.name: Notebook Intelligence
final_records.vendor: Plmbr GitHub organization (maintainer Mehmet Bektaş); community open-source project
final_records.deployment: local-capable / self-hosted JupyterLab or JupyterHub extension; cloud provider dependent
final_records.model_backend: Provider-dependent. Default mode supports four providers: GitHub Copilot; OpenAI- or LiteLLM-compatible endpoints, cloud or self-hosted (e.g. vLLM/TGI); and Ollama, local or on a host set through OLLAMA_HOST at server launch. Claude mode uses the Claude Code CLI for chat and the Anthropic API (or a configured Base URL) for inline chat and auto-complete. An experimental ACP mode, off by default, runs OpenAI Codex as its only agent type. Launcher tiles open the Claude Code, opencode, Pi, GitHub Copilot CLI or Codex CLIs in a terminal when they are installed.
final_records.data_handling_note: NBI runs inside the user's Jupyter Server and has no central server of its own. It documents no external telemetry: its in-process usage events go nowhere unless an administrator registers a listener. Prompts, surrounding cell source and attached files go to the configured provider. Saved cell outputs are sent when a notebook or cell is attached or read. Ollama keeps inference on the configured host. Claude mode is available to users by default (user-choice) and sends data to Anthropic through the Claude Code CLI outside NBI's provider list; ACP mode is off by default. Launcher tiles run agent CLIs directly in a terminal. API keys are stored in plaintext in ~/.jupyter/nbi/config.json. A remembered Copilot token is encrypted with a shared default password unless one is set.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local Ollama or an institution-operated endpoint, or a cloud provider route covered by an approved DPA or no-training agreement. On shared hubs, pin the provider and set Claude mode by admin policy. Clear sensitive cell outputs before attaching notebooks, and protect the plaintext key file.
suitability_notes.special: Only with the admin-guide HIPAA/sensitive-data preset applied in full, plus extra controls. The preset disables the Copilot, OpenAI-compatible and LiteLLM-compatible providers with environment re-enabling blocked, forces Claude and ACP modes off, disables the command-execute and file-edit tools, and serves Ollama on hardware the institution controls. In addition, hide all coding-agent launcher tiles, remove agent CLIs from the image, block egress to external LLM hosts, GitHub and npm, and pin the NBI version. A self-hosted vLLM/TGI route keeps the OpenAI-compatible provider enabled, and its Base URL is not documented as admin-lockable, so network egress control must enforce it. A LiteLLM proxy that forwards to cloud models does not qualify. The developer calls the preset a starting point, not a HIPAA certification, and it is not institutional approval.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free and open source (GPL-3.0); provider charges, where applicable, are paid directly to the chosen provider.
final_records.academic: free
use_cases: AI chat, inline edit and autocomplete in JupyterLab notebooks
Agent mode that edits, runs and fixes notebook cells
Chatbook natural-language notebook cells
Claude Code sessions inside JupyterLab; experimental Codex via ACP
Administrator-pinned providers, models and feature policies on managed JupyterHub
Local-model notebook assistance with Ollama for sensitive datasets
final_records.notes: JupyterLab extension with its own agent mode, admin policy controls, optional Claude Code mode and experimental ACP (Codex) mode. The repository moved to the plmbr GitHub organization. Agent modes and launcher tiles bypass the provider list unless they are separately disabled, so the sensitive-data preset must be applied as a whole and enforced with network egress controls.
final_records.tier_gate: Regulated data only with the documented local-only preset (cloud providers, Claude mode and ACP mode forced off), coding-agent launcher tiles and CLIs removed, egress blocked, and Ollama or an egress-enforced self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure

required_controls: Apply the admin-guide HIPAA/sensitive-data preset in full. Set disabled_providers to github-copilot, openai-compatible and litellm-compatible with allow_enabling_providers_with_env=False. Disable nbi-command-execute and nbi-file-edit with allow_enabling_tools_with_env=False. Set claude_mode_policy and acp_mode_policy to force-off.

Serve models from Ollama on institution-controlled hardware (OLLAMA_HOST set at server launch). If a vLLM/TGI endpoint is used through the OpenAI-compatible provider instead, enforce its Base URL with network egress control, since that field is not documented as admin-lockable. Do not use LiteLLM proxies that forward to cloud models.

Hide all coding-agent launcher tiles with disabled_coding_agent_launchers (claude-code, opencode, pi, github-copilot-cli, codex) and remove those CLIs from the image or PATH, because the tiles are independent of claude_mode_policy and the CLIs stay usable from a terminal.

Block egress to external LLM hosts, github.com, codeload.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com and registry.npmjs.org at the network layer. Pre-install MCP servers and host skills manifests internally. Pin the NBI version and review the changelog before upgrades. Protect the ~/.jupyter/nbi/ secrets.
residual_risks: Claude mode (user-choice by default) and ACP mode reach their own backends outside NBI's provider list. Agent-CLI launcher tiles and the Jupyter terminal are separate surfaces, so disabling providers alone does not make a deployment local-only.
NBI has no provider allowlist mode, so a new built-in provider added in a minor release would auto-enable unless the version is pinned. User config overrides base config for endpoint fields.

Saved cell outputs are sent when notebooks or cells are attached, and API keys are stored in plaintext. Local sessions, staged uploads, logs and tool actions need institutional access, retention and egress controls. The developer describes the preset as a starting point, not a HIPAA compliance certification.

final_records.name: MLJAR Studio
final_records.deployment: local desktop app (Windows, macOS incl. Apple Silicon, Linux via Ubuntu .deb) with local Python execution; AI via hosted MLJAR AI by default, or with the perpetual licence via BYOK cloud providers or local/self-managed model servers
final_records.model_backend: Hosted MLJAR AI by default (underlying model providers not disclosed); with the perpetual licence: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud, or local/self-managed servers (Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM, llama.cpp, custom OpenAI-compatible)
final_records.data_handling_note: Notebook code and Python run locally. MLJAR AI, a hosted service, is the default LLM provider; its underlying model providers, prompt retention and processing location are not published. The AI policy points to the Privacy Policy for MLJAR AI details, but that policy covers the mljar.com website and accounts and has no MLJAR AI retention or provider terms. The AI policy also states that by default no data is transmitted externally, which conflicts with the hosted default in the provider docs and with the home-page claim that data stays on the computer. MLJAR states it does not train its own models on customer data unless agreed, and does not control how external providers train. With own keys, prompts go to that provider under its terms. A local model keeps prompts on the machine. DataFrame enrichment sends each unique cell value of the chosen column to the provider Studio selects. First launch needs sign-in or licence activation, and AI Provider Settings run a licence access check. Desktop-app telemetry and offline operation are not documented.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local or institution-operated model endpoint (perpetual licence required), or an own-key provider covered by an approved DPA/no-training agreement. The default hosted MLJAR AI route has no published retention, subprocessor or DPA terms.
suitability_notes.special: Only with the perpetual licence and a local or institution-operated model server on controlled hardware. Leave MLJAR AI, OpenAI, OpenRouter and Ollama Cloud unused, along with conversation publishing, MLJAR-hosted Mercury deployment and cloud database connections. Verify at the network layer that chat, AutoLab, Workflows and enrichment requests reach only that endpoint, and that sign-in, licence and update traffic carries no data.

final_records.pricing: Pricing page on 2026-10-10: Free $0 (50 prompts/month), Pro $20/month (500 prompts), Business $60/month (2,000 prompts); perpetual licence $199 one-time with one year of updates, required for Ollama/local servers and own provider keys. EULA: perpetual licence covers 1 user and 3 devices; newer releases after the update period need a renewal. The MLJAR AI docs describe extra hosted usage as an add-on that requires the perpetual licence, which differs from the pricing page; verify at purchase.

use_cases: Natural-language exploratory analysis of CSV/Excel data with generated, inspectable Python code
AutoML and AI-run AutoLab experiments on tabular research data
AI-assisted notebooks with local Python execution and whole-notebook AI edits
Local-model data analysis via Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM or llama.cpp for private datasets

final_records.name: JASP

final_records.model_backend: Bring-your-own key/endpoint. Shipped presets in v0.98.1: OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Xiaomi, xAI (all cloud). Custom Provider accepts any OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint; release notes list local models as supported
final_records.data_handling_note: JASP runs no AI service of its own; data handling follows the configured endpoint. The AI is off until enabled; the enable dialog states that information from the data set, analyses, output and chat messages may be processed by the AI service and warns against sensitive or restricted data. Tool calls return dataset metadata (file path, column names and types, row counts) and analysis results. All shipped presets are cloud providers, and JASP's own blog recommends free API tiers while noting that free use means paying with your data. JASP's privacy policy (2018, no AI mention) says the software collects no user data but states it does not apply to the software itself. Update checks are opt-in. The full AI request body is written to the JASP log, which persists only if logging to file is enabled.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-approved paid provider under a DPA/no-training agreement, or a local/institution-operated endpoint via Custom Provider. Do not use free API tiers, which may use submitted data.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a Custom Provider pointing to a local or institution-operated OpenAI-compatible model server, no cloud preset key stored, and network egress verified. The local route rests on one release-note line and the Custom Provider endpoint field; there is no dedicated setup guide and the pull request lists only cloud providers as tested.

final_records.pricing: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0). The AI assistant needs a user-provided API key/model, so provider costs or free-tier data terms apply. Teams and institutions can contact JASP Services B.V. for professional support (no prices published).

final_records.name: IBM Bob
final_records.deployment: IBM-hosted SaaS on IBM Cloud (US East, Frankfurt or Tokyo region) / Enterprise self-hosted backend on customer-managed Red Hat OpenShift, including disconnected (air-gapped) clusters
final_records.model_backend: SaaS: IBM selects the model automatically per task; users and organisations cannot choose or restrict models, and the FAQ does not name providers. Self-hosted: exactly one customer-provided core model through the Model Gateway, either a self-hosted open-weight model from IBM's supported list (at review: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, Poolside Laguna S 2.1; Mistral Medium 3.5 only with the IBM Z package) or a frontier model via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Azure OpenAI; openai/gpt-oss-20b is the documented guardrail model for air-gapped deployments.
final_records.data_handling_note: SaaS (IBM Cloud): the FAQ says prompts, code and responses are held only in temporary memory for the interaction, are never written to persistent storage and are not used to train models; IBM calls this 'effectively zero-retention' and points to the IBM Bob Service Description (not reviewed) for contractual terms. The data-residency page says conversation data stays in the selected region (US East, Frankfurt or Tokyo) and expires at session end; account, admin, billing and user-management data are kept in US East regardless of region. Client telemetry (actions, features, errors; IBM says no code or prompts) is on by default and can be switched off; Enterprise Bobalytics needs it on. Bob keeps completed tasks for 14 days by default (configurable in Settings). Self-hosted (Enterprise entitlement): the backend runs on the customer's OpenShift cluster; inference runs wherever the single configured core model is served, on premises for the supported open-weight models or at AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Azure OpenAI in hybrid configurations. IBM's install guide lists telemetry as disabled for air-gapped installs and on by default (can be disabled) for connected installs. Usage metering reports only the active-user count (automatic 24-hourly upload when connected, manual upload when air-gapped).

suitability_notes.personal: SaaS only under an accepted institutional agreement and the IBM DPA: no training and in-memory payload handling are documented, but account, admin and billing data stay in US East whatever region is chosen. The self-hosted route is preferable.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Enterprise self-hosted deployment on institution-operated OpenShift, installed by the air-gapped method (on-premises inference only, telemetry disabled per IBM's install guide) with a supported open-weight core model and the gpt-oss-20b guardrail served on premises. Hybrid/frontier-model configurations and SaaS do not qualify.

compliance: IBM's Bob FAQ states 'IBM is ISO 27001 certified' at company level; penetration-test summaries and ISO 27001 certificates for Bob are offered under NDA. Bob-specific certification scope and audit reports not reviewed
final_records.pricing: SaaS: 30-day free trial (50 Bobcoins, no payment); Pro $20/month (50 Bobcoins), Pro+ $60/month (180), Ultra $200/month (1000); 1 Bobcoin = $0.50; prices indicative, vary by country, exclude taxes; opt-in overage. Enterprise (team admin, Bobalytics, on-premises/air-gapped deployment) via sales; self-hosted needs a self-hosted entitlement and its price is not published. Premium Packages (e.g. Java Modernization $20/month) cost extra.
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme listed on the pricing page.

The Bob backend runs on customer-managed OpenShift 4.20-4.22 (amd64); model serving is sized separately, and IBM's recommended vLLM settings for the 550B Nemotron 3 Ultra come from H200 testing at tensor-parallel size 8. This first self-hosted release has no in-place upgrades, no Admin UI activity logs and no Bobalytics. Product focus is enterprise software delivery and modernization, so research use needs an institutional platform team. The public IBM/ibm-bob GitHub repository carries an Apache-2.0 licence but holds only a README and the issue tracker; the product itself is proprietary.

Configure the single core model as a supported open-weight model served on premises (e.g. Red Hat OpenShift AI or vLLM) plus the gpt-oss-20b guardrail; configure no hybrid or frontier model endpoint.

First self-hosted GA release: no in-place upgrades and no Admin UI activity logs; security logging is the customer's responsibility at OpenShift level.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Coder Agents

Retention defaults keep chats indefinitely: auto-archive is off by default, and only archived conversations are purged (default 30 days after archiving; turning retention off keeps them indefinitely). Chat debug logging (full LLM requests and responses) is off by default; if enabled, debug data is kept 30 days by default. Deployment telemetry to Coder is on by default and, per the source code, includes per-chat metadata (IDs, status, message and token counts, configured provider and model names) but not message content, plus the administrator email; CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false turns it off. Licences with usage publishing send hourly Agent Time totals (licence JWT and deployment ID, no chat data) to Coder's Tallyman server, shared with Metronome; air-gapped customers must arrange an alternative with Coder.

suitability_notes.personal: Self-hosted deployment with either a self-hosted model endpoint or a provider covered by an institutional agreement/DPA; disable BYOK where personal keys are not allowed, and set retention and telemetry.
suitability_notes.special: Only with control plane, PostgreSQL and workspaces on institution infrastructure, a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model as the only enabled provider, BYOK disabled, telemetry and update checks off, debug logging off, retention/auto-archive set, and all egress (workspace templates, MCP servers, provider-native web search, STUN/DERP, usage reporting) controlled.

The pricing page lists up to 5 active Coder Agents for Community and Premium and unlimited for AI Premium; the Agents docs instead say a Premium licence with Agent Hours has no concurrency cap until the purchased hard limit is reached. Infrastructure and model costs are separate.

Ltd., Singapore, last update 2025-04-30) lists training among uses with no training-specific opt-out stated; terms for platform.kimi.com keys were not assessed. Which policy governs global-region logins (kimi login --region global) is not established. No DPA found. CLI: anonymous telemetry on by default, with or without sign-in (telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to disable); per source code it sends device ID, model, session ID, crash and API-error events with paths, emails, URLs and tokens scrubbed, to a Kimi collector (default mainland-cn region profile); the opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0 (2026-09-04). Auto-update on by default; signed-in users' web fetches use the managed Kimi fetch service unless an endpoint is set; /feedback can attach diagnostic logs and codebase context; Remote Control (paid membership, signed in) relays sessions through Kimi's relay. final_records.name: Deep Agents Code
final_records.deployment: local Python CLI (dcode) that runs a local LangGraph dev server on localhost; tools run locally or in optional remote sandboxes; inference via the chosen provider, including local Ollama
final_records.model_backend: Any LangChain-compatible chat model. OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini integrations are included by default. Extras include Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Groq, Fireworks, Hugging Face, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter and LiteLLM, among others. Also local Ollama, OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints (configurable base_url), and ChatGPT sign-in (openai_codex).
final_records.data_handling_note: BYOK: no dcode-hosted inference service is documented, so provider terms govern inference. If no model is set, startup falls back to an OPENAI, ANTHROPIC or GOOGLE key found in the environment. LangSmith tracing is off unless a LangSmith key is stored via /auth or the shell already sets LANGSMITH_TRACING=true with a key. It sends agent operations and tool calls to LangSmith. --no-tracing or DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LANGSMITH_TRACING=false disables it. Default-on network calls: a PyPI update check and auto-install at session start, and an hourly pricing-catalog refresh from raw.githubusercontent.com. Also, on each launch, langgraph-cli sends a usage ping (OS, OS version, Python and CLI version, command name, anonymised flags) to a Supabase endpoint unless LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. The dcode docs do not mention this ping. Optional cloud services: Tavily web search, remote sandboxes, MCP servers. Sessions, history and credentials live under ~/.deepagents. Offloaded conversation archives are deleted after 30 days by default.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local Ollama, an institution-hosted endpoint, or a cloud provider under an institutional agreement. Pin allowed models (managed [models].allowed). Keep LangSmith tracing off unless LangSmith itself is approved. Set LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. Control remote sandboxes, Tavily web search and MCP servers.
suitability_notes.special: Only with local Ollama (or an institution-hosted endpoint inside the controlled network) enforced by a managed model allowlist. Also required: tracing disabled, LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1, update checks and pricing refresh disabled, no remote sandboxes, no web-search key, and egress limited to the local endpoint.

compliance: The MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification. LangSmith tracing, Tavily web search and remote sandboxes are separate services with their own terms.

final_records.data_handling_note: The Harness privacy policy (last update 2026-09-20) separates official model services from custom model services. Its privacy value is local, Excel-faithful .xlsx recalculation, which does not change the inference boundary. (c) Exact model/telemetry boundary: NOT MET. The nobie.com homepage and privacy policy are byte-identical to 11 Sep 2026 (sha256 a70bc0ac... and 7d905cc8...). The homepage is a logo-only teaser (og image 'og-teaser-20260827'). The privacy policy (last updated 9 Jan 2025) describes a 'web application-based data modeling software platform' at nobie.app, names PostHog and Sentry for activity data, excludes data processed on a customer's behalf, and says nothing about the desktop app/CLI, workbook content, telemetry defaults or opt-out. The installer fetches the app from an update feed (updates.prod.nobie.com); no telemetry statement. README 'Documentation' link nobie.com/cli returns 404. Maintenance signal: docs-only repo (no source), last commit 19 Aug 2026 (LICENSE.md), no GitHub releases; two user bug reports open since 24 Aug with no maintainer reply. Lead only, UNVERIFIED: a search snippet from a third-party aggregator cites a July 2026 Show HN in which the company says it does not collect or transmit user data; not restated on any first-party page I could fetch. retained_reviews.appraisal: Status, licence and classification are unchanged since September. Gemini CLI is still an active Apache-2.0 client: stable v0.60 to v0.63 shipped between 15 Sep and 6 Oct. Since 18 June 2026 it is supported only through the paid Gemini API, Vertex AI (now Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) and Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise. The record's privacy and pricing links pointed to a frozen google-gemini.github.io copy that has no retirement banner and still describes the retired free tiers. They now point to the current geminicli.com docs. The data-handling note now records the retention that differs by route: abuse-monitoring logs on the paid Gemini API, zero data retention by exception on Agent Platform, and Code Assist being stateless. It also records two points researchers must configure on the personal-data route: the built-in web search tool uses Grounding with Google Search, whose logs cannot be disabled, and anonymous usage statistics are on by default.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: The CLI is an Apache-2.0 client; data handling follows the backend route. The supported routes (paid Gemini API, Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise) do not use prompts or code for training by default. Retention differs by route. On the paid Gemini API, prompts and responses are logged for a limited period for abuse monitoring, and Google points users who need guaranteed ZDR to Vertex. Agent Platform allows ZDR if you request an abuse-monitoring exception; it also keeps a 24-hour in-memory cache, which can be disabled per project. Code Assist Standard/Enterprise is stateless and does not store prompts or responses. The CLI's built-in google_web_search tool uses Grounding with Google Search, whose logs cannot be disabled: 30 days on the Gemini API, up to 3 days on Agent Platform. Unpaid use is no longer a supported Gemini CLI route. If an API key without an active billing account still works, the unpaid terms let Google use content to improve products, except in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, where the paid-service data-use terms also cover unpaid quota. Anonymous usage statistics are on by default and do not include prompt content, per the docs; turn them off with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false. Free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended on 2026-06-18.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: All retention claims check out against first-party pages: paid-API abuse logging, the Vertex ZDR pointer, the Agent Platform exception, the 24 h cache that can be disabled, Code Assist being stateless, grounding at 30 d and 3 d, and usage statistics defaulting to on. One sentence is wrong for the catalog's European audience. The Gemini API terms say the paid-service data-use terms also apply to unpaid quota in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, so the unqualified 'unpaid terms → product-improvement use' is wrong there. proposed_changes.old: Aider documents opt-in anonymous analytics excluding code, chat and API keys. A local model can keep inference on controlled infrastructure; cloud APIs use their own terms. proposed_changes.new: With a local model (e.g. Ollama) inference stays on controlled infrastructure; with a cloud API, prompts and code go to that provider under its terms. retained_reviews.appraisal: There has been no rename, licence change or contract change since September. GitHub's Customer Terms log shows no updates after June 2026, and the training split is confirmed: Business and Enterprise data is not used for training, while individual Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max data is used unless the user opts out. Max is now named explicitly in GitHub's training-policy page. This review is the first to appraise GitHub's documented Copilot CLI offline mode (COPILOT_OFFLINE=true with a local BYOK model). In that mode the CLI makes no requests to GitHub and disables telemetry, so under the catalog rule special-category suitability moves from no to cfg for that one route only. Every other surface and every GitHub-hosted model stays unsuitable. The record now also gives retention by surface: IDE prompts are not retained; GitHub.com, Mobile and CLI prompts are kept 28 days; cloud-agent logs cannot be deleted; and GitHub has announced account-lifetime retention for GitHub.com chat. It adds the Claude Fable 5/5.1 retention exception. It also corrects residency pricing: the cost is a flat 10% increase in AI-credit consumption, and the feature requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: cfg
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: I could not refute it. GitHub documents a Copilot CLI offline mode that contacts no GitHub servers, sends requests only to the configured BYOK provider and fully disables telemetry. GitHub says it is designed for isolated environments with a local or on-premises model. This meets the catalog rule as documented, and it matches the precedent for other commercial CLIs with a local-endpoint route (rca-jetbrains-junie, rca-grok-build). It applies only to the CLI offline route. The 7 Oct 2026 changelog repeats that offline mode is an explicit opt-in, and that choosing a local model alone does not disable telemetry.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: If you set the COPILOT_OFFLINE environment variable to true, Copilot CLI runs without contacting GitHub's servers. ... The CLI only makes network requests to your configured BYOK provider. Telemetry is fully disabled. (section 'Offline mode')

required_controls: Use Copilot CLI with COPILOT_OFFLINE=true and COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL pointing to a model served on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware (for example Ollama, vLLM or Foundry Local). Use no GitHub-hosted models.

Enforce offline mode and the provider endpoint in a managed environment, and block egress to GitHub and all other external hosts at the network level. Confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.

Disable CLI auto-update (COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false or --no-auto-update; the autoUpdate setting defaults to true and downloads CLI and first-party plugin updates at session start). Install and update a pinned CLI version through an institution-controlled channel.

Enable local sandboxing (off by default) with network access denied or limited to the local model endpoint. Use no remote MCP servers (they are never sandboxed), and restrict local MCP servers and web tools.
Do not use /delegate, cloud agent, remote control, session sync or remote export, GitHub.com, the Copilot app or IDE extensions for special-category data.
residual_risks: The CLI is proprietary and closed-source (GitHub Copilot CLI License). Its offline-mode network behaviour is documented by GitHub but cannot be audited independently, and this review did not test it.

COPILOT_OFFLINE is documented only in two how-to pages and the 7 Oct 2026 changelog. It is not listed in the environment-variable table of the CLI command reference, and the offline-mode pages do not mention auto-update or plugin-marketplace updates specifically.

Without COPILOT_OFFLINE=true, GitHub documents that telemetry is still sent even with a local BYOK model and no GitHub sign-in. Discovering or choosing a local Ollama model with /model does not turn on offline mode.

Local sandboxing is off by default and is lightweight OS-level isolation, not a VM or container. The CLI's built-in file tools run in-process outside the OS sandbox and follow the sandbox policy only on a best-effort basis. Unsandboxed agent commands can reach any network the machine can reach.
Copilot CLI keeps full session records under ~/.copilot/session-state and a local SQLite session store. Institutional access, retention and deletion controls are needed.
Capability depends on the local model, which must support tool calling and streaming; GitHub recommends a context window of at least 128k tokens.

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The status, boundary and inference values agree with suitability.special = cfg and with the catalog convention ('local-only' is also used for self-hosted endpoints elsewhere), so they are confirmed. Two gaps needed corrections. First, the CLI has an auto-updater that is on by default (autoUpdate defaults to true) and the offline docs never mention it, so disabling it is added as a control. Second, the sandbox docs say the CLI's built-in file tools run in-process, outside the OS sandbox, and that remote MCP servers are never sandboxed; both are now listed. All other controls and risks were confirmed against the first-party pages.

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Most of the change is supported. 'DPA applies by reference': ToS 4.2. Medical/sensitive-data bar: ToS 4.2 and Enterprise ToS 4.3. ACP carve-out: confirmed. Outposts: inference stays in the cloud. Corrections: (a) the model allowlist is a Teams & Enterprise control (controls reference), not only Enterprise. (b) Advising 'pseudonymize first' right after a medical-data prohibition implies pseudonymized medical data is allowed; the terms bar it regardless. (c) The DPA binds the contracting Customer as controller, and Pro/Max are individual plans, so dropping the organisational element weakens the gate for institutional data. (d) 'Every documented route' is overbroad: Cognition's own blog documents a legacy self-hosted deployment (maintenance mode, closed to new customers). Do not use LocalAgentConfig: despite its name it calls the Gemini API or Gemini Enterprise. Leave GEMINI_API_KEY, vertex=True and Google Cloud credentials unset.

Download and checksum the model checkpoint before isolating the host (litert-lm import pulls about 16.8 GB from Hugging Face). Then block outbound network egress during runs and verify that it stays blocked; the docs state the local route works without an internet connection.

Do not use web or search tools, remote MCP servers, cloud-backed skills (including the Antigravity Science skills), cloud-model subagents, or the documented hybrid pattern that pairs a cloud Gemini planner with local agents.
Leave OpenTelemetry export unset, or point it at an institution-controlled collector. Govern local session state, logs and workspaces.
residual_risks: The SDK depends on a closed compiled runtime binary (localharness). Its network behaviour in local mode is documented only as working without an API key or internet connection, and this was not independently tested.

No SDK-specific terms are published. The Antigravity Additional Terms reserve recording and storing Interactions while the Service runs, and they may apply to SDK use. Egress blocking is the technical control and DPO review is the contractual one.
The SDK changelog (v0.1.8) documents client OS and version information in telemetry headers. Whether the runtime emits any telemetry in local mode is not documented.

The SDK is pre-1.0 and marked Alpha on PyPI. The local route recommends at least 24 GB of VRAM or unified memory and works best with the Gemma 4 26B A4B LiteRT checkpoint, so capability is well below the cloud route.
Antigravity 2.0, the CLI, the standalone IDE and the IDE extensions remain cloud-only.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Since September JetBrains added Junie Lite (2 Oct 2026), a free model tier that runs on JetBrains servers and so is still a vendor cloud route, and Junie Local, an on-device engine for M5 Macs that the docs list for nightly builds. Re-checking the policies also exposed an omission in the record: on non-commercial licenses, common in academia, JetBrains IDEs collect detailed prompt and code data by default for training JetBrains models unless the user opts out. Classifications are unchanged (local; ok/cfg/cfg). The special-category route is still Junie CLI plus a local runtime, now with concrete controls; the IDE plugin cannot use local models.

proposed_changes.old: Junie CLI supports Ollama and custom local endpoints, allowing inference to remain on controlled infrastructure. For JetBrains-hosted/provider routes, detailed code-data sharing is opt-in and disabled by default for commercial organizations; one-year retention applies only after opt-in. BYOK and cloud routes must be assessed separately.
proposed_changes.new: Local route: Junie CLI with Ollama, LM Studio or Junie Local keeps inference on the researcher's hardware; JetBrains states that after the Junie Local model download no prompts, code or diffs are transmitted. Cloud routes (JetBrains AI models, Junie Lite on JetBrains infrastructure, BYOK providers): the JetBrains AI Terms bar training generative models on inputs/outputs without express consent and bind subcontractors to the same, but inputs may be stored for a limited period for abuse monitoring; BYOK traffic follows the provider's own terms. Detailed code-related data collection (full LLM prompts and responses, used to train JetBrains models, kept 1 year) is off by default for commercial individual and organizational licenses and needs explicit consent on free student/classroom/open-source licenses, but is ON by default (opt-out) for non-commercial licenses. EAP and nightly builds fall under the Junie EAP Terms, which let JetBrains store and analyse inputs and outputs for product improvement.
proposed_changes.why: Baseline described detailed data collection only for commercial organizations. Current JetBrains AI FAQ and Product Data Collection notice v1.6 say it is on by default (opt-out) for non-commercial licenses, which is relevant to researchers. retained_reviews.appraisal: Tricentis acquired Tabnine (announced 30 July 2026, missed in September). tabnine.com now redirects to Tricentis, the public pricing page is down, and the public IDE plugins no longer onboard new users, so Tabnine is in effect an Enterprise-only, quote-based product, while docs and private-installation releases stay active (v6.6.9, 8 Oct 2026). The special-category route is still documented (on-premises or own-VPC, air-gapped, self-hosted open-weight models) but needs tighter controls: non-air-gapped self-hosted clusters may send logs and hashed telemetry to Tabnine, private installs can be wired to Tabnine-hosted or third-party cloud inference, and SaaS retains repository indexes. Prices could not be re-confirmed, so the verified date stays 2026-09-11.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Self-hosted Tabby with a local model, or Pochi in BYOK mode with a local model, keeps code and prompts on controlled infrastructure. Pochi BYOK needs no account and stores task history locally by default. Telemetry is on by default: the Tabby server and IDE extensions send non-code usage statistics (server and hardware info, completion counts and latency) under a random ID to app.tabbyml.com, and each can be disabled. retained_reviews.appraisal: No change to Cognition's training, ZDR or privacy terms since September (legal pages last updated Mar-Jul 2026), and the agent brain still always runs in Cognition's cloud, so special-category use stays 'no'. New for researchers: Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams) lets sessions execute on a lab or institutional machine, but inference and planning remain in Devin's cloud. The record now states product-level retention (relationship term; 30-90 days after termination), the DPA's explicit exclusion of special-category data, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 on the Trust Center, and a Teams-pricing conflict between the now-readable pricing page and billing docs.

proposed_changes.new: Cloud. Devin Cloud runs the agent brain and Devbox in Cognition's multi-tenant cloud. Enterprise Customer Dedicated Deployment is a Cognition-hosted single-tenant VPC reached by AWS PrivateLink or IPSec; Enterprise Assured adds customer-managed AWS KMS keys. Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams; off by default on dedicated tenants) executes commands on customer machines while inference and planning stay in Devin's cloud.

Consumer terms and integrated third-party services need separate review; all catalogued AI inference is cloud-based.
proposed_changes.new: Plan-specific. Starter/Core (Terms of Service): Replit's model-improvement page says prompts, instructions, context and generated responses are used to develop and improve its models and AI features; no opt-out is documented for these plans. Pro (Pro Agreement): training on Customer Content is allowed by default; the opt-out in Settings > Personalization applies to new content and deletes nothing. No fixed product retention period is published; Enterprise prompt text is retained and retrievable through the Compliance API; the DPA allows a return or deletion request up to 90 days after termination, except where law requires retention. De-identified Usage Data may be used and shared with third parties. No zero-data-retention commitment was found. All Agent inference runs in Replit-operated cloud with US-based AI subprocessors.

retained_reviews.appraisal: No rename, acquisition, licence or privacy-policy change since 11 Sep 2026: the Agent Canvas core stays MIT, the Cloud privacy policy (effective 3 Sep 2025) still allows training on customer content, and nine releases have shipped since (v1.26.0 on 8 Oct). The update adds what researchers need to lock down the self-hosted route: Agent Canvas sends an anonymous install event before consent unless telemetry is switched off (opt-out added in v1.17.0), and Canvas can route work to third-party ACP agents such as Claude Code or Codex under their own vendors' terms. retained_reviews.appraisal: No new Jupyter AI release since v3.2.0 (3 Sep 2026); subpackages kept shipping (acp-client 0.3.2 on 2 Oct, Jupyternaut 0.1.0 on 21 Sep), licence and privacy policy unchanged. The September record missed a first-party local route: the optional, experimental Jupyternaut persona can call a local Ollama or self-hosted vLLM server, so special-category use no longer depends only on a third-party ACP agent. That route is fragile (docs flagged out of date, future under review), so suitability stays cfg with added controls, including v3.2.0+ for shared servers.

proposed_changes.old: Agent Client Protocol integrations include Claude, Codex, Copilot, Goose, Kilo, Kiro, Mistral Vibe and OpenCode. A customer-controlled inference route requires selecting and configuring a separately reviewed local-capable agent.
proposed_changes.new: No agent ships by default. Built-in ACP personas (jupyter-ai-acp-client 0.3.x): Claude, Codex, Copilot, Goose, Kilo, Kiro, Mistral Vibe and OpenCode, each using its own vendor login and models. The optional, experimental Jupyternaut persona and %%ai magics call models through LiteLLM, with documented local Ollama (default 127.0.0.1:11434) and self-hosted vLLM routes. Customer-controlled inference needs that route or a separately reviewed local-capable ACP agent.
proposed_changes.why: Record omitted the first-party optional Jupyternaut persona and magics, which call models via LiteLLM with documented local Ollama and vLLM routes; built-in ACP persona list re-confirmed in jupyter-ai-acp-client v0.3.2 entry points; getting started states no agent ships by default.

proposed_changes.old: Current Jupyter AI connects coding agents to JupyterLab notebooks through ACP. Notebook context and tool execution follow the selected agent and model provider's policies. A local Jupyter server does not keep data local if its agent uses a cloud model. Project Jupyter's general policy describes telemetry as opt-in and excludes third-party hosted products; it is not a privacy guarantee for connected agents.
proposed_changes.new: Jupyter AI routes notebook context, attachments and tool calls to the selected persona; the ACP agent or Jupyternaut's model provider then applies its own retention and training terms. A local Jupyter server does not keep data local if the persona uses a cloud model. Chats are saved as .chat files in the workspace; Jupyternaut's persistent memory (local SQLite) is opt-in. The ACP client emits operational events to Jupyter Server's EventLogger, which records them only where an operator registers handlers; the code describes them as free of customer content and PII, though failure events carry error messages. Project Jupyter's policy says telemetry is opt-in and does not cover third-party hosted Jupyter.
proposed_changes.why: Added product-level storage (chats as .chat files; opt-in local SQLite memory for Jupyternaut) and the ACP client's EventLogger telemetry, which the September note did not cover.

old.personal: Configure a reviewed ACP agent with institution-controlled inference, or separately approve the complete agent/provider route. Local JupyterLab alone does not keep notebook context local.
old.special: Requires local JupyterLab plus an ACP agent configured for customer-controlled inference, isolated notebook execution and approved integrations; a local notebook UI with a cloud agent does not qualify.

new.personal: Use an institution-controlled model route (Jupyternaut with local Ollama or self-hosted vLLM, or a reviewed ACP agent with such inference), or separately approve the complete agent/provider route. Local JupyterLab alone does not keep notebook context local.
new.special: Requires JupyterLab on institution-controlled infrastructure with local inference (experimental Jupyternaut with local Ollama/vLLM, or a separately reviewed local-capable ACP agent), isolated notebook execution and approved MCP integrations; a local notebook UI with a cloud agent does not qualify.

proposed_changes.why: Name the documented first-party local inference route alongside the ACP-agent route; suitability levels unchanged.

proposed_changes.old: Free and open source (BSD-3-Clause); users pay only any selected cloud-model provider costs
proposed_changes.new: Free and open source (BSD-3-Clause); costs come only from any connected agent subscription or cloud model provider
proposed_changes.why: Several built-in ACP agents (e.g. Copilot, Kiro) are billed through agent subscriptions, not only model providers; no Jupyter AI paid tier exists (BSD-3-Clause).

proposed_changes.old: Notebook integration for separately configured ACP coding agents. A notebook running locally does not determine where the connected agent sends context.
proposed_changes.new: Notebook chat host for separately installed ACP coding agents, plus an optional experimental Jupyternaut persona whose future is under maintainer review (jupyter-ai#1618). Where context goes is set by the connected agent or model provider, whatever runs the notebook. v3.2.0 (3 Sep 2026) made real-time collaboration optional and fixed frontend tool calls running in every connected browser.
proposed_changes.why: Add Jupyternaut status (experimental; future under review in issue #1618) and the v3.2.0 change relevant to shared servers.

required_controls: Run local JupyterLab with a separately reviewed ACP agent configured for institution-controlled inference. Disable cloud providers, external integrations and unnecessary telemetry; isolate notebook execution.
residual_risks: Requires local JupyterLab plus an ACP agent configured for customer-controlled inference, isolated notebook execution and approved integrations; a local notebook UI with a cloud agent does not qualify.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Classification is unchanged: Julius remains a US-hosted cloud workspace with a no-training commitment, so special-category data stays excluded and personal data still needs an executed DPA. The check adds facts the September record lacked: the Terms let Julius use inputs and outputs to improve its AI features, and the public subprocessor list includes an observability service (Raindrop) that receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces. Third-party models come from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Meta and Moonshot AI (the record named only the first two), and first-party sources disagree on paid-plan file retention (7 days of inactivity in the docs, permanent storage on the pricing page). Public prices are unchanged; the help docs and changelog list Ultra and Growth 1-4 tiers that the pricing page does not show.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Hex is unchanged in plans, prices and cloud-only deployment, but its self-serve terms (Community, Professional, Team) let Hex use AI-session inputs and outputs to improve its services unless the workspace opts out; only the Enterprise agreement rules this out. These terms date from May 2026, so moving the record from no-train to opt-out corrects the September classification. Since September Hex added six models to the default picker, including Grok 4.6, whose serving provider and retention terms are not on the subprocessor list, plus a skip-approvals agent mode and MCP project editing. For researchers, personal data needs Team/Enterprise with the DPA, the opt-out set and the provider-retention toggle off; special-category data remains unsuitable.

Only the Enterprise agreement contractually excludes training/improvement. The terms predate September (ToS last modified 2026-05-14), so this corrects the September classification under the conservative rule; it is not a new vendor change.

proposed_changes.old: Hex's LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) operate under zero-data-retention by default, with an admin-controllable exception for models that require safety retention (e.g. Claude Fable 5). Hex itself may use AI-session data for feature improvement unless the organization opts out in workspace settings. Personal-data use requires contractual controls, DPA, and appropriate residency; uploaded/output data still traverses Hex infrastructure. BYOK is Enterprise-only.
proposed_changes.new: Self-serve plans (Community, Professional, Team; ToS last modified 2026-05-14): unless the customer opts out in Settings > AI & agents, Hex may use AI inputs and outputs to develop, improve and evaluate its services. Enterprise agreement (last modified 2026-06-24): neither Hex nor its AI providers use Customer Data to train, improve or develop AI models, except models kept for that customer only. Hex's FAQ adds that staff may review AI prompts and related project data when needed to fix bugs or improve AI features. LLM providers do not train and run under zero data retention by default; an Admin toggle enables models that require provider safety retention (Anthropic: 30 days for Fable 5; Fable 5.1 added 2026-09-23). Product-level storage is separate: prompts carry project code, cell outputs, schema and table/column names; cell outputs are stored indefinitely unless custom retention (7-90 days, select Enterprise plans) is enabled; schema embeddings sit in a vector database on Hex infrastructure. BYOK (Enterprise) reroutes third-party inference only: typeahead still runs on Hex-run models, and Hex-hosted models such as Kimi are unavailable while BYOK is on.
proposed_changes.why: Made tier-specific (self-serve vs Enterprise), added product-level retention (cell outputs stored indefinitely without Enterprise custom retention), staff review of AI inputs/outputs, what goes into prompts, Fable 5 30-day provider retention and Fable 5.1, and BYOK scope limits.

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Personal: the controls named are real, but three points need fixing. (a) The DPA s11.1 relies on Hex's DPF certification and uses SCCs only if the DPF lapses or does not cover the transfer, so 'DPA (SCCs)' is wrong. (b) Recommending the EU stack for residency without saying that Anthropic inference is processed in the USA (subprocessor list) misleads EU researchers. retained_reviews.appraisal: No plan, licence, ownership or policy change since 2026-09-11: the Privacy Policy (2026-06-09), Terms and subprocessor list (2026-03-02) predate the September review; docs edits added Claude Fable 5.1 to the Covered Models list and widened Student-plan model exclusions, and a merged but not yet published docs change removes Zeta edit predictions from the Free plan. The update closes gaps that matter for researchers: Zed defaults route to hosted services (agent model, Zeta edit prediction, telemetry on), hosted summary/commit-message requests can reach cloud providers even when another model is selected, Business controls cover only Zed-hosted services, and the Terms bar HIPAA PHI from the hosted Service. Special-category stays cfg, but only for a signed-out, fully local configuration with every feature model and edit prediction pointed locally.

proposed_changes.old: Zed-hosted models, direct BYOK/subscriptions, external agents, and local Ollama/custom providers are separate request paths.
proposed_changes.new: Separate request paths: Zed-hosted models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google; Pro, Student, Business), provider API keys, existing subscriptions, gateways (e.g. OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vercel), local or self-hosted models (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible servers), External Agents via ACP, and Terminal Threads running agent CLIs. Edit prediction has its own provider setting; the default is Zed-hosted Zeta.
proposed_changes.why: Request paths now named as documented today, including gateways, llama.cpp/LM Studio, Terminal Threads and the separate edit-prediction provider (default hosted Zeta).

proposed_changes.old: Zed does not retain prompts/code context by default; feedback and elective training collection are exceptions. Hosted model-provider agreements prohibit training and normally require ZDR, with safety-retention exceptions for designated Covered Models (currently at least 30 days for Anthropic). BYOK, subscriptions, external agents, gateways and edit prediction are independent request paths. A local model alone does not make external agents or cloud edit prediction local.
proposed_changes.new: Zed does not retain prompts or code context by default; it stores AI data only when a user rates a response or opts into Edit Prediction training data (open-source projects only). Zed-hosted models: provider agreements prohibit training and require ZDR, except provider safety retention for designated Covered Models (Anthropic: at least 30 days); Zed's default settings withhold hosted requests to non-ZDR Anthropic models until the user consents. Zed's subprocessor list states that hosted summarization or commit-message requests may reach Anthropic, Google, OpenAI or xAI even when another model is selected. BYOK, subscriptions, gateways, External Agents, Terminal Threads and third-party edit prediction follow their own terms. Client telemetry (diagnostics, metrics) is on by default and can be disabled; server-side telemetry is collected whenever hosted AI or collaboration is used.
proposed_changes.why: Added three documented egress points the September note lacked: hosted summarization/commit-message routing to providers even when another model is selected, telemetry defaults (client on, server-side with hosted use), and the default consent gate for non-ZDR Anthropic models. Training/ZDR/Covered-Model claims re-confirmed.

old.personal: Use a fully local model, or a provider/DPA configuration accepted by the institution. Hosted models process data outside local infrastructure.
old.special: Requires Ollama or another fully local/self-hosted endpoint on controlled infrastructure. Hosted Zed/provider models are not acceptable.

new.personal: Use a fully local model, or a hosted/BYOK route the institution has approved. A DPA is available on request (Zed acts as processor for Zed Business). Hosted Zed models send prompts and code context to US-hosted providers under no-training/ZDR commitments, with provider safety retention for Covered Models.
new.special: Only the fully local route qualifies: Zed Agent, all feature-specific models and edit prediction on Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or a self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure, signed out of Zed-hosted services, telemetry off. Hosted Zed/provider models are not acceptable; Zed's Terms also bar HIPAA PHI from Customer Data sent to its hosted Service.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Cody remains an active, Enterprise-only assistant (new Cody model support in Sourcegraph 8.0, Sept 2026), but the IDE extensions have not shipped since June 2026. Sourcegraph updated its DPA on 2026-10-05 (explicit retention clause; 60-day instead of 30-day instruction window after expiry); AI conversation history is kept for the subscription term and deleted within 90 days after expiry. For most customers, current AI use is governed by the ToS, not the older Cody or AI terms; the ToS excludes GDPR Art. 9 special-category data even for self-hosted installs. For researchers this confirms Cody is not a route for special-category data; personal data needs the signed DPA and a confirmed model routing.

retained_reviews.appraisal: OpenCode is active and MIT-licensed. OpenCode 2 shipped in September (2.0.26 tagged 8 Oct; the opencode.ai installer now points to v2), and the 1.x line is still maintained (1.18.35, 6 Oct). The record was wrong to say that Go tiers no longer exist: OpenCode Go ($10/month) and Go Plus ($40/month) are documented, with a per-model privacy table. That table shows 30-day retention on the Grok, GPT Luna and Claude Haiku routes, and Meta training on the Muse Spark Contributor models. The Terms also allow use of unpaid-account Content to improve the Services. For researchers, the local-only route is unchanged and is now easier to enforce: v2 built-in Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM discovery, provider deny policies, and managed config. Two new controls are needed: v2 built-in web search (to third-party search APIs) must be disabled, and clients must be patched after a September high-severity local-server advisory.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: The client keeps sessions, logs and credentials on the local machine (~/.local/share/opencode). The vendor states that it does not store code or context data and that prompts go directly to the selected provider. With no OpenCode key set, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models by default (vendor source code), so choose a provider explicitly and block the rest. The hosted routes are not uniformly zero-retention. On Zen, OpenAI and Anthropic requests are retained for 30 days; Mistral and Jev data follow those providers' own retention policies; several free models may use data to improve the model; NVIDIA free endpoints log use; and Muse Spark Contributor trains Meta models. On Go, the Grok, GPT Luna and Claude Haiku routes retain for 30 days, the Muse Spark Contributor models train, and the DeepSeek ZDR agreement is renewed monthly. The Terms allow Content from unpaid accounts on the hosted Services to be used to improve them. V1 session sharing uploads conversations to opencode.ai; V2 has no sharing yet. Both lines can send web searches to third parties (V1 automatically with the OpenCode or Go provider, or with the Exa/Parallel flags; V2 through five search providers or Console-hosted search), and the webfetch tool, allowed by default, can reach any URL. Disable sharing, web search and webfetch for private work, and review every selected provider.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Every retention/training item in the proposal checks out against Zen docs, Go docs and Terms (all HTTP 200, full text, Oct 8 2026 docs). Three corrections: (1) the proposal implies web search is V2-only, but V1 docs say the V1 websearch tool is enabled with the OpenCode/Go provider via a keyless hosted service, so 'disable both' under-covers V1; (2) webfetch (default allow in V1 and V2 permission defaults) is an unmentioned egress path; (3) vendor source at v1.18.35 and v2.0.26 enables the built-in 'opencode' provider with apiKey 'public' and only zero-cost models when no key is set, i.e. hosted free models are the out-of-box route. Also adds omitted Zen exceptions (Mistral, Jev), the time-limited DeepSeek ZDR on Go, and scopes the unpaid-account clause to the hosted Services (Terms carve out self-run open-source software).

Enforce the settings: on V1 through managed config (/etc/opencode, /Library/Application Support/opencode, %ProgramData%\opencode, or a macOS MDM profile). V2 (2.0.26) has no documented system managed config, so pin to 1.x where enforcement is required, or protect the V2 config files with OS controls; Console-delivered policy needs a vendor-cloud connection.

On offline hosts, disable the remote model-catalog fetch, LSP downloads and auto-update (documented V1 flags: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD, autoupdate false; V2: update "disable").
Restrict host network egress to the local model endpoint, because shell commands run with the user's network access.
Keep clients at or above the patched versions; do not expose opencode serve/web or the V2 background service beyond localhost, and set a server password.
residual_risks: Local sessions, logs, credentials (auth.json) and the session database under ~/.local/share/opencode need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

Out of the box, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models, and V2 falls back to the newest available model when the configured one is unavailable; a missing deny rule or a stopped local runtime can route prompts to hosted models, some of which permit data use for improvement or training.
V2 provider policies are experimental, invalid statements are dropped with a warning, and policies do not sandbox plugin code.
V2 has no documented system managed config; users can change their own global config unless OS controls prevent it.
The local HTTP server and web UI have had high or critical advisories (most recently GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4, September 2026); V2 always runs a local background service.
OpenCode 2 is a new major line; V2 equivalents of some V1 egress flags were not verified.
Third-party MCP servers, plugins and LSP servers can send data outside the controlled boundary.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: The CLI keeps sessions, logs (./.crush) and state on the machine, and model prompts go only to the configured provider. Built-in tools can still reach the web from a local-model setup: the sourcegraph tool (enabled by default, no permission prompt) sends model-written search queries to sourcegraph.com; agentic_fetch asks once, then a sub-agent searches DuckDuckGo and fetches pages without further prompts; fetch and download ask per call. Pseudonymous usage metrics (PostHog via data.charm.land; no prompts or responses, but crash and panic error messages are sent) are on by default; disable with CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or `option metrics false`. A Hyper login links the metrics device ID to the Hyper account. At startup Crush queries the GitHub releases API for new versions (no documented opt-out) and, unless provider auto-update or default providers are disabled, refreshes the Catwalk catalog and the Hyper provider definition from hyper.charm.land. Optional Hyper: no training on prompts or outputs; content not stored by default but kept up to 30 days when retained for debugging, abuse prevention or legal compliance; operational usage data 90 days; operated from the US and routed to unnamed third-party model providers. The README and Hyper home page call Hyper zero data retention; the privacy policy's 30-day exception is the operative term. ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot and Grok sign-ins follow those accounts' own terms.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Proposed text says prompts go only to the configured provider 'so a local model keeps them local' and lists only metrics, GitHub update check and Catwalk as egress. All other sentences (PostHog endpoint, opt-outs incl. `option metrics` -> disable_metrics, Alias on Hyper login, unconditional update check, Hyper 30-day/90-day/US/SCC terms, ZDR wording) re-confirmed.

required_controls: Define the local OpenAI-compatible provider and model explicitly in config.toml (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio or Ollama on hardware you control) and check the active model, provider and API base with /status before each session.

Keep no Mistral API key on the machine or in the environment (MISTRAL_API_KEY, OS keyring, ~/.vibe/.env): with a key present the CLI fetches admin-managed config from Mistral at startup, and Teleport and the hosted-default fallback can reach Mistral's cloud.

Set enable_telemetry = false and enable_auto_update = false in a local config the institution controls; do not rely on Mistral admin-managed config, which Mistral describes as a distribution mechanism, not a security control, and which is fetched over HTTP from Mistral.

Disable or vet MCP servers, connectors, skills and web tools that reach external systems; do not use /teleport, '&' prompts or Vibe Code Web; do not trust repository folders that ship their own .vibe/config.toml.
Keep enable_otel off (OpenTelemetry export requires enable_telemetry = true, so it cannot be combined with the telemetry-off route).
Run v2.25.4 or later (MAI-2026-003 shell-permission fixes) inside an isolated workspace with least-privilege credentials; with auto-update off, track Mistral security advisories and update manually.
residual_risks: Since v2.26.1 a stale pin to the removed built-in local model ('local' alias) falls back to the hosted Mistral default with only a warning; if a Mistral API key is present, code and data can go to Mistral's cloud.
Telemetry and auto-update are on by default; a missed setting sends usage/error data or update checks off-host.

Configuration precedence (admin config > CLI flags > env vars > project .vibe/config.toml > user config.toml) means an organization admin config or a trusted repository's config can silently change the active model or provider; admin-managed values show only inside /config.
Shell-permission bypasses disclosed in September 2026 show prompt-injected content can trigger commands; treat the agent as able to read anything the user account can.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Cloud no-training or ZDR is not a substitute: ZDR covers only pay-as-you-go stateless API endpoints, not Vibe Work, Chat or other stateful products; Vibe Code Web retains session activity per plan.

proposed_changes.old: Managed model selection includes Anthropic, OpenAI and supported open-weight models; the available model list and multipliers change. Exact routing and retention depend on the selected model and account path.
proposed_changes.new: Managed cloud catalog; Kiro states it is powered by Amazon Bedrock. Includes Anthropic Claude models (Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 with experimental support), OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, open-weight models (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen) and an Auto router; Claude Fable 5.1 is an Enterprise-only Preview. Per the models page (updated 8 Oct 2026), GPT-5.6 has Global inference scope and uses the US endpoint even for Frankfurt profiles; other models stay in the profile's US or EU geography; Fable 5.1 runs only in us-east-1. AWS GovCloud (US) has a separate catalog. The docs index lists no local or bring-your-own model option. Models and credit multipliers change often.
proposed_changes.why: Added current catalog and per-model inference scope: GPT-5.6 now marked Global scope (Sep 9 page said US-served; experimental models were the only global exception), Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5 added (28 Sep, 2 Oct), Fable 5.1 Enterprise Preview (16 Sep, us-east-1 only); no local/BYO model option in docs index.

proposed_changes.old: Free and individual accounts may contribute content to service improvement/model training unless opted out; paid social-login or Builder ID accounts remain individual accounts. Enterprise content is excluded from service improvement, but may be stored in the configured profile region to operate the service, including prompt logging and daily reports. Cross-region inference and model-specific abuse retention remain separate boundaries. Enterprise telemetry/reporting is administrator-controlled. Local IDE/CLI execution does not make inference local.
proposed_changes.new: Free Tier and individual subscribers (paid via GitHub, Google or AWS Builder ID, including the Students tier) may have content used for service improvement, which Kiro says can include model training, unless they opt out (CLI: turn off Telemetry and 'Share Kiro content with AWS'); their content is stored in us-east-1, and Free Tier inputs may also be kept up to 60 days for abuse detection. Enterprise users (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) are excluded from service improvement and automatically opted out of telemetry/content collection, but content may be stored in the profile Region (US East or Frankfurt) to run the service; admin-enabled prompt logs and daily activity reports go to a customer-chosen S3 bucket in the customer's AWS account. Kiro also collects operational signals (error logs and metrics based on instructions, feedback and responses). Model-specific abuse retention applies to every tier: OpenAI GPT classifier-flagged traffic up to 30 days; all Claude Fable 5.1 Preview traffic up to 30 days, with possible human review of flagged traffic by AWS. GPT-5.6 uses Global cross-region inference (possibly outside the profile geography). Optional --cloud sessions keep conversation history, cloned repositories and sandbox files in an AWS-managed sandbox (us-east-1 only for Identity Center organisations; off for Enterprise until an admin enables it). Running the CLI locally does not make inference local.
proposed_changes.why: Data-protection page revised 17 Sep and 8 Oct 2026: per-user-type storage, enterprise prompt logs/daily reports now stated to go to a customer-selected S3 bucket, new operational-signals collection, Fable 5.1 all-traffic 30-day retention with possible human review, Global inference reframed per model. Added cloud-session storage boundary (CLI --cloud, since CLI 2.17) and Students-tier status.

Own infrastructure for cloud-agent execution does not establish a customer-controlled control plane or inference route. Review the exact plan's content collection and retention settings.
proposed_changes.new: Tier-specific. Business and Enterprise: Warp's privacy docs say these plans are covered by its ZDR agreement and no AI interaction or console data is collected; data collection is off by default and admin-enforceable. Free: telemetry must stay on to use AI features, and Warp's agent FAQ reserves the right to use collected data to train models (the privacy notice, last modified 18 Aug 2026, also lists model training as a purpose). Build/Max: data collection is on by default; users can opt out and keep AI. Provider ZDR covers OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and Fireworks AI, except Claude Fable 5/5.1, which Anthropic retains; Warp documents these as off by default for Enterprise teams. Product-level retention remains: cloud conversations and cloud-agent transcripts, artifacts and attachments sit in Warp-managed storage unless Enterprise maps them to its own S3 bucket; Codebase Context keeps embeddings; telemetry, when collected, is kept indefinitely; shared sessions expire after about one week. Warp's security pages still say telemetry opt-out keeps full functionality, which conflicts with the Free-plan rule on the privacy page.
proposed_changes.why: Adds tier-specific defaults (Free requires telemetry for AI; FAQ reserves right to train on collected data), the Claude Fable ZDR exception, product-level retention, and a first-party docs conflict. Classification stays no-train for the Business/Enterprise route.

retained_reviews.appraisal: On 2026-10-08 Augment and Harness announced that Harness has acquired Cosmos, the Auggie CLI, the Context Engine and related technology, and that Cosmos will become the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent. On 2026-10-10 the service, privacy policy and terms (unchanged since Aug 2025 / Jan 2026) were still Augment Computing, Inc.'s, so the data processor and DPA counterparty for researchers may change soon. Current docs also add detail that September missed: Enterprise BYOK, an EU-inference-only option for EU tenants, model allow-listing by retention policy, and self-hosted Cosmos daemons. The daemons move only tool execution; all LLM calls still go to Augment, so special-category stays 'no'. The Community Terms grant training rights, so the no-train classification holds only for paid plans under the Professional or Enterprise Terms.

retained_reviews.appraisal: There has been no product, licence or documentation change since September: v2.4.6 (2026-07-23) is still the latest release, the docs pages were last edited before 2026-09-11, and the licence is MIT. The record is now more precise in two ways that matter for researchers. First, two documented execution backends run remotely: swerex_modal (Modal cloud) and contree (ConTree cloud containers). They are now excluded from the special-category route, next to cloud models and routers. Second, mini saves the full run history and API keys (.env) locally, and these need institutional controls. Maintenance has slowed: no commits to main between 2026-09-11 and 2026-10-10, about 20 community PRs open, but a maintainer still triaged an issue on 2026-10-05. This is not abandonment, but check the pace again next cycle.

retained_reviews.appraisal: The local route is unchanged: the MIT client runs fully local through Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM, and OpenTelemetry tracing is still off by default. v0.34.0 shipped on 2026-09-18 and dev pre-releases continued to 2026-10-08. The gptme.ai managed service now publishes readable provisional terms (privacy policy v0.1.4 and ToS v0.2.0, both updated 2026-10-02) and a beta price of $10/month. Those terms say no training on instance content, deletion 30 days after an instance is deleted, and inference via OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter. No DPA was found, so the cloud path stays outside personal or special-category use. New subscription routes (ChatGPT Plus/Pro, SuperGrok) and a documented OpenRouter data_collection='deny' default were added. The docs also show that profile 'no network' rules are prompt-level only, which strengthens the egress controls the special route requires.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Local route: the MIT client runs tools with the user's permissions and saves every conversation, including tool calls, in local logs (~/.local/share/gptme/logs). With a local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM), inference stays on the machine. Optional OpenTelemetry tracing is off by default (GPTME_TELEMETRY_ENABLED default false). Offline use needs a pre-cached tiktoken tokenizer, because gptme may otherwise fetch it. Cloud routes send prompts and any file content the agent reads to the chosen provider. OpenRouter requests default to data_collection='deny', which restricts routing to endpoints OpenRouter classifies as non-training but does not prove deletion: require OpenRouter ZDR when retention matters. ChatGPT Plus/Pro and SuperGrok subscription routes fall under those consumer plans' terms (not reviewed here). gptme.ai managed service (beta) has a provisional privacy policy (v0.1.4, updated 2026-10-02) naming Superuser Labs Lund AB as data controller. It states no training on instance content; instance data is kept while the instance exists and deleted 30 days after deletion; LLM request metadata (no prompt or completion content) is kept 1–90 days (default 90) and server logs 90 days. Conversation content is sent to third-party model providers: the policy lists OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter, and the ToS adds OpenRouter sub-providers and Google. Hosting uses Google Cloud GKE and Supabase in the EU, but the policy says some infrastructure and processors operate outside the EU (SCCs or comparable safeguards). Web analytics and error reporting via PostHog (EU). No DPA was located.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Local-route statements all check out. Three gptme.ai statements are incomplete enough to mislead: (1) 'inference via OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter' is the privacy-policy processor table only; ToS §2.3 lists 'OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and its sub-providers, Google, etc.'; (2) 'Supabase (EU)' omits the policy's §8 statement that some infrastructure and processors operate outside the EU; (3) 'request metadata' should be qualified as LLM request metadata without prompt/completion content. Also adds that the policy names Superuser Labs as data controller (relevant to the 'no DPA' point) and PostHog analytics.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Open Interpreter is an actively maintained Apache-2.0 Rust fork of Codex (0.0.56 on 7 Oct 2026). The privacy policy and pricing pages are now readable when rendered: hosted models log full prompts, responses and attachments for up to 30 days (restoring the claim withdrawn in September), and Interpreter Desktop lists Free/$20/$60 plans. Source code shows usage analytics/OTEL metrics enabled by default (disable via [analytics] enabled=false). The September withdrawal of the 30-day claim is reversed with first-party evidence.

required_controls: Run inference only through a local provider (Ollama or LM Studio via --oss) on infrastructure the institution controls; no Open Interpreter-hosted, ChatGPT sign-in or direct cloud-provider route.
Set [analytics] enabled = false (optionally also [otel] metrics_exporter = "none") so usage metrics and analytics events are not exported.
Set web_search = "disabled", keep memories off, and connect only vetted local MCP servers.
Keep sandbox_mode read-only or workspace-write with network off, and enforce host-level egress controls.
Set [history] persistence = "none" or apply institutional retention and access controls to ~/.openinterpreter (sessions, logs, credentials).
residual_risks: Telemetry defaults were established from source code, not documentation; runtime network behaviour was not observed and may change across frequent releases.
Layered configuration (managed, user, trusted project, profile, CLI overrides) can re-enable network access or features; check the effective config with /debug-config.
Local model tool use can fail silently when the server context is too small; the docs warn this is not evidence the requested action happened.

Kilo's Terms of Service, updated 30 September 2026, now make Anaconda, Inc. the contracting party, and trust.kilo.ai now redirects to Anaconda's Trust Center. Kilo Pass prices ($19/$49/$199) are published again, and Kilo Desktop (beta) adds notebooks, conda environments and a local model server that requires Kilo sign-in.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: A fully local route is documented: Ollama/LM Studio/Atomic Chat inference, Ollama embeddings with LanceDB indexing, and local sessions in a local SQLite database. The privacy policy (29 May 2026) says Sentry receives no prompt content. Auto Free may route to providers that log prompts and use them to improve their services. Training and retention otherwise depend on the selected model provider. The Terms bar HIPAA-type regulated data.

retained_reviews.appraisal: No change to classification: Colab Enterprise remains the only personal-data route (Cloud DPA, no training on prompts), consumer Colab AI still collects prompts for product and ML improvement with human review and 18-month retention, and the tool stays cloud-only, so special-category data is not appropriate. The refresh adds facts that matter for EU research data: Google does not guarantee that Data Science Agent requests stay in the notebook region, agent conversation history is stored with no documented retention period, and Google's own docs disagree on CMEK support. It also corrects the model claim (the BigQuery guide documents model choice with a named default), records the published DSA token prices, and replaces the redirected Vertex AI pricing link.
