proposed_changes.new: Google-hosted Gemini models. The BigQuery Data Science Agent guide (last updated 2026-10-08) lets users choose a model and names the default as "Gemini 3.0 Flash"; the Colab Enterprise guide and the consumer Colab FAQ name no model. Treat the model as Google-managed and subject to change.
proposed_changes.why: First-party BigQuery DSA guide documents model choice with a named default; the record said no model was documented. Scoped to that guide because the Colab Enterprise guide and consumer FAQ name no model.

proposed_changes.old: Consumer Colab AI may collect prompts, code, outputs, usage, and feedback for product/model improvement, including human review and retention up to 18 months; Google warns against sensitive/personal data. Colab Enterprise provides contractual Cloud controls but remains cloud-based.
proposed_changes.new: Colab Enterprise: Google states that Gemini does not use prompts or responses to train its models, and handles prompts under the Google Cloud terms and Cloud Data Processing Addendum. Data Science Agent session data, such as conversation history, is stored at rest (CMEK-encryptable through the default runtime template); no retention period and no agent-specific zero-data-retention option are documented. Google does not guarantee that Data Science Agent requests are processed in the notebook's region. Consumer Colab (free or paid): Google collects prompts, related code, outputs, feature usage and feedback to improve products and machine-learning technologies; human reviewers may read them; data is stored so it cannot be linked to the user, deletion requests can then no longer be fulfilled, and it is kept up to 18 months; Google asks users not to include sensitive or personal information.
proposed_changes.why: Adds product-level facts confirmed today: Enterprise DSA stores session data such as conversation history at rest (retention period undocumented), no DSA-specific ZDR is documented, and Gemini requests are not guaranteed to stay in the notebook region. Consumer FAQ terms re-confirmed unchanged.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Classification is unchanged: no-train, with special-category data only via a customer-managed Enterprise deployment that uses a customer-controlled model endpoint. Since September, Deepnote has merged Auto AI into Deepnote Agent and widened API/MCP write and delete tools (9 Oct). Enterprise EU-hosted OpenAI (July) and Agent Workspace (August) predate the last review but were not captured; the Apache-2.0 open-source CLI and toolkit now confirm the licence of the open part. Newly recorded limits matter for researchers: Deepnote-hosted single-tenant is not customer-controlled, no air-gapped option exists, no documented switch removes native providers from the Agent model picker, and the free Education plan excludes Deepnote AI.

proposed_changes.new: Multi-tenant cloud (US, us-east-1) / Enterprise single-tenant (Deepnote-managed, or in the customer's own AWS, GCP or Azure account) or on-premise; no air-gapped option. Open-source VS Code extension, CLI and toolkit run notebooks locally.

proposed_changes.new: Native OpenAI and Anthropic models (user-selectable or Automatic). Enterprise adds OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints for Agent, block edits and prompt suggestions, plus EU-hosted OpenAI via Azure Sweden Central. Code completions use a separate Deepnote completions provider. The open-source CLI agent block calls a user-configured OpenAI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama and LiteLLM documented).
proposed_changes.why: Added Enterprise EU-hosted OpenAI (Azure Sweden Central, changelog 2026-07-16, not captured in September), per-user model selection, the separate completions provider and the open-source CLI agent block's configurable endpoint.

proposed_changes.old: Deepnote states processed AI content is not used for model training. Current AI privacy docs explicitly allow provider safety retention (e.g. up to 30 days for OpenAI); only some real-time suggestions use ZDR agreements. Enterprise custom endpoints can serve agent/chat features, but native completions and block-output sharing require separate controls. Special-category eligibility is conditional on a documented institution-controlled Deepnote deployment and inference endpoint, with all remaining cloud features disabled.
proposed_changes.new: Deepnote states AI-processed content is not used for model training and that its provider agreements prohibit training. The AI privacy page allows provider safety retention (OpenAI up to 30 days) and cites zero-retention only for some real-time code suggestions; the security overview separately states ZDR for Anthropic. Product-level retention of prompts, agent history and AI-action logs is not published. Sharing block outputs (which can include row-level data) with the LLM is a separate switch, and admins can disable Deepnote AI. The terms let Deepnote use usage statistics (not Customer Data) to improve the product. Enterprise custom endpoints cover Agent, edits and suggestions but not code completions.
proposed_changes.why: Security overview states Anthropic ZDR, while the AI privacy page limits zero-retention to some real-time suggestions; recorded both conservatively and added unpublished product-level AI log retention, block-output switch and usage-statistics clause from the terms.

old.special: Only a customer-managed Enterprise deployment with a customer-controlled model endpoint can qualify. new.personal: The default multi-tenant cloud runs in the US (us-east-1) with provider safety retention. Use an Enterprise agreement/DPA with single-tenant EU residency or EU-hosted OpenAI, or a customer-operated deployment with a controlled endpoint. new.special: Only a customer-managed Enterprise deployment (own cloud account or on-premise) with a customer-controlled model endpoint can qualify. Disable code completions and block-output sharing, block native AI providers at egress, restrict external MCP access, review every integration and obtain institutional approval. Deepnote Cloud and Deepnote-hosted single-tenant deployments do not qualify.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Genie Code stays a pure-cloud Databricks agent (special-category data: no). Admins can no longer switch partner-hosted models off in the UI (release note 2026-09-08, missed in September) and the setting disappears on 2026-11-01; a Beta local CLI launched on 2026-10-06, but its inference still runs through Databricks Unity Gateway. Current docs also show Agent mode defaulting to classifier-based auto-approve and keeping automatic cross-session memory, so researchers handling personal data should set 'Ask first', narrow permissions and plan chat/memory retention. Product-level retention remains: Genie Code chat history is stored with notebook content (small notebook results default to the Databricks control plane), Genie Code saves automatic cross-session memory, and Agent mode sends data samples and cell outputs to the model. Provider ZDR is therefore not end-to-end deletion.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Databricks-selected models. With the partner-powered AI features setting on (default for non-CSP workspaces), Agent mode uses Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI on Databricks and Anthropic on Databricks (Anthropic endpoints hosted by Databricks within its security perimeter). With it off (default for CSP workspaces), Genie Code runs on a Databricks-hosted open model without agentic capabilities; in CSP workspaces this fallback exists only under the HIPAA, FedRAMP Moderate (US), PCI-DSS or HITRUST (US/ANZ) standards. Autocomplete always uses a Databricks-hosted model. Since 2026-09-08 the setting can no longer be switched off in the settings UI, but the Settings API can still change it until 2026-11-01. 'Open models' is supported by the trust page, which says Databricks-hosted models are open-source models such as GPT OSS.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: If partner-powered AI features are enabled, the toggle is disabled ... You can still use the Settings API to enable or disable the setting.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Databricks states it does not use prompts, responses or submitted data to train generative foundation models it makes available to third parties; partner-powered features use partner zero-data-retention endpoints. Provider ZDR is therefore not end-to-end deletion. These commitments are stated for the workspace AI assistive features; the Genie Code CLI (Beta) sends prompts and local file content as Unity Gateway model usage, and the trust page does not separately document how that traffic is handled.

retained_reviews.appraisal: The privacy policy and terms are unchanged (both effective 2025-09-17), so the classification stays the same: paid Privacy Mode means no training, Free may train, every AI request goes through Runcell's cloud, and there is no public DPA. The current pricing page now renders. It lists Hobby, Pro, Pro+, Ultra and Teams, so September's 'Hobby and Pro+ no longer appear' was wrong. It also lists Privacy Mode for Pro+ and Ultra, which closes most of September's Ultra gap, although the policy text still names only Pro and Team. New and undocumented: a macOS desktop beta (v0.3.1-0.3.4, Sep 2026), a preview headless agent runtime that calls service.runcell.dev, routing of some models through OpenRouter, and a sign-in 'Cloud Agents' page with a server-side Python workspace. None of these is a controlled-infrastructure route for researchers. Each adds a data path that the privacy policy does not describe.

proposed_changes.old: Plan lineup is now Free, Pro, Ultra, and Team ('Hobby' and 'Pro+' no longer appear). Exact current prices and credit amounts render client-side and could not be extracted on the audit date; treat earlier figures as stale and verify on the pricing page. proposed_changes.new: Rendered pricing page on 2026-10-10: Hobby (free, 20 credits/month, limited model access, no Privacy Mode); Pro $20/month (500 credits); Pro+ $60/month (2,000 credits); Ultra $200/month (10,000 credits); Teams from $40/seat/month (500 credits per seat). The page offers annual billing. Ask/Chat and Agent use token-based credits at 30 credits per USD of provider-equivalent model cost (changed from 100 on 2026-07-15). Other AI features use fixed credit rates. The pricing page lists Privacy Mode on Pro, Pro+ and Ultra; Teams includes 'Everything in Pro'.
proposed_changes.why: The pricing page rendered in a browser today and shows all five plans with prices. September's statement that Hobby and Pro+ had disappeared is not supported. The credit conversion rate comes from the token-credits doc.

proposed_changes.new: Runcell-hosted access only, with no BYO key. The credit table snapshot dated 2026-09-05 lists Claude (Anthropic), GPT (OpenAI) and Gemini (Google) models, plus xAI, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, Xiaomi and Z.ai models; the inventory changes with each release. Requests go through Runcell's cloud orchestrator, and some models go through OpenRouter. Free has limited model access; paid plans unlock advanced models.
proposed_changes.why: The token-based credits doc lists models from many more providers. Release notes state a model is served 'through OpenRouter'. The archived credit table shows openrouter/ model routes. The home-page FAQ confirms there is no BYO key.

proposed_changes.old: cloud
proposed_changes.new: Cloud service used through a JupyterLab 4.4+ extension, installed via pip, conda/uv or the JupyterLab Extension Manager; Docker setups are documented. Notebook code runs in the user's Jupyter kernel, but every AI request goes through Runcell's cloud orchestrator. The privacy policy says offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported. Also available: a macOS desktop beta (v0.3.4, 2026-09-22; data flow not separately documented) and a preview headless agent runtime that calls service.runcell.dev. Self-deployment is only offered as 'contact us'.
proposed_changes.why: The download page payload and the GitHub release metadata show desktop beta builds. The PyPI 0.2.5 README documents the headless runtime and its remote backend URL. The privacy policy states the deployment boundary.

proposed_changes.old: The policy excludes own model training by default on Pro and Team; Free permits training and Ultra coverage is not explicit. Provider no-training instructions apply only where available. Optional cloud sync stores notebooks/chat until deletion; disabling sync does not itself delete earlier history. Local notebook execution still uses cloud model routes. No public institutional DPA was established.
proposed_changes.new: On paid plans Privacy Mode is on by default, so prompts, context and outputs are not used to train or fine-tune models. The policy names Pro and Team; the pricing page also lists Privacy Mode for Pro+ and Ultra. Free (Hobby) has no Privacy Mode, and its inputs/outputs may be used for training. Prompts and selected notebook context go to Runcell's cloud and then to the chosen model provider, in some cases via OpenRouter. Runcell asks providers not to train only where the provider's controls allow it. Optional cloud sync stores conversations until you delete them; turning sync off stops new uploads but does not delete history already synced. The service collects product analytics (Microsoft Clarity) and telemetry without notebook or chat content; no opt-out is documented. Where cross-session Agent Memory is stored is not documented. There is no public DPA or subprocessor list.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Paid plans: Privacy Mode is on by default and Runcell does not use prompts, context or outputs to train or fine-tune models. The policy names Pro and Team; the pricing page also lists Privacy Mode for Pro+ and Ultra. Free (Hobby) has no Privacy Mode, and Runcell may retain and use prompts, context and outputs for training. Prompts, selected notebook context and short interaction history are assembled on Runcell's cloud and sent to the chosen model provider, for some models via OpenRouter. Runcell instructs providers not to train only where their controls allow it, and providers may run abuse/quality checks. No ZDR commitment is stated. Optional chat cloud sync stores conversations server-side; neither its default state nor a retention period is stated. Turning sync off stops new uploads, and previously synced content has to be deleted from the account. Storage of long-running Agent job state and of cross-session Agent Memory is not documented. Product analytics (Microsoft Clarity) and payload-free telemetry exclude notebook and chat content; no opt-out is documented. No public DPA or subprocessor list was found.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The proposal's core is confirmed: Privacy Mode scope, Free training, OpenRouter routing, analytics and the absence of a DPA. Four corrections. (1) 'stores conversations until you delete them' reads as an indefinite-retention promise; the policy gives no retention period and does not say whether sync is on by default. (2) No ZDR commitment and provider abuse/quality checks (policy section 4) were left out; MAINTENANCE.md requires ZDR scope. (3) Free-plan wording should be 'retain and use', per section 4. retained_reviews.appraisal: No rename, licence, plan or price change since September: the MIT runtime is very actively maintained (v0.40.2 on 8 Oct 2026) and Free/Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise tiers are unchanged. The pricing FAQ now names US hosting with possible Europe overflow only (Singapore no longer stated) and says Ollama requires its NVIDIA Cloud Provider partners to keep no-logging, no-training and zero-retention policies. Suitability ratings stay the same, but the special-category route now names the documented local-only switch (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD), the unauthenticated local API and the reserved usage-metadata collection, so researchers know exactly what to configure.

proposed_changes.old: Ollama's privacy policy distinguishes local models, whose prompts it does not receive, from cloud models, which it processes transiently without training. Current pricing says cloud infrastructure is primarily US-based with possible Europe/Singapore routing. Do not assume US-only hosting or infer a DPA/certification from no-training claims. Optional cloud models and agent integrations need their own boundary review.
proposed_changes.new: Ollama's privacy policy (last updated March 2026) says Ollama does not receive prompts or data processed with local models; cloud-model prompts and responses are processed transiently and never used for training. The pricing FAQ says cloud models are hosted primarily in the United States, may be routed to Europe for extra capacity, and are served with NVIDIA Cloud Provider partners that Ollama requires to have no-logging, no-training and zero-retention policies. Limited device and usage metadata is collected. These are vendor statements; no public DPA, trust centre or certification was found. Cloud inference and web search can be switched off (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud).
proposed_changes.why: Pricing FAQ now states US hosting with possible Europe overflow only (Singapore no longer stated) and that cloud partners (NVIDIA Cloud Providers) must have no-logging, no-training and zero-retention policies; local-only switch documented in FAQ; no DPA/trust page found.

Optional cloud inference is a separate US-hosted service under Ollama's terms; local availability is not institutional approval.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Meta's Model API Terms of Service changed on 2026-10-09: a Muse Code subscription is now Contributor (training) by default whatever model is selected, with an opt-out Account setting that applies only going forward, and the terms warn that requests may be routed to a Contributor model. First-party processor terms (MGPT, no training on Standard Services), an open-ended retention clause, a Usage Data/telemetry clause and organisation-level ZDR are now documented, so data_handling moves to opt-out and personal data becomes cfg only through a managed-account organisation key with Meta-enabled ZDR on a pinned Standard model. Subscription prices ($5/$15/$50 per month) are now published. Inference remains Meta-cloud only, so special-category data stays not appropriate.

proposed_changes.old: no-train
proposed_changes.new: opt-out
proposed_changes.why: ToS updated 2026-10-09 adds section 3.3: a Coding Harness (Muse Code) subscription counts as Contributor Services (training) by default regardless of model; Standard requires an Account-setting change, prospective only. The archived 2026-08-28 ToS said the selected model decided content use. Pay-as-you-go Standard models remain no-train; ZDR exists for qualified organisations.

proposed_changes.old: Standard tier: 'your prompts and completions are not used to train Meta models' (first-party pricing docs). The Contributor tier is an opt-in training-for-discount route (roughly 10-20x cheaper in exchange for permission to train on prompts and completions) and must not be selected for any non-public code or data. No retention statement, telemetry statement, DPA, or compliance page was found anywhere in the developer docs at verification, so the retention posture is unverified. Client-side safety defaults are strong: approvals and OS sandboxing on by default, proxy-only network with per-destination approval, workspace-scoped writes.
proposed_changes.new: Terms depend on account route and model tier (Meta Model API Terms of Service, last updated 2026-10-09). Standard models (muse-spark-1.1/1.2/1.3): Meta acts as processor under the Meta Global Processor Terms and does not train on Content. Contributor models (1.2/1.3-contributor) permit training, and the ToS forbids sending personal, sensitive or confidential data (including confidential code) to them. Since the 2026-10-09 ToS, a Muse Code subscription counts as Contributor (training) by default whatever model is selected; Standard terms require changing an Account setting and apply prospectively only. The ToS also warns that the system may route requests to a Contributor model. Without ZDR, Content and Usage Data (which include tool-call sequences, logs and telemetry) are retained 'as needed' with no fixed period, and Content may be used to develop Meta safety and security systems; the Data Commitments page says Content can be viewed and deleted through the account. ZDR exists only for qualified organisations, enabled by Meta through sales; personal accounts are not covered, support may vary by model, and flagged content may still be kept up to 2 years. CLI: settings include telemetry options with undocumented defaults; a local session event log is kept by default (--no-session-log disables it); voice input is on by default on macOS; four background observer agents make extra model calls by default. Client guardrails are on by default: approvals (default Auto-review profile, where an automated judge clears eligible requests), OS sandbox, proxy-only network with per-destination approval, workspace-scoped writes.
proposed_changes.why: Retention (ToS 4.4), Usage Data/telemetry (4.2), processor terms (5.1), routing warning (preamble), ZDR scope (Help Center) and CLI defaults (configuration/interactive/extending docs) are now documented; the September note said no retention, telemetry or DPA statement had been found.

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The proposal's premises are confirmed in first-party sources. ToS 5.1 makes Meta a Processor under the MGPT for Standard Services, with no training on Standard Content. The Help Center confirms organisation-level ZDR enabled by Meta, with personal accounts excluded. auth.md confirms that Business & Enterprise managed accounts must use an API key in Muse Code. Comparable records (Amp, Augment Code) are already cfg when a documented contractual route exists and the institution must confirm DPA and retention terms. cfg is therefore defensible, but only as a gated route. The proposal itself lists as unresolved that ZDR coverage of Muse Code traffic and of Muse Spark models is undocumented ('ZDR support may vary by model'). The routing warning and the opt-out diagnostic upload are residual risks. The MGPT, Data Security Terms and subprocessor list could not be read (facebook.com returned HTTP 400). The suitability_notes must carry these conditions (see correction). If the integration pass wants evidence of ZDR applying to Muse Code before allowing cfg, 'no' would be the conservative fallback.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Ante is still actively maintained: it moved to semver releases (v0.2.0 on 2026-09-17, latest v0.2.9 on 2026-10-05), and the ACP and Slack/Discord gateway apps joined the Apache-2.0 repository. On 2026-09-20 the README dropped its sentence saying the core is developed in a private repository, but the core agent is still not published: it ships only as a prebuilt binary under the unchanged Binary Preview Terms, and the open-sourcing tracking issue is still open. The licence classification therefore stays proprietary/commercial. Since September, WebFetch spill files and staging downloads have moved to the OS cache and temp directories outside ~/.ante (v0.2.0). Antix, the vendor's optional proxy, is documented to record request and response bodies on every call. Gateway mode and /term-driven agents are egress paths outside the offline boundary. The special-data route stays config-required, local-only, with tightened controls; telemetry semantics are unchanged.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Qwen Code remains an active, Apache-2.0 CLI (stable v0.25.0, 2026-10-05) that can run fully against local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio endpoints, so its classification is unchanged. The September gap is closed: docs now state that usage statistics are on by default and go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint, and the source shows the payload includes the configured base URL, so researchers must switch this off explicitly. New opt-in integrations (Browser Use in the signed-in Chrome profile, Channels via messaging apps, Mem0) and Alibaba's Token Plan add egress paths and cost options that the special-data route must exclude.

proposed_changes.old: Docs state Qwen Code itself does not use prompts, code, or responses for model training; training/retention is governed entirely by the chosen backend (API-key mode under the provider's policy, ModelStudio under Alibaba Cloud's privacy policy). Anonymous usage statistics (commands, performance metrics, error reports - documented as excluding code content, prompts, responses, and personal information) may be collected; the default on/off state is not explicitly stated in fetched docs, so assume enabled and disable explicitly in settings.
proposed_changes.new: Docs state Qwen Code itself does not use prompts, code or responses for model training; training and retention follow the configured backend (own API key: that provider's terms; Alibaba Model Studio: Alibaba Cloud terms, whose international privacy page says customer data is never used for training but call data is stored, period not stated). Usage statistics are ON by default (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=true) and are sent to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; docs say they exclude prompts, responses, file content and PII, but the source also sends a pseudonymous installation ID, model name and, for OpenAI-compatible auth, the configured base URL. The ToS page's claim that API-key mode collects no additional data conflicts with this; disable with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false or QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false. OpenTelemetry export is off by default; if enabled, logPrompts defaults to true. Startup update checks and a daily models.dev catalog download are also on by default (both can be switched off).
proposed_changes.why: Settings docs (updated 2026-10-03) now state usage statistics default to enabled and go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; source shows installation ID, model and base URL in the payload; OTel logPrompts default true; update checks and models.dev refresh on by default. Resolves the September 'default not stated' gap.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Docs state Qwen Code itself does not use prompts, code or responses for model training; training and retention follow the configured backend (own API key: that provider's terms; Alibaba Model Studio: Alibaba Cloud terms, whose international privacy page says customer data is never used for training but call data is stored, period not stated). Usage statistics are ON by default (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=true) and are sent to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; docs say they exclude prompts, responses, file content and PII, but the source also sends a pseudonymous installation ID, session ID, OS type/version, CLI version, model name and, for OpenAI-compatible auth (which includes local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio endpoints), the configured base URL. The ToS page's claim that API-key mode collects no additional data conflicts with this; disable with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false or QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false (the environment variable takes precedence). OpenTelemetry export is off by default; if enabled, logPrompts defaults to true. Automatic update checks and installations on startup (general.enableAutoUpdate) and a daily models.dev catalog download are also on by default (both can be switched off).
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Every substantive claim confirmed independently: settings docs (last updated Oct 3, 2026) give privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled default true, QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED 'Defaults to enabled when neither is configured', and the RUM endpoint note; qwen-logger.ts (unchanged since 2026-09-30) sets user id from installationId and adds auth_type, model and base_url (OpenAI auth only) plus session id and os.platform/os.release; core config.ts returns telemetry enabled ?? false and logPrompts ?? true; telemetry docs show the same defaults; ToS (Oct 1, 2026) says 'API Key: No additional data is collected by Qwen Code beyond what your chosen API provider collects'; Alibaba privacy notice (Sep 28, 2026) confirms no-training and stored call data. One correction: general.enableAutoUpdate covers automatic update checks AND installations on startup, not only checks (relevant to upgrade drift and air-gapped hosts). Added the extra payload fields and env-var precedence for completeness; also made explicit that local endpoints use the OpenAI auth type, so their base URL is what gets reported.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Factory announced Factory Private on 18 Sep 2026 (private preview), which runs the control plane in a customer VPC or on-premises, and the docs now give the air-gapped build its own page and network contract. Session retention can now be traced to first-party docs: CLI sessions sync to Factory cloud by default and orgs set retention between 14 and 365 days, so researchers on standard plans should switch sync off. A Factory for Science program now gives researchers and labs free access, but its data terms are unpublished. Suitability ratings stay unchanged; the website moved from factory.ai to factory.com.

proposed_changes.old: First-party security page states customer code is not used as training data; AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, sandboxed single-tenant environments. No session-content retention period is published on fetched pages (the privacy policy covers personal data only, with US processing except the EU deployment option), so retention is treated as unverified. Anthropic Mythos-class models carry 30-day trust-and-safety retention where org admins opt in. Current pricing advertises ZDR on Business and above; the exact session/product retention scope remains a contract question, separate from model inference.
proposed_changes.new: Factory states customer code is not used as training data; individual terms limit internal use of Customer Data to providing the service and producing aggregated de-identified data. Product-level retention: CLI sessions are mirrored to Factory cloud by default (cloudSessionSync true; users can switch it off, org admins can pin it), and synced session history is kept for an org-set 14-365 days; the default period is not published. Factory-hosted operational logs follow gated Trust Center terms. Personal data (privacy policy updated 20 Aug 2026) is primarily stored on AWS US West and deleted no later than 10 years after last use unless contracted otherwise. ZDR is listed for Business and above; its scope relative to session sync is a contract question. Mythos-class Anthropic models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) carry 30-day trust-and-safety retention where org admins opt in. Telemetry: OTEL metrics also reach Factory's collector in connected deployments; message-content spans are off by default and go only to a customer collector. Airgap builds send no runtime data to Factory.
proposed_changes.why: Product-level session retention is now traceable: cloudSessionSync defaults to true and org sessionRetentionDays is 14-365 days. Added privacy-policy personal-data retention (10 years max), telemetry routing, and airgap no-runtime-data statement. Training statement re-confirmed.

old.personal: Use a documented enterprise customer-operated route, or a cloud agreement/DPA with acceptable session retention and model exceptions. Inference-layer ZDR alone is insufficient.

new.personal: Use a Business/Enterprise contract with the DPA (EU SCCs; EU-region deployment for residency on Enterprise), switch off cloud session sync or set a short sessionRetentionDays, restrict models to ZDR-covered endpoints and avoid opt-in Mythos-class retention, and keep message-content telemetry off or on an institutional collector. new.special: Only customer-operated routes qualify: the sales-gated airgap build, a hybrid deployment with in-network models and collectors, or Factory Private (customer VPC/on-prem; private preview). Factory states Airgap Mode is cooperative, so isolation must come from institutional network controls. Managed cloud, Factory-hosted Droid Computers and the public DPA (which lists no special-category data) do not qualify.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: no-train
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Unchanged. The security page still states code is not used as training data. The individual terms let Factory freely use aggregated de-identified data, but they do not mention training, so no-train stands (zdr applies only to Business+).
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: that means not using your code as training data (Security, 'Never misusing your data'; HTTP 200)

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Factory states customer code is not used as training data. Individual terms (14 Jul 2026) let Factory use Customer Data internally to provide the service and to generate aggregated de-identified data, which it may freely use and retain for business purposes including improving its products. Product-level retention: CLI sessions are mirrored to Factory cloud by default (cloudSessionSync true; users can switch it off, org admins can pin it); forked sessions and AutoWiki content (wikiCloudSync, on by default) also sync to Factory cloud. Orgs can turn on auto-deletion of synced sessions after 14-365 days (sessionRetentionDays); no default deletion period is published. Factory-hosted operational logs follow Trust Center terms, which are not publicly readable. Personal data (privacy policy, 20 Aug 2026) is primarily stored on AWS US West and deleted no later than 10 years after last use unless contracted otherwise. ZDR is listed for Business and above; its scope relative to session sync is a contract question. Mythos-class Anthropic models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) carry 30-day trust-and-safety retention where org admins opt in. Telemetry: in connected deployments OTEL metrics (with user, session and repo attributes unless aggregate granularity is pinned) also go to Factory's collector; message-content spans are off by default and go only to a customer collector. Airgap builds send no runtime data to Factory.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Most components verified: cloudSessionSync default true, the 14-365 range, the privacy-policy dates, US West storage, 10-year deletion, the Mythos footnote, metrics fan-out, customer-only spans, and airgap with no runtime data. Three fixes. (1) 'Kept for an org-set 14-365 days' implies a bounded retention always applies, but the changelog describes turning session retention on, the table default is only 'Org default', and auto-deletion policies are opt-in. (2) The terms also allow free use and retention of aggregated de-identified data for product improvement, which 'limit internal use' understates. (3) wikiCloudSync (default true) and forked-session sync are further product-level cloud data paths.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: Turning on or shortening session retention now warns you that existing sessions past the limit are permanently deleted before you save (CLI v0.203.0, 25 Aug 2026)

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Ratings are fine; the routes listed are over-broad. (a) Factory Private is listed as a qualifying route with no inference condition. Its only first-party evidence is a private-preview announcement, which says it 'can keep' model access in the customer environment and also allows frontier models 'through their own providers'. The strict rule requires documented in-boundary inference. (b) The hybrid caveat is softer than the telemetry docs: metrics go to Factory's collector in every connected deployment, and only airgap builds lack that leg. (c) The public DPA annex does not cover research-subject personal data, so 'use the DPA' alone does not establish a personal-data route.

Researchers should note the non-optional daily version check and that paid seats above 10 users need Roomote Cloud licence activation.

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Could not refute. First-party docs establish every leg of an institution-controlled workflow: self-hosting on infrastructure the operator manages, local Docker sandboxes (default for the Linux installer) with a documented egress=none policy, Ollama/vLLM/OpenAI-compatible endpoints explicitly described as running on infrastructure you control, inference proxied by the deployment's own gateway (sandboxes need no direct endpoint access), a local CPU judgment sidecar, and opt-out telemetry. The remaining non-optional outbound calls (daily version check: instance ID + version; licence reporting for >10-user deployments) carry metadata only. The Ollama/vLLM pages exist in the repo since 2026-07-17 (gh commit history of apps/docs/providers/inference/*.mdx), so this is a correction of an over-conservative September call, not a vendor change. Consistent with how the catalog treats self-hosted OpenHands, Cline, Kilo Code etc. Documentation-only; no hands-on test.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: Ollama serves models on infrastructure you control. Use it for local development, private deployments, or workloads where you want to keep inference inside your own network. (Ollama page, intro)

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: status config-required / boundary customer-controlled / inference customer-controlled-endpoint (confirmed). Fix required_controls: (1) replace 'Set DOCKER_WORKER_EGRESS_POLICY=none or restrict sandbox egress to institutional mirrors' with 'Set DOCKER_WORKER_EGRESS_POLICY=none' (the only documented values are internet and none; the default internet policy allows public egress and blackholes private ranges, so an 'institutional mirrors only' setting is not documented); (2) add 'Leave Memory disabled, or run it with local embeddings (COMPOSE_PROFILES=brain,local-inference) and the helper role on the institution endpoint; do not configure OpenRouter/OpenAI R_BRAIN_* keys'; (3) add 'Reach the deployment over the private network only (--tls-mode internal, clients trust Caddy's local CA); do not front it with Cloudflare Tunnel or another third-party tunnel'. Add residual_risks: (a) first-party sources conflict on licensing — docs Users page says paid keys are activated with Roomote Cloud (lease up to 72 h), the operator reference says keys are verified offline and licensed deployments report licence ID and registered-user count to Roomote's Ping service even with analytics off; (b) the operator reference prerequisites still list a stable public HTTPS origin, a required GitHub App and Slack/Teams sign-in, and the docs source-control checklist assumes a public HTTPS URL, so a fully private deployment with self-managed GitLab/Gitea is assembled from several pages, not documented end to end; (c) whether task sandboxes can clone from a private-network GitLab under egress=none is not documented (Gitea clone traffic is documented as routed through a local proxy). Optional mitigation to note: R_PING_BASE_URL (default https://ping.roomote.dev) is documented as configurable, but behaviour when the version check is redirected or blocked is undocumented. All other listed controls and residual risks checked against first-party docs and hold.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Status/boundary/inference agree with special=cfg and with the documented gateway proxying. One required control cites a capability the docs do not provide (egress allow-listing to mirrors); Memory (an optional feature that by default sends embeddings to OpenRouter/OpenAI) is missing from the controls; third-party tunnels (documented in the private-network section) would route traffic through Cloudflare; and the licence/telemetry and private-network prerequisites are contradicted between the docs site and the operator reference.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Clusy is active and its prices are unchanged. The Privacy Policy was re-dated 23 Sep 2026 with only minor edits; the Terms changed without a new date, and Clusy added native R notebooks and a terminal. The record now names routes that were already in the policy but missing here: DeepSeek in mainland China is the default and the fallback whatever model is selected, prompts carry the user's IP address, and the local runner does not keep data off Clusy's cloud. proposed_changes.old: Managed Auto/open-model routes and paid frontier models; BYOK for supported Anthropic/OpenAI accounts and paired Claude/Codex CLI execution are documented. Providers and regions vary.
proposed_changes.new: Plan-gated hosted models from DeepSeek (default Auto; mainland China), Moonshot, Alibaba (Qwen, Singapore), Cloudflare Workers AI (Kimi, GLM), AWS Bedrock (Claude) and Azure OpenAI (GPT); Claude and most GPT models need Max. BYOK for Anthropic/OpenAI keys on any plan; an optional local runner drives the user's own Claude Code/Codex CLI, with inference still at Anthropic/OpenAI. No local or self-hosted model route is documented.
proposed_changes.why: Re-verified provider list; record now names the actual routing (DeepSeek default Auto in mainland China, Moonshot, Alibaba Singapore, Cloudflare, AWS Bedrock, Azure) and states that no local/self-hosted model route exists. Model inventory kept at provider level because the pricing page and docs list different model names.

proposed_changes.old: Clusy now explicitly excludes its own training, fine-tuning and distillation of customer notebooks, prompts, chats and outputs. It does not apply no-training/ZDR controls uniformly across model providers; routing can include the US, mainland China, Singapore and other regions. BYOK uses the user's provider terms while Clusy stores the key encrypted. Notebooks, files, chat and outputs persist until deletion; subagent activity logs retain content for 30 days, and some trace/security records have no defined expiry. Paired-machine execution still uses cloud control/provider services and does not establish local-only inference.
proposed_changes.new: Clusy states it does not train, fine-tune or distil models on customer notebooks, prompts, chat or outputs. It does not send no-training/zero-retention instructions to every provider. Default Auto and inline completion use DeepSeek (mainland China); a turn whose provider fails is retried on DeepSeek whatever model was selected; titles/tags and memory embeddings go to AWS Bedrock. Prompts carry the user's IP address and approximate location. Hosted Fable 5.1 requests may be retained by AWS for up to 30 days for misuse review. BYOK applies the user's provider terms (key stored encrypted). Notebooks, files, chat and outputs persist until deletion; sub-agent logs 30 days; the performance-trace archive and security records have no set expiry. In-app PostHog analytics run by default (exclusion by email request). The local runner is a credential boundary, not a data boundary.
proposed_changes.why: Sharpened with first-party facts present in the policy since at least 4 Sep 2026 but missing from the record: DeepSeek is the default and fallback route regardless of selection, background features use Clusy-chosen providers, IP/location go into prompts, AWS 30-day retention for hosted Fable 5.1, telemetry, and the local runner being a credential (not data) boundary.

(2) Inline completions are on by default but can be switched off, which is a real user control the note omitted. (3) The IP is sent 'where your browser connection has a public IP address' and the user can ask for it not to be sent. retained_reviews.appraisal: DataFoundry's privacy design is unchanged: the install repository's README, licence, architecture and security files are byte-identical to September and suitability stays ok/cfg/cfg, though this review adds two boundaries the record missed (a separate embedding endpoint, example Alibaba DashScope, and an approval-free command sandbox with broad host read access). adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The proposal's core is right: providers/src/index.ts l.60-63 passes baseURL unchanged, and .env.example and quick-start show only DashScope and DeepSeek. Two errors: (1) the blanket 'no first-party local-model example' is wrong, because services/datalink/src/datalink/config.py in the same repository lists a localhost:11434 base_url; (2) it misses that an empty API key silently switches to the mock provider (l.53-57) and that embeddings fail without a key, which matters for keyless local servers.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: if (!config.api_key) { return { kind: "mock", ... } } ... baseURL: config.base_url (l.53-62); DataLink config.py l.16-17: "http://localhost:11434/v1"

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: No DataGallery-operated service: sessions, conversation memory, run events, SQL audit, files and outputs persist in local SQLite/storage paths that need lifecycle controls. Prompts carry schema, SQL results (the compact observation shows the model 20 rows by default, configurable up to 1000), file, command and knowledge excerpts to the configured LLM endpoint; knowledge documents go to the embedding endpoint. Shipped examples point both at Alibaba Cloud DashScope. DataLink (defaults to api.openai.com if no base_url is set) and MCP services are separate processing boundaries. DataFoundry adds no telemetry of its own, but its bundled CopilotKit runtime sends anonymous usage analytics by default (opt out: COPILOTKIT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true or DO_NOT_TRACK=1) and the Next.js build collects anonymous telemetry (NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1); DataFoundry's .env.example sets neither.
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The proposal says 'No telemetry setting or dependency found in the main package manifests'. That is misleading. @copilotkit/runtime is a direct dependency in the root and apps/api package.json; CopilotRuntime is instantiated in apps/api/src/server.ts l.404 with no telemetry option; and CopilotKit's own runtime README and docs say analytics are on unless disabled. The lockfile also pulls @segment/analytics-node and @scarf/scarf through CopilotKit, and posthog-node through @mastra/core 1.46.0. Whether Mastra's PostHog client fires in DataFoundry is not established: its usage-sync caller sits in Mastra's deployer server, which DataFoundry does not use. These runtime sends were not observed, because nothing was run. The '20 rows' figure is the default of sqlMaxModelRows (max 1000) and applies only to the SQL observation; read_file and execute_command output (maxOutputTokens 3000) also reach the model. DataLink defaults: config.py l.30-31 and l.104. data_handling value 'local' unchanged and consistent with peer BYO-endpoint rows.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: With none of these identities, Runtime sends anonymous telemetry. ... Set COPILOTKIT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true in your runtime environment. (CopilotKit Open-source Telemetry page)

The review corrects the record against the project's own privacy page and code: evidence sent to the optional OpenAI layer can carry segment labels such as customer or person names, parsed uploads sit in a process-wide cache for up to an hour, and pinned Streamlit 1.59.2 sends usage statistics by default with no repo override, plus a Google Fonts browser request. proposed_changes.old: The core runs with no LLM at all: the dashboard does not require an API key, execute generated code, or intentionally persist uploaded datasets, and files are processed within the active Streamlit session (project SECURITY.md). With the optional OpenAI layer enabled, only computed schema roles, summaries, evidence, deterministic recommendations, and user-typed context are sent; raw uploaded rows are not included in model prompts and request storage is disabled for model API calls. The project's own security notes warn that the boundary does not turn a public hosted app into an approved environment for regulated data. Streamlit framework-level telemetry defaults are not addressed in the repo (unverified).
proposed_changes.new: Without a key, parsing, cleaning, schema detection, charts, anomaly/forecast and rule-parsed Ask ADA answers are computed in-process with pandas (docs/privacy.md). Uploads stay in memory and are not written to disk; parsed files sit in a server-process cache (at most 8 files, up to 1 hour) that is not tied to the browser session and clears on restart. With the optional OpenAI layer, the planner receives the typed question plus column names, types and roles; the strategic read receives typed context, schema, computed summary, evidence and recommendations. Raw rows are not sent, but evidence sentences can name segment labels (e.g. a customer or product name). Requests set store=False and send a hashed session identifier; OpenAI's API terms still apply (no training by default; abuse-monitoring logs kept up to 30 days unless OpenAI approves ZDR). Pinned Streamlit 1.59.2 sends usage statistics by default (browser.gatherUsageStats = true) and the repo config does not turn this off; the app stylesheet also loads Google Fonts in the browser. The docs' 'no network call' statement therefore holds for ADA's own code, not for these framework/browser requests. SECURITY.md: the no-raw-row boundary does not make a public hosted app an approved environment for regulated data.
proposed_changes.why: Corrected and completed: evidence sent to OpenAI can include segment labels; planner sends the typed question; server-process upload cache (8 files, 1 h); Streamlit telemetry default now verified as on and not overridden in repo config; Google Fonts browser request; OpenAI API retention terms.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Analyst is still active and, under Microsoft's new pricing model from 23-25 Sep 2026, is part of the per-user Copilot licence (USL). Copilot Credits billing covers only Cowork, Code, Autopilot and frontier models. The core privacy commitments have not changed: no training on prompts, responses or Graph data, and retention is in the tenant under Purview. The record now also covers the AI-subprocessor model layer, which matters for personal data: OpenAI-operated models are on by default; Anthropic models are off by default in the EU/UK and sit outside the EU Data Boundary; and admins can opt in to 'Anthropic models with Data Retention', which run outside Microsoft's DPA. A first-party academic price (USD 18/user/month) now replaces the earlier 'unverified' academic note. Special-category suitability stays 'no' because this is a pure Microsoft cloud service.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: Microsoft states Analyst runs inside the Microsoft 365 commercial data processing boundary and inherits Microsoft 365 privacy, security and compliance commitments. Prompts, responses and Microsoft Graph data are not used to train foundation LLMs; interactions are stored encrypted as Copilot activity history in the tenant, governed by Purview retention policies and user deletion. Optional user feedback may be used to improve Copilot (not foundation-model training) and is admin-controllable. Copilot opted out of Azure OpenAI abuse-monitoring human review; Anthropic models carry Anthropic-operated safeguards to detect illegal content. Models are Microsoft-hosted or come from AI subprocessors under Microsoft's DPA: OpenAI-operated models (on by default for eligible commercial tenants since 24 Jul 2026; in the EU Data Boundary with documented exceptions; outside in-country processing commitments; in certain Copilot experiences OpenAI's Responses API is used with ZDR subject to OpenAI's limits) and Anthropic models (on by default for most commercial tenants outside EU/EFTA/UK, off by default inside them; excluded from the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments). Admins can also opt in to 'Anthropic models with Data Retention', processed by Anthropic as an independent processor outside Microsoft's DPA with up to 30-day retention (longer if flagged); the fetched Microsoft docs do not say whether Analyst can use them. LLM calls can route to other regions under high load; EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary (Anthropic models excepted). Python-sandbox data handling is not separately documented (unverified).
adversarial_field_verdicts.why: Every new safety-relevant element checks out against the 2026-09-18 Anthropic page and the 2026-10-09 OpenAI page: the Data Retention opt-in outside the DPA, the 30-day retention, OpenAI on by default since 24 Jul, and the EUDB and in-country exclusions. Four precision gaps: (1) Anthropic is ON by default for most non-EU commercial tenants, while the note says only 'off by default in EU/EFTA/UK'. (2) Anthropic is also excluded from in-country processing. (3) The Responses API ZDR applies to 'certain Copilot experiences', not to all OpenAI-operated calls. (4) The abuse-monitoring opt-out is Azure OpenAI-specific. Attributing the boundary claim to Microsoft is also safer, since subprocessor models are processed by third parties.

Special therefore moves from no to cfg. SaaS and BYOC still do not qualify, because BYOC keeps a Zerve-hosted control plane. Training and retention for managed inference remain undocumented, so data handling stays unknown. The pricing contradictions persist, and a University Partnerships page plus an Education Accounts clause in the Terms now inform the academic field.

required_controls: Run a reviewed source build on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware (an official binary only with Updates Off, accepting its unauditable private components), with inference only through local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) under the same control.
Point the background 'cheap model' (tab naming, reply suggestions, auto-approve reviewer, extension text generation) at the same local model, or switch it off.

Keep the default loopback-only access; never enable the passwordless LAN mode (p or --public) on shared networks; in Docker, where --public is used, publish the port only to localhost or an isolated network; do not use the official binaries' WAN modes.

Set Settings > Updates to Off (default Automatic polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h with version, OS, architecture and an install-count mark; official macOS desktop builds also auto-download updates) or block that egress, and confirm with egress monitoring after each upgrade.

Disable the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch capabilities in Settings > Extensions for every project (stored as plugins.disabled in <project>/.juggler/config.json), or deny the WebSearch and WebFetch tools globally with a beforeTool hook in ~/.juggler/hooks; both run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies.
Block or explicitly accept outbound requests to cdnjs.cloudflare.com: the web UI loads diff_match_patch from it on each page load (allowed by the CSP, no integrity attribute).

Use the Default or Read-only strategy so writes and shell commands need manual approval; do not use YOLO, the Auto-approve reviewer, or `juggler run` without an explicit --strategy (it defaults to yolo); do not use ACP agents (they bypass Juggler's strategies and their permission requests are auto-allowed by default); keep the Exa extension (ships disabled) and remote MCP servers off; install only reviewed extensions.

Apply institutional access, retention and backup controls to <project>/.juggler/, ~/.juggler/credentials.json and the platform log directory, and keep .juggler/ out of shared repositories and sync folders.
residual_risks: No privacy policy, telemetry statement or DPA; the update ping and install counting are described only in source-code comments, and how juggler.studio handles request logs is undocumented.
Young project (repository created June 2026) with one principal maintainer, rapid releases and no LTS; network behaviour can change between versions.
The server binds all interfaces and relies on an application-level LAN gate (403 for non-loopback requests); a host firewall is still advisable.
Shell commands run with the user's full privileges; SECURITY.md states the shell filter is not a security control, and agent tools can read files in the home directory, including stored API keys.
Extensions are unsandboxed JavaScript; their declared permissions are disclosure, not containment.
Built-in web tools are enabled by default and disabled per project; a new project or a new version can re-expose them unless a global hook or network egress control is in place.
The UI runs a third-party script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com without an integrity check, in a page that can approve tool calls (supply-chain exposure).
Official binaries are built from a private repository and may include proprietary components that cannot be audited from the public source.

Vendor docs claim code is never used for training, which contradicts ToS §4.1 for Free accounts; the docs-linked Trust Center is broken, and the working one (trust.forgood.ai) lists the certifications with reports by request. Pricing tiers are Pro/Pro Plus/Pro Max, with private deployment listed under Enterprise.

discovery_decisions.name: Nobie
discovery_decisions.reason: Reconsider condition NOT met (1 of 3 parts met). (a) Current product terms/pricing: MET. First-party Nobie License Agreement v1.0 (6 Jul 2026) makes the desktop app and CLI free for all internal use; fees ($0.50 per end user per month, or per training instance-hour) apply only to companies above US$100M trailing revenue that embed Nobie in external products or train distributed models on it. Optional paid features have separate, unpublished terms. (b) Off-the-shelf agent workflow with distinct researcher need: PARTIAL. The README documents `nobie skill` / script schema for coding agents, but Nobie has no built-in model or agent; whatever reaches an AI model is governed entirely by the external agent the user connects. Its privacy value is local, Excel-faithful .xlsx recalculation, which does not change the inference boundary. (c) Exact model/telemetry boundary: NOT MET. The nobie.com homepage and privacy policy are byte-identical to 11 Sep 2026 (sha256 a70bc0ac... and 7d905cc8...). The homepage is a logo-only teaser (og image 'og-teaser-20260827'). The privacy policy (last updated 9 Jan 2025) describes a 'web application-based data modeling software platform' at nobie.app, names PostHog and Sentry for activity data, excludes data processed on a customer's behalf, and says nothing about the desktop app/CLI, workbook content, telemetry defaults or opt-out. The installer fetches the app from an update feed (updates.prod.nobie.com); no telemetry statement. README 'Documentation' link nobie.com/cli returns 404. Maintenance signal: docs-only repo (no source), last commit 19 Aug 2026 (LICENSE.md), no GitHub releases; two user bug reports open since 24 Aug with no maintainer reply. Lead only, UNVERIFIED: a search snippet from a third-party aggregator cites a July 2026 Show HN in which the company says it does not collect or transmit user data; not restated on any first-party page I could fetch. Why hold, not drop: the record was owner-accepted on 13 Aug and the product looks pre-launch, so a public launch could supply the missing documentation. The scope question (a spreadsheet engine for agents with no AI of its own, in an AI-agents catalog) is the owner's call; my default if nothing changes by the next sweep is drop as out of scope. If the owner restores it before then, use the conservative classification: data_handling unknown; suitability nonsensitive ok, personal no, special no; special_route not-appropriate; openness commercial, license_status proprietary, software_license null.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Restore only when ALL hold: (1) nobie.com publishes product documentation (nobie.com/cli or a successor page resolves); (2) a desktop-app/CLI-specific privacy or telemetry statement covers workbook content, crash/usage telemetry defaults (PostHog/Sentry) and an opt-out; (3) either Nobie ships its own AI/agent feature with a named model provider and data terms, or the owner rules that an agent-facing local spreadsheet engine with no AI of its own is in scope. If nothing changes by the next full sweep (third consecutive hold), drop as out of scope.

discovery_decisions.name: Orion
discovery_decisions.reason: Remaining condition settled against inclusion. Required account: current source labels Orion Cloud sign-in the 'Required first onboarding step' (Google-only OAuth via Supabase; onboarding passes no skip option). Changelog 0.18.0 says 'require Orion Cloud sign-in during setup', and the August 2026 first-session guide tells users to sign in to Orion Cloud to continue setup. Two older first-party texts contradict this and are stale: docs 'Local vs hosted app' (June 2026: 'optional Orion Cloud sign-in') and docs/architecture.md ('no account or hosted backend is required'). Privacy terms: none published. The orion-agent.ai sitemap lists only /, /about and /install. /privacy, /privacy-policy and /terms return 404 on both the site and app.orion-agent.ai. A web search surfaced no policy (lead only). The About page makes local-first/privacy claims, but they are marketing, not terms. Storage/telemetry: chat history (SQLite), settings and provider credentials are local under ~/.orion. Notebooks go to Orion Cloud (Supabase Storage) only on explicit publish. The sign-in dialog says it will 'sync your Orion Cloud work' (scope undocumented). package.json has no analytics SDK (only Supabase), and release CI sets NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, but no telemetry statement is published. Local inference is documented (Ollama, LM Studio, MLX, OpenAI-compatible endpoints). Licence: package.json and PyPI declare Apache-2.0. The LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 text with two parenthetical phrases removed, so GitHub reports NOASSERTION. Fit and maintenance: the website now pitches an 'AI business analyst' for 'non-technical founders' (README and docs still say researchers). Single maintainer (every issue self-filed). Latest release v0.20.2 on 4 Sep 2026 (npm and PyPI agree), with no commits or releases in the 5 weeks since, after a weekly cadence. With a mandatory vendor-cloud account and no privacy terms at all, no local-data recommendation is supportable. The notebook-agent niche is already covered by catalogued tools (Jupyter AI, marimo, Runcell). Dropped from the hold list; not a permanent ban.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Re-enter through discovery only if all of the following hold: released builds make Orion Cloud sign-in optional or removable for local use; a first-party privacy policy/terms covers Orion Cloud accounts, 'sync' and published notebooks, with retention and telemetry stated; maintenance resumes (releases after 2026-09-04); and the product still targets research/data-science users.

issues.problem: HIGH. tier_gate, suitability_notes and special_route list Factory Private (private preview) as a qualifying special-category route. The deployment string also groups the Factory-operated EEA cloud ('EU-region') with hybrid and air-gapped builds, which reads as customer-controlled.

Remove Factory Private from every qualifying clause until first-party docs establish in-boundary inference. Reword deployment to 'EU-region (Factory-operated EEA cloud)'. Merge the verifier's wikiCloudSync control, the localhost-Ollama-can-serve-cloud-models risk and the connected-mode metrics risk.

issues.problem: HIGH. The proposal adds GitLab Dedicated for Government as a deployment and in special-route control 3. The verifier found GitLab's own page lists the Agent Platform as unavailable there, and Dedicated is GitLab-hosted single tenancy (vendor cloud). Control 4 also overstates runner isolation, and editor-extension telemetry to GitLab is missing.

issues.problem: HIGH. These special routes contradict themselves. Bionic: the controls allow LM Link remote devices and Auto Review (undocumented reviewer model; Shell Judge auto-approves network calls), while the note and gate say LM Link must stay unused. Antigravity: the controls allow an 'institution-controlled server' under local-only and blanket egress blocking, docs show localhost only, and LocalAgentConfig (the quickstart class) is a cloud route. Ante: a LAN host 'must also be institution-controlled'. Posit: the special note admits an 'admin-enforced in-boundary endpoint on Workbench', which can include Workbench managed-credential vendor clouds. Zed: the gate says signed out, but the controls allow signed-in Business. OpenHands: licensed Enterprise is listed as qualifying despite documented licence telemetry and required egress to replicated.app and *.r9.all-hands.dev, and ACP agents are allowed in the controls but excluded in the note. Junie: Junie Local is recommended while the record also says it is nightly-only under EAP Terms that prohibit personal data, and the verifier found the nightly-only claim is itself overstated. Zerve: the gateway is documented as a proxy to cloud upstreams, and the air-gapped claim comes from the Enterprise marketing page, which the pricing FAQ contradicts (orchestration credits are charged even when self-hosted).
issues.proposed_resolution: Merge each verifier's corrected special_route and suitability_notes.special before publication. Default wording: Bionic LM Link and Auto Review excluded, Manual review only. Antigravity localhost only, LocalAgentConfig and Science skills excluded. Ante same host only. Posit local Ollama/LM Studio only. Zed signed out, or Business with the Zed Model Provider and hosted Edit Prediction disabled by the admin (pick one). OpenHands MIT self-host only, Enterprise only with its vendor-egress qualifier, no ACP agents. Junie release channel required, conflict recorded. Zerve upstreams must be institution-hosted, with licence/metering egress as a residual risk and the Self-Managed docs as evidence.

issues.problem:
HIGH. Verifiers found default-on egress paths that the proposed special-route controls do not cover:
- Crush: the sourcegraph tool sends model-written queries to sourcegraph.com with no permission prompt, and the agentic_fetch sub-agent runs web tools without hooks.
- Juggler: WebSearch and WebFetch are on and auto-approved, `juggler run` defaults to yolo, and the UI loads a script from cdnjs.
- Qwen Code: web_fetch is registered by default.
- Ante: WebFetch is a default tool.
- OpenCode: webfetch is allowed by default, the hosted free models are on when no key is set, and managed config exists only in V1.
- Tabby/Pochi: the webFetch tool.
- Nanocoder: a project-level config can override the provider and sandbox settings.
- Open Interpreter: session rollouts are written even with persistence=none, and there is a startup update check.
- Kilo: the small model and autocomplete fall back to Kilo Gateway.
- Mistral Vibe: a configured Mistral key triggers a managed-config fetch, and the otel control contradicts telemetry off.
- Goose: the Desktop auto-updater is on by default.
- Copilot CLI: autoUpdate defaults to true, and remote MCP servers are never sandboxed.
- marimo: falls back to openai/gpt-4o when OPENAI_API_KEY is set, and checks for updates daily.
- Aider: onboarding picks a cloud model from an environment key, and voice goes to whisper-1.
- DataFoundry: CopilotKit runtime analytics are on unless disabled, and DataLink defaults to OpenAI.
- Deepnote CLI agent: falls back to OpenAI gpt-5.
- mini-swe-agent: containers have no network restriction.
- Roomote: Memory embeddings go to OpenAI/OpenRouter by default, and tunnels route traffic through Cloudflare.
- ADA: Streamlit checkip.amazonaws.com lookup and fonts.gstatic.com.

HIGH. Verified first-party evidence in the rca-ollama, rca-jetbrains-junie, rca-factory and rca-poolside verdicts shows that a signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so an agent pointed at localhost Ollama may still send data to Ollama's cloud. These 24 special=cfg routes name Ollama as the local runtime, but their special_route, gate and note text contains no Ollama local-only-mode control. Only rca-ollama and rca-poolside name OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD or ':cloud' explicitly.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add one standard control to every cfg route that names Ollama: 'Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.' Add the matching residual risk. Wording comes from the verified rca-ollama record.

issues.problem:
MEDIUM. special_route.inference is used inconsistently.
- 36 of the 39 baseline cfg routes say 'local-only', yet almost all of their required_controls also allow an endpoint on separate institution hardware. Verifiers flagged this for Aider, gptme, mini-swe-agent, Qwen, Antigravity, Ante and DataFoundry.
- The new client tools JASP, Kimi Code CLI, MLJAR, Notebook Intelligence and Poolside use 'customer-controlled-endpoint' for the same pattern, while Twinny, Oh My Pi and Deep Agents use 'local-only'.
- Server platforms that broker model calls are split: Deepnote, Roomote, Zerve, Coder and IBM Bob use 'customer-controlled-endpoint'; GitLab, Tabnine, Datalore, Factory and Zencoder use 'local-only'.
issues.proposed_resolution:
Michaela's call; default rule:
- 'local-only' = a client talks directly to a model served on the same host or on institution-owned hardware inside the network.
- 'customer-controlled-endpoint' = a self-hosted platform or gateway brokers the model calls server-side, so forwarding to external providers is technically possible.
Applying this, switch JASP, Kimi Code CLI, MLJAR, Notebook Intelligence and Poolside to 'local-only'. Optionally switch GitLab, Tabnine, Datalore, Factory and Zencoder to 'customer-controlled-endpoint'. Either way, control 1 should name both options explicitly instead of mixing them under one enum.

issues.problem: MEDIUM. These routes accept an institution-operated OpenAI-compatible endpoint or gateway, but no control requires that endpoint to serve only institution-hosted models and forward nothing to external providers. A LiteLLM-style proxy would pass the check while sending data to a cloud. rca-zerve and rca-ibm-bob already state this condition; MLJAR only partly ('confirm the endpoint executes on controlled hardware').
issues.proposed_resolution: Add to each: 'The endpoint must serve only models hosted on institution-controlled hardware and must not forward requests to external providers; verify with egress monitoring.'

issues.problem:
HIGH. The same situation gets different data_handling labels. Group A (individual or self-serve tiers train by default, the organisational tier does not, and the record's gate is the organisational or paid tier):
- 'no-train': Copilot, Codex, ChatGPT, Kiro, Kiro CLI, Cursor, Warp, Replit, and also Devin and Devin Desktop, whose gate itself requires a training opt-out.
- 'opt-out': Antigravity (gate is Gemini Enterprise, which is no-train), Hex (changed this cycle) and Muse (changed this cycle; the gate is an organisation API key on Standard models, which is no-train).
Group B (vendor model route by default plus a documented local route):
- Kilo, OpenCode, Cline, Mistral Vibe, Crush, Zed and MLJAR are 'local'.
- Grok Build, Kimi and Poolside are 'opt-out'.
- Among cloud-first commercial products with an on-premises special route, Tabnine, Zencoder, Junie and Datalore are 'local', while Copilot, Codex, Posit, Factory, GitLab and IBM Bob (verifier changed local to no-train) carry the cloud label.
Verifiers on Devin, Warp, Windsurf, Replit and Copilot each asked for one rule.
issues.proposed_resolution:
Michaela's call; default rule, written into MAINTENANCE.md:
(a) Vendor-cloud-first products: data_handling = the training/retention default on the least-protective plan that tier_gate admits for personal data, before any user or admin opt-out. A gate that requires a training opt-out gives 'opt-out'. A gate tier that is no-train or ZDR by contract or default gives that label.
(b) BYO-model clients and self-hosted runtimes that need no vendor model service: 'local', with the hosted default and its training terms stated in data_handling_note.
Resulting changes:
- Devin and Devin Desktop: no-train to opt-out.
- Antigravity: opt-out to no-train.
- Muse: opt-out to no-train.
- Grok Build, Kimi Code CLI and Poolside: to 'local'.
- Hex and Jules: unchanged (opt-out).
- Re-check Junie, Tabnine and Zencoder under (a).
- Clusy: consider 'unknown', because provider-side training on its default DeepSeek route is not established.
Alternative rule (label = state once the gate is met): Devin and Devin Desktop stay no-train, Hex becomes no-train. Antigravity and Muse become no-train under either rule.

issues.problem: MEDIUM. The two records share one Kiro Enterprise profile but have different gates. The CLI gate requires model governance that restricts Global-scope and Preview models; its verifier calls this load-bearing, because governance is off by default for Enterprise and exposes the default profile to Global-scope GPT-5.6, including from Frankfurt. The IDE gate omits it and names Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web instead. The verifier also found that the CLI's 'including the Students tier' as individual subscribers is an inference. rca-kiro has no adversarial verdict.
issues.proposed_resolution: Give both records one gate: Enterprise profile under institutional AWS terms, model governance restricting Global-scope and Preview models (block Auto if the approved list must bind), and Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off or assessed separately. Use the same Students wording in both: 'training opt-out applies; classification as individual subscriber not stated'.

integration.consistency_summary:
Schema: all 61 reverify updated_records, all 12 add corrected_records and all 12 discovery add proposals pass Coding_Agents/schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12, format-checked) and the validate_catalog.py cross-field rules: special/route agreement, the open-source licence rule and URL fields. Merging verifier corrections is a hazard: 19 corrections are prose or instructions, not values, plus one '[keep proposed text]' placeholder.

Privacy core:
- Every pure-cloud record is special=no with route none/none (22 baseline, 2 adds).
- All 49 cfg routes are customer-controlled with local-only or customer-controlled-endpoint inference. No record uses 'ready'.
- Six no-to-cfg upgrades (Copilot CLI offline, Antigravity SDK, Codex --oss, Posit local, Roomote self-host, Zerve Self-Managed) were confirmed by verifiers as documented in-boundary inference. Each needs control corrections, and the vendor-cloud boundary must be removed in two places: Factory Private and GitLab Dedicated for Government.
- Verifiers overturned no rating, but refuted many sub-claims.
- Customer-owned cloud accounts (Deepnote, Tabnine, Zerve Self-Managed) are treated consistently as customer-controlled; vendor-hosted VPC or single-tenant offerings (Devin, Windsurf, Replit, Hex, Deepnote-hosted) are consistently no.

Main inconsistencies:
- data_handling scope for mixed-tier and local-capable products (proposed rule plus relabels).
- The local-only versus customer-controlled-endpoint convention.
- Missing cross-cutting controls: Ollama cloud models through localhost (24 routes), no-forwarding endpoints, default web tools and auto-update.
- Sibling gates (Kiro, Cognition).
- Consumer-plan personal routes.
- Confidence calibration.
- Seven records with no adversarial verdict.
- A pre-existing build filter bug that marks 39 records as Free/academic.

Discovery: Snowflake add/hold, Orion hold/drop and Moyai hold/not-added resolved; ZCode and Qoder deduplicated. HN lead window used epoch 1757548800 (2025-09-11, a year wider than intended; leads only). No web fetches were needed.
